11.3 Patterns Adopted and Set Aside

System of context was adopted as the primary pattern, because the requirement is at its root an ontology
with agents that draft, managers who decide, memory instead of training, and a command center. Its
three layers sit in a fixed order: systems of record below, never replaced, never modified, never loaded;

the operator-owned object model in the middle as a projection over those systems, never a shadow copy,
with crossing mappings that answer questions no single system can; and applications and agents above,
governed by one small grammar in which nouns become objects, facts become properties, relationships
become typed links and actions change them. Three patterns were set aside with reasons. Object
tracking and trajectory forecasting were set aside because moves already carry equipment identity from
the terminal operating system and the equipment control systems. Edge orchestration was set aside
because phase one runs on the operator's central hardware and only the offered crane tier would add
gateways. Labelling and retraining were set aside because the improvement path the requirement names
is memory of confirmed outcomes, not weight updates.

11.4 Where the Reasoning Lands

The reasoning lands on four equipment classes, each carried from the shelf into the design: the 141 GB
HBM GPU class that hosts the frontier model on one node of eight GPUs; the frontier model GPU
footprint sizing rule for vLLM and SGLang serving, under which 753 billion parameters at FP8 are 753 GB
of weights on 1,128 GB of memory, leaving 375 GB beside the weights against the 151 GB the 1.2
planning factor reserves; the hardware data diode carrying one-way transfer out of the control zone; and
the fixed thermal camera class held at 9 Hz or less to stay under the export control line that would
otherwise require a license. Every one of these choices, and every figure in this paper, traces to recorded
reading: nothing shown was inferred, and nothing rests on a source the register does not hold.

title: Industrial Data Ontology for a Cold Chain From Plant to Store in the United States
text:
V E R T I C A L - D R I V E N A R C H I T E C T U R E S · S U P P LY C H A I N & L O G I S T I C S · D E S I G N E D W I T H P R A X I S · N O V E M B E R
2026

Industrial Data Ontology for a Cold
Chain From Plant to Store in the United
States
Lot Thread: Industrial AI for Cold Chain Traceability From Plant to Store

Muhammad Umar, Cofounder, CodeNinja

For the quality and regulatory lead accountable for traceability, cold chain and logistics managers, and the data,
integration and platform engineers who would build and run it.

Vertical-Driven Architectures is a CodeNinja series of system designs. Every design in the series is driven by a real-
world problem and scenario in a single industry, and every one is designed on Praxis, CodeNinja's platform for
designing physical AI systems. Operations are described by class, never by name.

ABSTRACT

A Lot's Journey Should Take Hours, Not a Week and
Three Phone Calls
An industrial data ontology for a cold chain from plant to store in the United States has to answer one
question: when a retailer reports a soft case, which pallets shared its dock time and its truck, and when
the federal food traceability rule asks, can the lot's whole journey be produced within twenty four hours.
Today the operator cannot answer either within a day, because its chain has five custodians and five
vocabularies: a pallet is a lot in the plant, a license plate in the warehouse, a shipment line in transport, a
receipt in the retailer's notice and a case in a complaint. A temperature excursion on a dock is logged by
the warehouse while the truck's telematics logs a different one an hour later, and neither is joined to the
lot that sat on the dock. The quality managers hold the mapping between the vocabularies in their heads,
which is why producing a record takes a week and three phone calls and why the rule's compliance date
of July 2028 finds the operation unprepared.

The design reads eight named systems of record, from the plant manufacturing execution system to the
recall and complaint register, through three adapter families: an integration adapter for change data
capture, a telemetry adapter for reefer and dock readings, and an EDI adapter for retailer notices and file
routes. Everything lands in one governed object model of sixteen objects with typed links, from Lot and
Pallet through Dock, Truck, Excursion and Hold to the trace record the rule asks for, held as a projection
over the systems of record rather than a copy of them. Six services, from ontology and identifiers through
the command center to the phase one corridor, expose four surfaces: an excursion and hold approval
queue, a mapping exception queue, a trace queue and an escalation view. The model register is
deliberately empty, because no open weight model survived live verification on this run; the work surface
commits frontier class open weights self hosted for sovereignty, to be sized when a verified entry stands
in the register. All of it runs on the operator's own hardware in the United States, and no product, lot or
partner data leaves that boundary.

The paper covers, in order: the industry problem and the regulatory regimes behind it; the join failure
across the five vocabularies; the constraints and scoping decisions; the stack from systems of record to
surfaces; the object model of sixteen objects and their typed links; ingestion through adapters; where
serving sits and why no edge inference exists; the empty model register and what it will take to fill it; the
two phase rollout with its gates, measurements, failure modes and open questions; who owns what the
design builds; and finally the chapter on how Praxis contextualized and reasoned the design, so any
choice can be traced to the recorded reading behind it.

 Figure 1. The design on one page: the sources the operation already runs, one object model, what it computes, and the
                                                 person who decides.

Contents

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 1

An Industrial Data Ontology for the Cold Chain Starts at
the Dock Door

The loading dock is where most temperature excursions happen, and the federal food
traceability rule will demand a lot's whole journey within twenty four hours from July 2028,
which today takes a week and three phone calls.

The abstract set out an industrial data ontology for a cold chain from plant to store, from dock door to
regulator's request, and claimed the journey can be produced in hours. This chapter grounds that claim:
the question the operator cannot answer today, the rule that sets its deadline, and the operation that must
answer it.

1.1 The Question and the Rule

The operator needs one question answered: when a regulator or a retailer names a lot, what was its
whole journey from plant to store, which critical tracking events of shipping, receiving and transformation
did it pass through, and what did it see on the way. The federal food traceability rule requires lot level
records of each critical tracking event for listed foods, produced within twenty four hours of a request, with
a compliance date of July 2028. Answering it requires data the operation already holds but cannot join:
the lot and its transformation events from the plant, the license plate and dock time from each cold store,
the temperature readings from the reefer unit, the shipment line from transport, the receipt and condition
notes from the retailer, and the holds and complaints that follow. Two regulatory regimes bind: the
traceability rule itself, and the refrigerated storage rule under which an indication of possible temperature
control failure holds food until a qualified individual determines it was not rendered unsafe. Industry
criteria for full chain traceability, ratified by a standards body, add the auditor's view of the same duty
(GS1 2021).

1.2 The Documented Cost of the Problem

A year of recalls has shown the industry how small cold chain breaks become large food safety events,
and the public record shows how a single cold chain site propagates. At a third party cold storage facility
serving major grocery retailers, an outbreak that began with three workers rose to eleven confirmed cases
with many more identified as close contacts, all from one site in the chain (Unitedworkers 2021). The
record keeping itself carries exposure: a staffing firm paid 2.7 million dollars in a settlement after exposing
the private medical information of about 72,000 people during contact tracing, a penalty for losing control
of records whose entire value is that they can be produced on request (Foxnews 2024). Against this, the
operator's present position is that producing a lot's journey takes a week and three phone calls, where the
rule will allow twenty four hours.

1.3 The Operation as a Scenario

The operator is a refrigerated and frozen food manufacturer in the United States, producing frozen and
chilled products at its plants and moving them on pallets through its own and third party cold storage, by
refrigerated truck to retail distribution centers and on to stores. The chain has five custodians and five

vocabularies: a pallet is a lot in the plant, a license plate in the warehouse, a shipment line in transport, a
receipt in the retailer's notice and a case in a complaint. Eight named systems of record hold the data: the
plant manufacturing execution system, the warehouse management systems of the operator's own and
third party cold stores, the carriers' reefer telematics, the transportation management system, the
retailers' receiving notices, the quality hold and release system and the recall and complaint register. The
people in the loop are the quality managers who hold the mapping between the five vocabularies in their
heads, the regulatory lead who answers requests, the analysts who reconcile identifiers by hand, and the
plant, warehouse and transport operators who log the events. The physical environments are freezer
rooms, loading docks where most temperature excursions happen, refrigerated trailers, distribution center
receiving bays and store back rooms. The regulatory ground is the federal traceability rule and the
refrigerated storage hold rule described above, and the compliance date of July 2028 is the clock the
whole design runs against.

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 2

Five Custodians Keep Five Vocabularies for One Pallet

Each system of record sees one slice of the chain, and none of them can say which pallets
shared a dock and a truck with a reported soft case, which is the join failure the design exists
to close.

Chapter 1 stated the question and the clock the rule imposes on it. This chapter walks the eight systems
of record one at a time and shows that each sees one slice of the pallet's life, which is why no one of
them can answer it.

2.1 What Each System Sees

The plant manufacturing execution system sees the lot, its production date and its transformation events,
and misses everything after the pallet leaves the line, because the license plate the warehouse issues
never reaches it. The operator's own cold store warehouse management system sees license plates,
dock schedules and storage locations, and misses the lot inside each pallet and the meaning of a
temperature reading for the food on the dock. The third party cold store's warehouse management
system sees the same things in a partner's vocabulary, and misses the operator's lot numbering entirely,
which is why its records cannot be read without translation. The carriers' reefer telematics sees in transit
temperature readings per reefer unit, and misses which lots were in the trailer and how long they stood on
a dock before loading. The transportation management system sees shipment lines and truck
assignments, and misses the pallet level composition of each shipment and the product's identity. The
retailers' receiving notices see receipts and condition notes such as the soft case, and miss the pallet and
lot behind each receipt and any excursion history. The quality hold and release system sees holds,
releases and their approvers, and misses which other lots share the excursion that triggered a hold. The

recall and complaint register sees complaints and cases, and misses the joined journey that tracing a
case requires. Figure 2 sets these eight views side by side.

     Figure 2. Eight systems, each seeing one part of the answer. The question needs all of them in one place at once.

2.2 What None of Them See Together

No system holds dock time, reefer readings, lot identity and receipt condition at once, so the questions
that matter are exactly the joins: which pallets shared a dock and a truck with a reported soft case, and
which lots were exposed when a dock door stayed open. In practice the cost is measured in the
operator's own words: a week and three phone calls to produce a lot's journey, a retailer told after the
truck arrives rather than before, and quality managers acting as the human join between five
vocabularies, which does not scale and leaves no record of why a join was made.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 3

Sovereignty and the Twenty Four Hour Rule Shape
Everything

Four constraints govern the whole design: data never leaves the operator's control, the
systems of record are never replaced, every decision keeps a named approver, and the first
gate must be able to stop the work cheaply.

Chapter 2 showed the join failure: eight systems, five vocabularies and no shared record of a pallet's life.
This chapter turns that failure into four constraints that shape every layer of the design, then records what
the scoping bought, what it cost and what was set aside.

3.1 Data Never Leaves the Operator's Control

The operator's boundary is absolute: product, lot and partner data stay on its own hardware, models are
open weights it hosts, and no third party model service receives anything. This is hard in this industry
because the chain's data is not the operator's alone; reefer readings belong to carriers, dock records to
third party cold stores and receiving notices to retailers, so each partner feed is gated on written data
terms before it goes live, and contract data terms are recorded on the custodian object rather than in a
filing cabinet. The posture is not only principle, because mishandled records carry penalties, as the
contact tracing settlement showed (Foxnews 2024). It is also the posture an industrial data ontology the
operator owns rests on: the organization that produced the data holds the data and the weights that
reason over it.

3.2 The Systems of Record Stay in Place

Eight systems span five custodians, and several of them are not the operator's to modify at all; a third
party cold store's warehouse system and a retailer's receiving notices will never take an extension from a
manufacturer. The design therefore projects rather than migrates: it reads live feeds, binds the silos in
place and never replaces or loads a system of record, and the sole writes are the named approval paths
into the quality hold and release system and the outgoing trace record itself. This is what makes full chain
traceability reachable at all, because criteria for tracing across a whole chain require crossing boundaries
no single system owns (GS1 2021). The cost is that every join becomes explicit mapping work, and
mapping quality, not software, becomes the program's main risk.

3.3 Every Decision Keeps a Named Approver

Under the refrigerated storage rule, an indication of possible temperature control failure holds food until a
qualified individual determines it was not rendered unsafe, which makes a hold a person's decision by
law. The design encodes this: no agent places or lifts a hold, or sends a record to a regulator, without a
named approval; the excursion agent drafts and a quality manager approves, and the mapping agent
proposes a join that an analyst confirms. This is hard because both clocks, the twenty four hour
production duty and the within the hour excursion join, must run through people, so approval queues, an
escalation view for unacknowledged excursions and a rehearsed degraded mode where people work the
owning systems directly are designed parts of the system, not fallbacks.

3.4 The First Gate Must Stop the Work Cheaply

Phase one runs one product family through one plant, one cold store and one retailer for a quarter, gated
on record production within hours instead of a week, lots joined end to end, excursions joined to exposed

lots within the hour, and a rehearsed dock door event in which the retailer is told before the truck arrives.
This is hard because the July 2028 compliance date pulls toward estate wide rollout; the gate exists so
that measured join quality and the acceptance rate of confirmed mappings, not a calendar, decide
extension to the rest of the estate.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 4

One Stack Runs From Systems of Record to Surfaces

The architecture is three layers in a fixed order: systems of record below, the operator owned
object model as a projection in the middle, and services, agents and surfaces above, all on

Chapter 3 fixed the constraints: read only from the systems the operation already runs, keep every fact on
the operator's own hardware, leave each decision with a named person, and prove the join before any

4.1 Why Three Layers in a Fixed Order

The pattern is three layers, and the order is the design. Below sit the systems of record, eight of them
from the plant manufacturing execution system to the recall and complaint register, each the sole owner
of one custodian's truth, read and never written. In the middle sits one object model the operator owns,
sixteen objects with typed links, built as a projection over the systems of record rather than a copy of
them, so a change in a source changes the projection and nothing drifts. Above sit six services, the
agents that draft work for people, and four surfaces where those people decide. The order matters
because the join is the deliverable: five custodians keep five vocabularies, and no single system of record
can reconcile them, so the reconciliation has to live in a layer that belongs to none of them. Figure 3
shows the layers with their counts, from eight sources and three adapter families at the bottom to four
surfaces at the top. The same order places this design among sovereign reference architectures:
everything above the sources runs on hardware the operator owns, and no fact crosses the boundary to a
third party model service.

Sixteen Objects Turn Cold Chain Data Into One Journey

One small grammar turns the five vocabularies into a single argument: nouns become
objects, facts become properties, relationships become typed links, and a query can then
walk from a complaint to the dock doors and trucks a lot shared.

Chapter 4 fixed the stack's order and named its seven stages. This chapter opens the middle layer, where
the five vocabularies of the chain become one argument a query can walk.

5.1 Sixteen Objects and the Links Between Them

The object model holds sixteen objects, each with a kind and an anchor. The materials are Product, Lot
and Case; the assets are Pallet and Truck; the events are the Critical Tracking Event and the Excursion;
the sites are Location and Dock; Custodian is the actor; Reefer Reading is the measure; Hold, Release,
Complaint and the Traceability Record are records; and Receipt is a document. Each object is anchored
in the system of record that owns it: the Lot in the plant manufacturing execution system, the Pallet in a
warehouse management system, the Receipt in the retailers' receiving notices, while the Traceability
Record, which carries a lot's full journey events, its production time in hours and the requester, is the one
object the model itself produces. Figure 4 shows every object and the typed links between them. What
the links buy is reach: given a Case, a query walks the lot reference to the Lot, through the critical
tracking events to the Pallets, along their dock time to the Docks and their custodians to the Trucks, and
from the Excursions to the Holds that answered them. A document store can return every document that
mentions a case, but it cannot walk a join, because the relationship is not stored as a thing in its own
right; a standards body ratifies assessment criteria for full chain traceability across supply chains, and
those criteria interrogate the links, not the documents (GS1 2021). Table 8, printed from the plan, lists
each object, the system it is anchored in and its typed links.

5.2 Where the Human Loop Lives

The loop is the point of the layer above the model. The mapping agent drafts a join and an analyst
confirms it; the excursion agent drafts a hold and a quality manager approves it in the quality hold and
release system; the trace agent drafts a record and the regulatory lead sends it. No agent places or lifts a
hold, and no agent sends a record, without a named approval, and every confirmed join is remembered
so the second join is cheaper than the first, with the disagreement record held as the evidence. The
hosting posture follows the constraint: the model runs on the operator's own hardware in the United
States, and product, lot and partner data never leave that hardware. Identity runs on Keycloak, so every
approval attaches to a named person. External links are inbound only, and there is no egress path to any

third party model service. The single write path into any system of record is a person acting in the owning
system; the platform reads the resulting state back.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 6

Every Source Enters Through an Adapter, Never Directly

Eight named systems of record reach the object model only through three adapter families,
each carrying a provenance class, so the ontology never writes into a system of record and
every fact keeps its source key.

Chapter 5 described what the object model holds and where the human loop lives. This chapter describes
how data reaches it: eight named sources, three adapter families, and a backbone that keeps every event
ordered, proven and recoverable.

6.1 Eight Sources and Their Adapter Paths

Every source in this design is a named system of record, read only, and each reaches the object model
through one of three adapter families. The plant manufacturing execution system owns the lot and its
transformation events; the own cold store warehouse management system owns license plates, dock
schedules and storage locations; the third party cold store warehouse management system owns license
plates and dock time in a partner's vocabulary; the carriers' reefer telematics owns the in transit
temperature readings; the transportation management system owns shipment lines and truck
assignments; the retailers' receiving notices own receipts and condition notes such as the soft case; the
quality hold and release system owns holds and releases; and the recall and complaint register owns
complaints and cases. Each carries the same provenance class, an operator or partner system of record
whose data arrives as a feed, and the same direction, inbound. Figure 5 maps every named system to its
class and its adapter path, and the table below sets what each system sees beside what it misses.

       Figure 5. The 8 named systems, the adapter path each one takes, and the object model they all map into.

6.2 What the Adapter Tier Guarantees

The adapter tier makes four guarantees. It normalises: every record, whatever its source vocabulary,
enters the object model in the same grammar of objects, properties and typed links, with the integration
adapter running Debezium change data capture on the transactional systems, the telemetry adapter
carrying reefer and dock readings, and the EDI adapter running Apache Camel routes for the retailers'
notices and partner files. It proves: every fact is stamped with its source system and its source key, so a
trace record can cite the key a regulator or retailer can check in the owning system. It protects: no
adapter exposes a write path into a system of record, so the ontology can never corrupt a custodian's
truth. It gates: an approvals register confirms each partner's contract data terms in writing before its feed
goes live, because cold storage and carrier contracts may not permit lot level sharing by default, and the
register holds ingest until the confirmation exists. The boundary has a real price when it fails, and not only
in this industry: a staffing firm paid 2.7 million dollars in a US Justice Department settlement after about
72,000 people's private medical information was exposed during COVID-19 contact tracing work
(Foxnews 2024).

6.3 The Event Backbone

Apache Kafka 4.3 in KRaft mode, with three dedicated controllers, carries every adapter's output into the
platform. Ordering is per key: each event is keyed by its source key, so a lot's events arrive in order even
when different sources lag differently. Delivery is at least once, paired with idempotent writes into the
ontology so a replayed event cannot create a second pallet or a second excursion. Buffering absorbs the
dock log's cadence: the broker holds events while a consumer lags, so a dock log that arrives in a batch

still joins to the lot that was on the dock, and phase one measures that batch interval against the within
the hour excursion budget. Replication keeps ingest alive: partitions replicate across brokers, so a single
broker loss halts no feed. Beneath it, Chrony synchronises plant, warehouse and carrier clocks, because
a join that depends on dock time is a join that depends on clocks agreeing.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 7

All Serving Sits on the Operator's Own Metal

No compute is placed in freezers, docks or trucks: readings arrive as partner data, and all
serving, from the event backbone to the work surface, runs in the operator's existing server
room inside the United States.

Chapter 6 described how eight systems of record enter through three adapter families, integration,
telemetry and EDI, and what the adapter tier guarantees each record on the way in. This chapter
describes where the compute those feeds touch actually runs, and the answer is deliberately short: on the
operator's own metal, in its existing server room, inside the United States.

7.1 One Tier, and It Is Central

There is a single inference tier in this design, and it is central. The event backbone (Apache Kafka 4.3,
running KRaft with three dedicated controllers), the ontology store, the telemetry store that holds reefer
and dock readings beside it, and the serving hardware for the work surface all run on the operator's
central and site hardware. No compute is placed in freezers, on docks or in trucks, because the constraint
the operator set is to read its own systems and the partners' feeds: reefer and dock readings arrive as
partner data, not as signals from sensing this design supplies. Figure 6 shows the one tier, what runs on
it, and the one crossing that exists, the inbound partner feeds.

The memory arithmetic the plan holds is the sizing rule for the frontier work surface. The operator names
GLM 5.3, and the rule puts its 756 GB of FP8 weights on one 141 GB class node, eight GPUs per node
drawing about 10 kW, with about 280 GB of KV cache headroom left for the context the command
center's conversations and citations consume; the alternatives weighed were BF16 across two nodes and
a mid size model in place of the frontier work surface. The arithmetic is the rule, not a commitment: no
model row survived live verification on this run, so the footprint names where it runs and the node count is
derived only when a verified entry stands in the register. The document reading and embedding entries
the design cites fit one to four cards of the 141 GB class on an air cooled PCIe server in the same room.

        Figure 6. Where each tier runs, what runs there, and the narrow set of outputs that cross the boundary.

7.2 Three Clocks Set the Budget

The latency budget is three nested clocks. The outer clock is the rule's ceiling: a lot's full journey must be
produced within twenty four hours of a request, and the July 2028 compliance date fixes when that duty
bites. The middle clock is the design's own nominal, four hours to produce a lot's full record, with any
measurement above it a breach; the fault the rollout rehearses against is a dock door left open at the cold
store. The inner clock is the excursion join, within the hour from reading to the lots it exposed, because
that is what lets the retailer be told before the truck arrives rather than after a case is opened. The dock
log's own batch interval is not assumed: phase one measures it and negotiates a faster cadence where
the interval exceeds the hour. Joins that meet these clocks must still meet a standards body's ratified
criteria for full chain traceability, a higher bar than looking joined on a screen (GS1 2021).

7.3 The Boundary and Its Failures

What crosses the network boundary is inbound only: eight read feeds over existing connections, and
nothing else. Product, lot and partner data never leave the operator's hardware and no third party model
service is called, so no egress path is built; a one way transfer diode would be precision no data flow in
this design consumes. When the link fails, the event backbone buffers and replays partner feeds in order,
and the mapping exception queue surfaces unjoined identifiers rather than letting a silent gap become an
incomplete trace. When power fails, rack power and UPS, managed with Network UPS Tools, carries the
room; a single node failure still halts the command center and all agent drafting, which is why the design
carries a rehearsed rollback and a documented degraded mode in which people work the owning
systems directly, kept warm. When the update path fails, artifacts and weights move only through the
Harbor registry, so a bad update rolls back to the artifact that preceded it; and Chrony keeps NTP time
across the systems, because the joins consume business record ordering, not precision timestamps.

                                                                         model of a lot's journey from plant to store

     The ground it runs          Frontier GPUs: the work surface         sized by the committed footprint
     on                          footprint is unsized on this plan, so
                                 no GPU count is stated; GPUs are
                                 excluded from this price.

PA R T I I I · C H A P T E R 9

Shadow Mode Comes Before Any Join Is Trusted

Two phases carry sixteen items: the foundation builds the ontology, the identifiers and the
ingest normalisation, and the phase one corridor runs one product family end to end, gated

on hours instead of a week and on a rehearsed dock door event.

Chapter 8 closed the model and equipment register with the license terms and the single node the work
surface runs on. This chapter turns that register into a sequence: two phases, sixteen items, and gates
that measure hours rather than promises, so the first gate can stop the work cheaply if the joins do not
hold.

9.1 Two Phases Carry Sixteen Items and Two Gates

The Foundation phase carries seven items across three workstreams: ontology and identifiers, sovereign
serving, and traceability and compliance. Its items include the governed cold chain ontology model, the
explicit identifier mapping across the five custodians, and the ingest normalisation that reads the systems
of record through the adapter tier. Nothing here touches an agent or a surface; the phase exists to prove
that one governed model can hold a lot's journey as a projection over systems that are never modified,
never migrated and never loaded.

The Phase One Corridor carries nine items across four workstreams: agents and memory, command
center, the phase one corridor itself, and traceability and compliance. Its items include the mapping agent
with analyst confirmation, the excursion agent with quality manager approval, and the trace agent for
regulator and retailer requests. The corridor runs one product family through one plant, one cold store and
one retailer, and extension to other plants, retailers and families is decided at the gate, never before it.
The corridor's exit gate is the design's proof point: record production inside hours instead of a week, lots
joined end to end, excursions joined to exposed lots within the hour, and a rehearsed dock door event in
which the retailer is told before the truck arrives. Requirement coverage stands at one requirement
stated, one covered, with no partial coverage and no gap; Figure 8 sets the phases, their item counts,
their gates and that coverage on one page.

             Figure 8. The two phases and their gates, and coverage of the one requirement across them.

9.2 What the Rollout Measures

The headline measure is hours to produce a lot's full record, with a nominal of 4.0 hours and a breach
whenever production runs above it; the fault the corridor rehearses against is a dock door left open at the
cold store, because the loading dock is where most temperature excursions happen. The baseline the
measure replaces is a week and three phone calls. Two further measures sit beside it: the time from an
excursion reading to the exposed lots being named, which must land within the hour, and the mapping
agent's acceptance rate in shadow mode, which is measured before any credit is taken for a join. The
record the trace agent drafts is rehearsed against published assessment criteria for full chain traceability,
so the corridor proves itself against a ratified external standard rather than an internal one (GS1 2021).

9.3 Failure Modes and What the Design Does

Table 5 lists the failure modes the design carries answers for, drawn from the risk register the reasoning
produced.

   level sharing                              live; the approvals register gates ingest

   and the unjoinable rate stays high         acceptance rate before any credit is taken

9.4 Lessons the Reasoning Carries Forward

Write the excursion disposition rule before the feed goes live. The vaccine cold chain precedents
Praxis read taught that a temperature feed without a disposition rule produces alarms, not decisions, and
that the rule must cover excursions in both directions, warm and cold, because a dock door and a failing
reefer fail differently. The excursion agent's drafted hold therefore exists before the first reefer reading is
joined.

Gate join quality separately from record production. A visibility layer fixes only what it measures,
which is the lesson of the second precedent: producing a record quickly and joining identities correctly are
two different capabilities, and the corridor measures both so that neither can hide behind the other.

Shadow the mapping agent before anyone credits a join. The quality managers who hold the five
vocabularies in their heads are the benchmark, and the disagreement record between their confirmed
joins and the agent's drafts is the evidence that a second join is cheaper than the first.

9.5 What Is Still Open

Four questions remain open. The dock log's actual batch interval is unknown until the corridor measures
it, and settling it either confirms the within the hour budget or sends the negotiation for a faster cadence.
The telemetry store engine, InfluxDB 3 Core against TimescaleDB, is chosen with the operator's database
lead at design, and settling it fixes the reefer and dock reading path. No open weight model was verified
live on this run, so the register holds catalog entries each verified by a person on the date it carries, and
that live check is outstanding before any weights are committed; the work surface's GPU count is derived
only when that row stands. Finally, each partner's written data term gates its own feed, and settling those
terms decides how much of the five custodian join the corridor can actually rehearse.

PA R T I I I · C H A P T E R 1 0

The Mapping Knowledge Should Stay with the Operator

The object model, the confirmed join memory and the decision record belong to the operator
that produced them, held on its own hardware under open weight licenses it can stand
behind, with every approval named.

Chapter 9 set the gates the corridor must pass and the measures it must beat. This chapter settles the
quieter question those gates protect: who owns what the corridor produces, and on what ground it sits.

10.1 What the Operator Owns

The object model, all sixteen objects and their typed links, belongs to the operator from the first item of
the Foundation phase. It is a projection over systems of record the operator already owns, so the middle
layer adds governed joins without transferring any system of record to anyone else, and the vocabulary
mapping it encodes is the asset that took a week and three phone calls to reconstruct by hand.

The weights question is a license question, because nothing is trained or fine tuned into them. The design
runs GLM 5.3 at FP8 on one 141 GB class node in the operator's own server room, under an open weight
license whose attribution notice and managed service trigger are reviewed by counsel before the weights
are hosted; internal use does not touch the trigger, so the operator holds its weights without a service
relationship it cannot exit.

The decision record is the third asset. Every hold, release, confirmed join and sent trace record carries a
named approver, and the memory of confirmed mapping joins is what makes the second join cheaper
than the first. Keeping the record the next decision reads is a standing duty of food businesses, not an
optional courtesy (GOV n.d.), which is why the record is owned and held rather than borrowed. The
boundary completes the ownership picture: product, lot and partner data never leave the operator's
hardware, no third party model service is called, and every feed is inbound and read only.

10.2 The Offer Behind the Design

The design maps to CodeNinja's offer in a direct way. Hyper Ontology holds the governed object model of
the cold chain; Hyper Pragma is the work surface on which the operator's quality team works the
excursion, mapping and trace queues and builds its own agents; Hyper Engram keeps the record of
decisions and outcomes that each run reads before it acts, without updating any weights; Decision
Systems is the ranking, attribution and reconciliation the mapping and excursion agents draft and named
people decide; and Sovereign Infrastructure is the ground it all runs on, the operator's own hardware,
open weight licenses and in country operation. Praxis is the platform on which the design was produced,
and this paper is the trace of that reasoning.

PA R T I V · C O N C L U S I O N

The Join Is the Deliverable, and the Operator Keeps It
The design is one governed projection over eight systems of record that never replaces them: sixteen
objects and their typed links turn five custodians' vocabularies into a single lot journey, agents draft the
mapping, the excursion disposition and the trace record while named people approve them, and the
whole argument runs on the operator's own hardware inside the United States with no external model
service. The first gate is cheap and decisive: one product family through one plant, one cold store and
one retailer, judged on whether a lot's record appears in hours instead of a week, whether lots join end to
end, whether excursions join to exposed lots within the hour, and whether a rehearsed dock door event
tells the retailer before the truck arrives.

Running the same shape elsewhere takes three things that transfer and one that does not. What transfers
is the grammar: nouns become objects, facts become properties, relationships become typed links, and
the ontology stays a projection over systems of record that are bound in place, never migrated. What
transfers is the discipline: entity resolution is first class work and the program's schedule risk, not a
byproduct, so the mapping agent runs in shadow mode with a measured acceptance rate before any
credit is taken. What transfers is the control: no agent places or lifts a hold or sends a record to a
regulator without a named approval, and every record carries citations to source keys. What does not
transfer is the vocabulary itself: each new chain brings its own custodians, its own identifiers and its own
contract data terms, and confirming those terms in writing before each feed goes live is where the next
build begins.

PA R T I V · C H A P T E R 11

Recorded Reading Stands Behind Every Choice

Every design in this series is produced on Praxis, and this chapter lets a reader trace any
choice back to the recorded reading that justified it, from the regulatory rule to the case
studies and the sizing entries it read.

Chapter 10 closed the argument with ownership. This chapter opens the record of how the design was
reasoned, so a reader can trace any choice back to what justified it (Figure 9). Every design in this series
is produced on Praxis, and this chapter is where the record meets the page: what was asked, what was
read, which lenses read it, and which patterns the reasoning adopted. Nothing here is a method
disclosure; it is the bibliography of each decision.

11.1 Contextualizing the Ask

The ask, written in the operator's voice, was an industrial data ontology for a cold chain from plant to
store, driven by the federal food traceability rule and its July 2028 compliance date, with lot level critical
tracking events producible within twenty four hours of a request. Praxis assigned the design to the
Enterprise AI family and the Supply Chain and Logistics industry. Praxis read the corpus shelf of each
lens; nothing was ranked or filtered by keyword. The domain brief gave the fragmentation problem in the
operator's own terms: five custodians, five vocabularies, and quality managers holding the mapping in
their heads.

 Figure 9. From the ask to the design: the family and industry Praxis assigned, the eight lenses and what each cited, the

11.2 The Eight Lenses

contributed to the design. No lens returned nothing; all eight contributed.

11.3 Patterns Adopted and Set Aside

One pattern was adopted, as primary: System of context, pinned by the design lead and justified by the
brief itself, since the requirement crosses five custodians' silos no single system reconciles. Its shape is
fixed: systems of record below, never replaced, never modified and never loaded; the operator owned
model in the middle as a projection, never a shadow copy; applications and agents above, acting through
the sense, decide, act, learn loop whose return edge keeps the model living. The small grammar carries
the whole build: nouns become objects, facts become properties, relationships become typed links, and
actions change them. No pattern was set aside, which is itself a finding: the brief's control tower warning
was satisfied inside the adopted pattern by refusing write back to any system of record.

11.4 Where the Reasoning Lands

The equipment classes close the trace. The Frontier Model GPU Footprint Sizing Rule, for vLLM and
SGLang serving, puts GLM 5.3's 756 GB of FP8 weights on one 141 GB HBM node with about 280 GB of
KV headroom, which fixes the work surface's ground as the operator's existing server room rather than a
new data center. The Cold Chain Sensing Classes force every temperature feed to name its
measurement point, ambient, return air, supply air or product simulating, so a dock reading and a reefer
reading are compared as measurements rather than assumed to agree. Every figure in this chapter, the
lens citations, the sizing arithmetic and the precedent notes, was recorded reading; nothing is inferred,
and the records read stand behind each choice on request.

title: A Self-Improving AI System for Cement Kiln Control in Saudi Arabia
text:
V E R T I C A L - D R I V E N A R C H I T E C T U R E S · H E AV Y I N D U S T R Y & C O N S T R U C T I O N · D E S I G N E D W I T H P R A X I S ·
NOVEMBER 2026

A Self-Improving AI System for Cement
Kiln Control in Saudi Arabia
Heavy Industry & Construction Watch: One Living Picture of the Operation

Muhammad Umar, Cofounder, CodeNinja

For the leaders accountable for heavy industry & construction operations, their supervisors, and the data and platform
engineers who would build and run it.

Vertical-Driven Architectures is a CodeNinja series of system designs. Every design in the series is driven by a real-
world problem and scenario in a single industry, and every one is designed on Praxis, CodeNinja's platform for
designing physical AI systems. Operations are described by class, never by name.

ABSTRACT

The Answer Already Exists in the Systems the Operation
Runs
A self-improving AI system for kiln control at a cement company in Saudi Arabia: open weight models on
the company's own hardware in the country, reading its systems of record and getting better at advising
the kiln every shift from what operators confirm worked, on one governed ontology of the kiln line, its
equipment, tags, setpoints, recipes, raw meal lots, fuel lots, clinker samples, upsets, operator actions,
shell scans, work orders and shifts, each fact tied to its source system.

The design reads 10 source systems through 3 adapter families into one object model of 16 objects, runs
7 services over it and opens 3 surfaces to the people who decide, with 3 models placed where the data
is. A sovereign, read-only advisory system for one kiln line: a governed ontology over the plant's seven
systems of record, three named agents that draft causes, setpoints and handovers for people to confirm,
and memory that compounds confirmed outcomes without ever changing weights. Phase one runs one
line for one quarter against a measured baseline, gated on an on/off comparison in the units the national
energy efficiency program itself collects.

The paper covers the operation and the problem its systems cannot answer, the constraints, the stack,
the object model, ingestion, inference placement, the models and their licenses, the rollout and its proof,
ownership, and finally how Praxis contextualized and reasoned the design.

 Figure 1. Heavy Industry & Construction Watch on one page: the sources the operation already runs, one object model,
                                    what it computes, and the person who decides.

Contents
Each chapter is tagged for the reader it serves most directly: Executive, Team Lead, FDE, Reference.

        Abstract · The Answer Already Exists in the Systems the Operation Runs               Executive

 PA R T I · T H E P R O B L E M

 1      A Daily Question Goes Unanswered in the Systems That Hold the Data                   Executive

 2      Every System Sees One Slice of the Operation                                         Executive   Team Lead

 PA R T I I · T H E D E S I G N

 3      Four Constraints Shape Everything Downstream                                         Team Lead

 4      One Stack Runs From the Systems of Record to the Surfaces                            Team Lead     FDE

 5      Sixteen Objects Turn Operational Data Into One Argument                              FDE

 6       Every Source Enters Through an Adapter, Never Directly                         FDE

 7       Inference Belongs Where the Data Is                                            FDE

 8       The License Decides What the Operator Can Own                                  FDE      Executive

  PA R T I I I · T H E R O L L O U T

 9       Shadow Mode Comes Before Any Flag Is Trusted                                   Team Lead      Executive

 10      The Intelligence Should Stay with the Operation That Produced It               Executive

  PA R T I V · H O W I T WA S D E S I G N E D

         Conclusion · The Pattern Repeats Wherever Systems of Record Do Not Meet        Executive

 11      How Praxis Contextualized and Reasoned This Design                             Team Lead      FDE

         Sources                                                                        Reference

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 1

A Daily Question Goes Unanswered in the Systems That
Hold the Data

The operation holds every fact the question needs and no system answers it.

The abstract promised a self-improving AI system for kiln lines, sketched in one paragraph: a sovereign,
read-only advisory system for one line, agents that draft for people to confirm, and memory that
compounds without touching weights. A self-improving AI system earns its keep only if the question it
serves is stated exactly and the ground it stands on is real, and that is this chapter's work.

1.1 The Question and the Regimes It Must Satisfy

The operation needs one question answered every shift: given the fuel lot now burning, the raw meal now
feeding and the hundreds of variables now streaming from the line, which setpoint moves hold thermal
energy per tonne of clinker low while clinker chemistry stays in specification, and when the line upsets,
which moves bring it back soonest. The question carries a second half that matters as much, the why,
with evidence a named person can check before acting. Answering it requires all seven systems of record
at once: streaming tag values and historian context from the distributed control system, raw meal and
clinker quality from the laboratory, calorific value and feed rate from the fuel records, shell temperature
profiles from the scanner, equipment state from maintenance, actions and handovers from the shift log,
and tonnes and energy from production reporting. Three regimes frame the answer. The national energy
efficiency program collects and verifies thermal energy per tonne, so the figure the system is judged on is
already measured by a third party. Operational technology cybersecurity controls set the control burden

by facility criticality level, which fixes how anything may connect to the control network. Air quality
regulation sets stationary source emission limits, so emission lineage must be traceable even though the
permit reporting duty stays with the plant.

1.2 What Unrecorded Practice Costs

Heavy industry and construction pays for unrecorded practice in two currencies. The first is human: more
than 1,000 construction workers have died on the job annually since 2016 (CPWR n.d.), a toll that
disciplines every change made near operating equipment and every claim of automation. The second is
energy and clinker. Fuel is the main cost at a plant of this class, thermal energy per tonne is the figure the
company is measured on, and every shift runs the kiln differently: one operator holds the burning zone hot
and burns fuel, another runs it cool and makes poor clinker, and when a quality excursion or a shell hot
spot is found, the cause is rebuilt by hand across the historian, the lab and the fuel log. Regulators have
begun to expect a change of this kind to be treated as a process change, with revised guidelines relating
AI reliability assessment in plant safety to traditional methods such as HAZOP and FMEA (GO n.d.), and
this design adopts that standard for its approvals path. The ask for a self-improving system is timely
rather than fashionable, since recursive self-improvement has moved from frontier laboratories into the
broader corporate ecosystem (Stanford 2026), and the design must deliver it in a form a plant can audit.

1.3 The Operation as a Scenario

The operator is a cement company in Saudi Arabia running several integrated plants. Each plant runs a
preheater, a kiln line of several thousand tonnes of clinker a day and a cooler, watched from a control
room where an operator tracks hundreds of variables shift by shift; a model predictive controller runs on
some lines, and operators switch it off when a ring forms or the fuel changes. Three roles sit in the loop
by name: the control room operator who moves setpoints, the shift supervisor who confirms drafts, and
the production manager who owns the line's energy and quality figures. The plant's most experienced
operator retires this year, and the knowledge of how he brought the kiln back from an upset is in nobody's
notes. The physical environment is desert heat, with a record ambient of 52 C and dust that argues for
sealed, fanless compute. The regulatory ground is the energy efficiency program's collected figure, the
operational technology controls by facility criticality level, and the air quality limits with the industry's
annex override. The counts behind the scenario: seven named systems of record, three named roles,
several plants, and one line in phase one.

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 2

Every System Sees One Slice of the Operation

Each system of record sees its own part of the answer and none sees the whole.

Chapter 1 stated the question and the scenario that holds it. This chapter shows why no existing system
can answer that question: each system of record sees one slice of the kiln, and the slices never meet in
one place.

2.1 One Slice at a Time

The distributed control system and its historian see every tag value, the recipe and the controller state,
but not why the tags moved, because fuel chemistry, laboratory findings and operator reasons live
elsewhere. The laboratory system sees raw meal and clinker chemistry against specification, but not the
process conditions that produced each result. The fuel and alternative fuel feed records see lot identity,
calorific value, moisture, ash and feed rate, but not what each fuel change did downstream in the kiln. The
shell scanner sees the shell temperature profile and the position of a hot spot, the earliest physical sign of
burning zone trouble, but not the cause or the moves that cleared it. The maintenance management
system sees equipment state, work orders and refractory history, but not the process upsets that
preceded each failure. The shift log sees operator actions, reason codes and handovers, the human half
of every upset story, but not the hundreds of tag values behind each action. The production reporting
system sees clinker tonnes and energy against plan, but not the decisions and conditions behind each
figure. Figure 2 sets these seven slices side by side, and the pattern is the same in each row: the slice is
faithful, complete in its own terms, and silent about everything the question joins it to.

   Figure 2. Seven systems, each seeing one part of the answer. The question needs all of them in one place at once.

2.2 What No System Sees Together

What none of them see together is an upset and its cure as one story: the trigger tags, the fuel lot burning
at the time, the raw meal feeding, the operator's moves in order, the lab findings that followed, the shell
scan that confirmed recovery, and the time and fuel it cost. That join failure is paid every time a quality
excursion or hot spot is found and the cause is rebuilt by hand across three systems, and it is paid once
more when the retiring operator leaves, because the recovery moves that worked live in his judgment and
in no record any successor can read. The model predictive controller compounds the loss rather than
repairing it, since operators switch it off precisely when the kiln misbehaves, so the hardest episodes, the
ones worth learning from, are the ones no system captures. The data for the daily question is all present;
the argument that joins it is not.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 3

Four Constraints Shape Everything Downstream

The goals, the scoping decisions and the exclusions were fixed before any component was
chosen.

Chapter 2 showed that the failure is a join failure, not a data failure, so the fix is an argument built across
systems rather than another copy of them. Before any component was chosen, four goals were fixed, and
every choice downstream had to satisfy all four at once; this chapter states them and the scoping they
forced.

3.1 Sovereignty Is a Sizing Problem

The first goal is ownership: open weight models on the company's own hardware, in the country, with
nothing about the plants leaving it. In this industry that is hard because the frontier model in the design
needs a node of eight accelerators of the 141 GB class, and the export license position for that class into
the country is not yet confirmed, with two nodes of the 80 GB class as the fallback shape. Sovereignty
also collides with the operational technology controls, which set the connection burden by facility criticality
level, so the boundary design has to be settled with the security function before design freeze rather than
after.

3.2 The Human Loop Is the Control Design

The second goal is that people decide: the system reads the systems of record and never writes to the
control system, and operators and supervisors make every setpoint change. This is hard because the
plant's own history shows what happens to advisory layers operators do not trust, as the model predictive
controller is switched off whenever the kiln misbehaves. The design answers with draft quality gates,
explicit operator authority recorded against each draft, and a one-way boundary between the analytics
zone and the control network. Guidance on safety management for autonomous equipment on industrial

sites points the same way (ISSA 2026), and the approvals path treats the advisory system as a process
change under hazard-study methods (GO n.d.).

3.3 Improvement Without Touching the Weights

The third goal is a self-improving AI system in a form a plant can audit. Frontier laboratories delegate a
growing share of AI development to AI systems themselves (Anthropic n.d.), but a kiln cannot risk weights
that drift shift by shift, and the requirement forbids training on the fly. The design therefore improves
through memory alone: every confirmed outcome, the upset, the moves and the measured recovery, is
kept and read before the next draft, while the model weights never change. What compounds is the
record, not the parameters.

3.4 Proof Before Trust

The fourth goal is measured improvement, gated. The precedent that sets the honesty bar is the kiln
control build whose continuous-month saving of 4.1 percent became 2.2 percent under a controlled on/off
comparison, so phase one runs one line for one quarter against a measured baseline and gates on the
on/off comparison alone, in the units the national energy efficiency program itself collects.

3.5 Scoping Decisions

Three scoping decisions follow from the four goals, and Table 1 records what each buys and what it costs.

  Table 1 · Scoping Decisions

   DECISION                        W H AT I T B U Y S                   W H AT I T C O S T S

   Run one kiln line for one       A clean baseline and an honest       Findings from one line reach the other
   quarter first                   on/off gate in collected units       plants slowly

   Bind the seven systems read-    Safety sign-off and no risk to the   No closed-loop savings; every benefit
   only                            control path                         must pass through a person

   Improve through confirmed       An auditable record of what worked   Improvement is bounded by what
   memory, not weights             and who confirmed it                 operators actually confirm

3.6 What the Design Chose Against

Table 2 records the alternatives the design rejected and why, and it closes with the scope boundary. The
ontology decision deserves a word, because the projection discipline is what separates this design from
the document stores that pass for industrial ontology examples in most plants: the ontology is a governed
projection over the seven systems of record, never a shadow copy, so a query can walk from an upset to
the fuel lot, the operator actions and the lab findings without any of them being duplicated.

   Table 2 · What the Design Chose Against

    WHERE                      W H AT WA S P I C K E D            I N S T E A D O F, A N D W H Y

    Control                    Advisory agents riding above the   Replacing or re-tuning it; the precedent rode above
    architecture               incumbent model predictive         the incumbent optimizer so one control path survived
                               controller                         and operators kept authority

One Stack Runs From the Systems of Record to the
Surfaces

Systems of record below, one object model in the middle, services and surfaces above.

A self-improving AI system for kiln lines usually fails at the join between the control system and everything
else the plant knows, not at the model, and Chapter 3 fixed the four constraints any answer must survive:
read-only systems of record, weights that never change, named people who decide, and nothing leaving
the country. This chapter lays out the stack that satisfies all four at once, running from the sources to the
surfaces the control room actually sees.

4.1 The Pattern and Why It Fits

The architecture is three layers in a fixed order: the systems of record below, never replaced, never
modified, never bulk loaded; one object model in the middle, owned by the company and held as a
projection over those systems rather than a copy of them; and the applications and agents above, which
draft causes, setpoints and handovers for people to confirm. The order matters because the distributed
control system stays authoritative for control and its historian stays authoritative for history, so the object
model only has to join what each already holds, and every capability traces to a clause the company

asked for. Because the advisory layer changes how the control room works, the stack is treated as a
process change and assessed with the plant's own hazard-study methods, the way revised plant-safety
guidance expects AI reliability to be weighed against methods such as HAZOP (GO n.d.). Figure 3 shows
the layers with their counts: seven systems of record feeding three adapter families, one object model of
sixteen objects, seven services and three surfaces, with three models doing the inference.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 6

Every Source Enters Through an Adapter, Never Directly

Nothing reaches the object model except through an adapter that owns its contract.

Chapter 5 showed what the object model holds once data is inside it; this chapter shows how data gets
there, and why nothing can arrive by any route the design does not own. The rule is absolute: every
source enters through an adapter, never directly, because an unowned path into the model is a path
nobody can validate, time-stamp or replay.

6.1 Every Named Source and Its Provenance

Seven named systems feed the model, all of one provenance class: systems the company already owns
and runs, read in one direction only. The distributed control system and historian supply the streaming
triggers and the historian context; the laboratory system closes the loop between advice and clinker
quality; the fuel and alternative fuel feed records carry the calorific value behind every drift and trigger the
setpoint agent when a lot changes; the shell scanner gives the earliest physical sign of burning zone
trouble; the maintenance management system joins upsets to equipment state and refractory history; the
shift log holds the operator actions and handovers that are the human half of every upset story; and the
production reporting system holds the clinker tonnes and energy figures that form both the baseline and
the gate. Figure 5 maps each source to its adapter path and its provenance class.

      Figure 5. The 10 named systems, the adapter path each one takes, and the object model they all map into.

6.2 What the Adapter Tier Guarantees

Three adapter families cover the seven sources: the integration adapter for the operational systems, the
telemetry adapter for the streaming tag flow, and the ops systems adapter for logs, work orders and
reports. The tier guarantees five things. Each adapter owns its source contract, so a schema change at
the source surfaces as a contract failure rather than silent corruption; each validates every record against
that contract before it passes; each stamps provenance and receipt time and aligns both to the plant time
source through Chrony, because a join between the historian and the laboratory system is only as good
as their shared clock; each buffers when a source is slow or briefly absent and backfills on return; and
every adapter is read only, with no path existing from the tier back into any source.

6.3 The Event Backbone

The backbone is Apache Kafka 4.3 with KRaft, the Raft-based controller that removes the older
coordination service. Ordering holds per key: tag streams are partitioned by tag name, so the sequence
of any one variable is never reordered even when the whole plant is flowing through at once. Delivery is
at least once, made effectively once by idempotent writes keyed on each source's sequence numbers, so
a replay after a fault cannot double-apply an operator action or a lab value. Buffering sits at two levels: the
adapter buffers against a slow source, and the plant side of the boundary buffers when the link into the
analytics zone fails, with the backbone resynchronizing on restore. Replication runs inside the plant
cluster, so the loss of a broker does not lose a shift. The one crossing of the control boundary is the Lidi
with Eurydice one-way transfer, which fails closed: when the link, the power or the update path fails, the
diode stops, the adapters buffer, the agents pause their drafts, and the kiln's control path is untouched.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 7

Inference Belongs Where the Data Is

Each tier runs what its data and its link can carry.

Chapter 6 described how the plant's systems of record enter through three adapter families, never
directly, and how the event backbone orders and buffers what they emit. This chapter fixes where each
model runs, what each tier can carry, and what happens when the connections between those places
break.

7.1 Three Tiers Hold Three Different Jobs

The frontier tier runs GLM 5.3 on one node of eight accelerators of the 141 GB class, and the memory
arithmetic is the whole argument for that shape. The model has 753 billion parameters filed, and at FP8
precision, one byte per parameter, its weights occupy 753 GB. Multiplying by the 1.2 planning factor,
which reserves room for the KV cache and activations, gives 904 GB the GPUs must hold. One node of
eight 141 GB accelerators offers 1,128 GB of usable memory, which leaves 375 GB beside the weights,
more than twice the 151 GB the planning factor reserves, so the KV cache ceiling clears with margin and
the work surface never needs a second node. This tier carries the reasoning work: drafting causes from
an upset's assembled story, drafting shift handovers, maintaining the ontology, and answering the control
room's questions with citations.

The plant tier runs on the plant GPU server, on one or two PCIe cards and no high bandwidth memory
node. Chronos-2, about 0.24 GB at 16-bit precision, forecasts the stable band on the streaming tags and
its residuals are thresholded to raise the drift trigger. BGE-M3, about 1.1 GB at FP16, embeds past
upsets, shift logs and maintenance history so the reasoning tier can retrieve them. Both models fit on a
single card with room to spare, which is why the design buys no additional frontier hardware for them.
This tier is where the stream meets a model: the telemetry adapter feeds the tag stream of hundreds of
variables into the event backbone, and the timeseries model watches it continuously.

The edge tier is the industrial octa-core SoC edge unit with a 6 TOPS NPU in a sealed fanless enclosure,
served by ONNX Runtime. It holds roughly 33 degrees C of margin at the 52 C record ambient before
solar gain, and it sits closest to the data. Figure 6 sets the three tiers side by side, with what runs on each
and what crosses between them.

         Figure 6. Where each tier runs, what runs there, and the narrow set of outputs that cross the boundary.

7.2 The Latency Budget Follows the Physics

Each agent's deadline is set by the cadence of the physical process it serves, not by a service level
anyone chose. The drift anomaly must land inside the scan rate of the tag stream it watches, because a
warning that arrives after the next scan is a history entry rather than advice. The setpoint agent's drafts
after a fuel lot change must arrive while that lot is still feeding the burner, or they describe a lot that has
already been burned through. The handover draft has the end of the shift as its deadline, and the
improvement figures behind it close when the laboratory data lands.

Cause drafting is the one job with no tight deadline, because an upset's story is assembled across hours
of historian, laboratory and fuel data, and depth of reasoning matters more than speed there. That is
frontier tier work by choice rather than necessity. The design's rule is simple: anything with a physical
deadline runs on the plant tier beside the stream, and only drafts, citations and questions travel to the
frontier node.

7.3 The Boundary and What Fails Through It

Reads flow one way from the systems of record into the analytic zone, and the control network boundary
is enforced by the Lidi with Eurydice one-way transfer stack, a data diode that carries plant data out for
analysis and makes a return path physically absent rather than merely blocked. No model output crosses
into the control system in any direction, because the single write path in the whole design is a human
confirming a draft, and nothing about the plants leaves the country: every weight runs on the company's
own hardware inside it.

When the link between tiers fails, the event backbone buffers and the historian backfills on reconnect,
while the surfaces mark every standing draft as stale with the time it was computed at, so a control room

operator never mistakes a prediction frozen mid-shift for a live one. When power fails, the sealed edge
unit restarts, resynchronizes against the plant's time sources under Chrony with the offsets recorded, and
reconstructs the stream from the historian rather than from its own memory. When the update path fails,
the Harbor offline registry keeps the running versions in place: containers and models are staged, signed
and verified on site, and if a staged update cannot be verified, the previous version keeps serving while
the mismatch is surfaced to the platform engineers rather than left to diverge silently.

The License Decides What the Operator Can Own

8.1 Each Model Was Chosen Against Its License

Figure 7 shows the model stack as three cards: GLM 5.3 at the frontier tier, Chronos-2 and BGE-M3 at
the plant tier, with the equipment classes beneath them. GLM 5.3, named in the company's own
requirement, is a mixture of experts language model with 753 billion parameters filed and published as
open weights. At FP8 its weights occupy about 756 GB, roughly 1.5 TB at BF16, which is why it needs
eight accelerators of the 141 GB class before any KV cache is counted. It runs on the frontier node in the
country and carries two jobs: the agentic work surface, where the control room's people build and run
their agents against the ontology, and ontology maintenance, where the governed model of the kiln line
stays aligned with the systems of record beneath it.

Its license is the GLM-5.3 bespoke license, whose terms allow commercial use, fine tuning and
redistribution. Two consequences follow. The company can hold the weights on its own hardware without
a service relationship it cannot exit, and the license's model as a service trigger stays inapplicable
because every inference is internal advisory use inside the company's boundary. Recursive self-
improvement is an active priority at frontier AI companies and is beginning to diffuse into the broader
corporate ecosystem (Stanford 2026); this design declines that road in the one place its license would
permit it. The weights never change, and improvement compounds in the memory of confirmed
outcomes, which is retrieval rather than training.

Chronos-2 is the timeseries model, about 0.48 GB at 32-bit precision and about 0.24 GB at 16-bit, small
enough to sit beside the embedding model on a single PCIe card in the plant GPU server. It performs
zero-shot multivariate forecasting with covariates: it forecasts the stable band on the streaming tags, and
its residuals are thresholded to raise the drift trigger. Its Apache-2.0 terms impose nothing on the
company beyond attribution, and with no fine tuning in the plan the model can be held, moved and rerun
inside the plant for as long as the plant wants it.

BGE-M3 is the retrieval embedding model, about 2.27 GB at float32, about 1.1 GB at FP16 and about 0.6
GB at 8-bit; the design serves it at FP16. It performs multilingual dense, sparse and multi-vector retrieval
in one pass, which is what keeps Arabic and English shift logs and part numbers from the maintenance
system retrievable in the same query. Its MIT license sits at the permissive end of the register, so the
company holds it outright.

9.2 What the Rollout Measures

One number carries the gate: thermal energy per tonne of clinker, drawn from the production reporting
system, compared between periods with the drafts on and periods with the drafts off, on the same line.
The honesty bar comes from the sector's own precedent, in which a continuous month that read 4.1
percent fell to 2.2 percent specific heat consumption once the same line ran a controlled on/off
comparison, so the headline month is never the gate. Around that number the rollout measures
acceptance from the first weeks: how many drafts each control room operator confirms, edits or rejects;
how many upsets move from open to cause confirmed; time to recover, set against comparable upsets
already held in memory; and free lime held inside its specification band while the energy number moves.
Together these show whether the memory is compounding or merely recording, and they are the figures
the improvement surface puts in front of the shift supervisor.

9.4 Lessons

Shadow the drafts before anyone approves them. The incumbent controller lost the control room
because it argued from a model the operators could not question, and both crews switched it off when the
kiln misbehaved. The advisory route inverts that: drafts run first in shadow, every draft names its cause
and its expected effect, and the operator's confirmation or rejection is itself the recorded outcome the
memory compounds on. Trust is measured, not assumed.

Gate on the on/off comparison, not the headline month. The sector precedent is the instruction: a
continuous month read 4.1 percent where the controlled comparison on the same line read 2.2. Any figure
quoted without the on/off discipline is a forecast wearing the clothes of a measurement, and the phase-
one gate refuses to read it.

Capture the retiring operator before the retirement date. The knowledge of how the most experienced
operator brought the kiln back from an upset lives in nobody's notes, and it leaves with him. Elicitation

sessions sit in the opening weeks of Phase One, and the elicited recoveries seed the upset objects the
agents retrieve against.

9.5 What Is Still Open

Three questions settle before design freeze, and each one moves the design. The export license position
for the 141 GB class node: settling it either confirms one node of eight accelerators or reshapes the
footprint onto two 80 GB class nodes, changing the memory arithmetic with it. The facility criticality level
under the national OT cybersecurity control: settling it sets the control burden and the boundary
engineering, and it is the OT security function's call, not the design's. The master asset register: settling
whether the DCS tag namespace or the maintenance equipment hierarchy is master decides how the
ontology joins tags to equipment, which is the join the whole argument rests on. A fourth question is the
phase-two gate itself: settling what evidence extends the system to further lines and plants decides how
the single-line proof is read.
