PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 6

Every Source Enters Through an Adapter, Never Directly

All eight named source systems enter through one of two adapter families, telemetry for the
logger network and integration for everything else, so no source is read directly and no
system of record is modified.

Chapter 5 described what the object model holds and who writes to it. This chapter describes how data
gets into it: all eight named source systems enter through one of two adapter families, and no source is
ever read directly.

6.1 Every Named Source and Its Provenance

Every source in this design is of operator provenance and read-only in direction. The instrumentation data
logger network and its historian supplies the minute-level readings for every instrument. The satellite
radar deformation reports supply the quarterly surface deformation surveys that join to instrument trends
in the section story. The daily inspection app holds the operators' recorded observations, today in words
nobody searches. The trigger action response plan supplies the trigger levels and predefined actions the
agents draft against. The engineer of record's reports and drawings supply the design basis and the
section definitions the ontology anchors on. The deposition and raise plans supply the events that explain
instrument behavior. The water balance model supplies the forecast that pond level divergences are read
against. The regulator's correspondence supplies the submissions, notices and due dates that are
tracked as objects. Figure 5 maps each named system to its provenance class and its adapter path. The
industry has reached the same conclusion from the other side: the Global Mining Guidelines Group
published a guideline for sharing open data sets in mining because data held in systems that cannot be
joined is data wasted (Gmggroup 2022), and China's national mine safety authority issued basic
requirements for data fusion and sharing in intelligent mines (Chinamine-safety 2023). This design joins
the owner's data inside its own boundary instead of publishing it.

       Figure 5. The 8 named systems, the adapter path each one takes, and the object model they all map into.

6.2 What the Adapter Tier Guarantees

The adapter tier makes five guarantees. First, no service, agent or model reads a source system directly;
the telemetry adapter and the integration adapter are the sole readers, so the no-modification rule is
enforced at one choke point. Second, every source enters with its provenance class and read direction
recorded, so any object can be traced to the system that holds it. Third, the telemetry adapter follows the
site's own standard, reading the historian's live API or OPC UA feed rather than imposing a protocol, and
the integration adapter takes reports, plans and correspondence on a schedule suited to each. Fourth,
mappings land in the object grammar of nouns, properties and typed links, and readings carry quality
flags so a degraded sensor is visible as such rather than silently trusted. Fifth, the tier applies
backpressure, so a surge of readings slows ingestion instead of flooding the model, and no write path
ever returns to a system of record, which is what leaves the existing TARP alarm path in the historian
untouched.

6.3 The Event Backbone

Between the adapters and the object model sits an event backbone, Apache Kafka 4.3.x in KRaft mode,
and its job is to preserve order and causality. Readings are keyed by instrument tag, so every
instrument's readings keep their order within a partition even when the fleet of loggers delivers in bursts.
Delivery is at least once, with idempotent writes keyed on tag and timestamp, so a replay after a fault
cannot double-count a reading. Broker retention buffers the flow when a consumer pauses, and
replication inside the site server room keeps the backbone alive through a node loss. Because every
causal claim in the section story joins readings on timestamps, time itself is a first-class concern: linuxptp

with an OCP Time Card grandmaster, disciplined by chrony, keeps the loggers, the edge units and the
services on one clock. Telemetry lands in InfluxDB 3 Core for trend queries, and every artifact and model
update arrives through Harbor in offline install as the air-gapped registry, so even the update path crosses
no external boundary.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 7

Screening Belongs at the Loggers and Reasoning on
Site

Anomaly screening runs on edge units at the logger network, trend baselines and the drafting
agents run in the site server room on one node of eight 80 GB GPUs, and nothing crosses
the network boundary.

Chapter 6 described how every source enters through an adapter and lands in the object model, never
directly. This chapter places the compute that reads what lands: anomaly screening on edge units at the
logger network, trend baselines and drafting agents in the site server room, and nothing beyond the
owner's own hardware.

7.1 Three Tiers and the Memory Arithmetic

The design runs inference on three tiers, and each tier exists because of what it must see and how soon
it must see it. The edge tier is a set of on-device edge units placed at the logger network, where Granite
Tiny Time Mixers (TTM r2) screens readings for anomalies before they travel anywhere; its footprint is
about 0.003 GB at 32 bit, small enough that the precision choice barely matters, and it serves many
instrument tags at the gateway on CPU-class hardware under ONNX Runtime. The NPU load on the
edge core is unmeasured for this screener, so a dev-board measurement stands as a phase gate before
the units are committed.

The site tier runs in the site server room beside the GPU node. Chronos-2, about 0.48 GB at 32 bit as
published and about 0.24 GB at 16 bit, builds trend baselines and residual anomalies for cross-instrument
patterns, taking rainfall and pond level as covariates so the pattern agent gets context with no training
run. Nomic Embed Text v2 MoE, 475 million parameters at about 0.95 GB in fp16, embeds reports and
inspection text for retrieval with citations; all of its parameters must stay resident because every expert is
live at inference.

The central tier is the drafting tier: gpt-oss-120b served with vLLM on one node of eight 80 GB GPUs, 640
GB of memory in total. The sizing rule the design stands on files 117B parameters at INT4, 0.5 bytes per
parameter, which is 58.4 GB of weights; the 1.2 planning factor reserves about 12 GB more for KV cache
and activations, so the GPUs must hold 70.1 GB, and the node holds it with 582 GB to spare beside the
weights. The model card files the same model as 116.8B total parameters with 5.1B active in a mixture of

experts architecture at MXFP4, about 61 GB, which fits a single 80 GB GPU with headroom. Figure 6 sets
the three tiers side by side, with what runs on each and what crosses between them.

         Figure 6. Where each tier runs, what runs there, and the narrow set of outputs that cross the boundary.

7.2 The Latency Budget

The budget is set by the cadence of the work rather than a number on a slide. The historian produces
minute-level readings, so edge screening must complete inside the reading interval: a screening result
that arrives after the next reading has displaced it screens nothing. Site-tier baselines run on the same
cadence, and their outputs feed the pattern agent rather than an operator, so they must be ready when a
trigger fires rather than when someone asks. The drafting agents work at the rhythm of an engineering
shift, because a pattern draft is useful while the trigger is still open and a response draft is useful while its
approver is still on site. The conversational surface must answer with citations at the pace of a
conversation, which is where the KV cache ceiling bites: the planning factor's reserve leaves the node's
memory mostly free above the weights, so concurrent sessions do not queue behind them.

7.3 The Boundary and the Failure Paths

Nothing crosses the network boundary. All compute sits on the owner's own hardware on site, no third-
party model service is called, and if the site segregates its logger network a hardware data diode is the
drop-in that keeps it that way. When the link between the logger network and the server room fails, the
edge units keep screening against their local model while the event backbone buffers and replays what
could not travel, so no reading is lost, only delayed. The existing trigger action response plan alarm path
keeps firing on single instruments regardless, because this design sits beside that path rather than
replacing it. When power fails, the edge units and the server room restart, the backbone replays its log,
and the agents resume from memory, since every confirmed pattern and its outcome is kept and read
before the next draft. When the update path fails, Harbor, the air-gapped artifact and model registry

installed offline, holds the newer artifacts and the running versions continue until an update can be carried
in; models arrive as artifacts on site, never as a service. One obligation stays open: the on-site compute
commitment is bound to a named scope item and confirmed with the owner's own compliance owner
before design freeze.

self-hosted, so the owner holds weights it can keep.

owner hold every weight it runs, which is the question an industrial AI reference architecture exists to

8.1 Four Models, One License Family

The work surface model is gpt-oss-120b, named by the owner. It is a mixture of experts architecture filed
at 116.8B total parameters with 5.1B active, which is why a model of this size fits one node rather than a
frontier cluster. Its checkpoint is 60.8 GiB, 65.2 GB of root safetensors, with the MoE weights in MXFP4 at
4.25 bits and the rest at 16 bit; that is about 61 GB, fitting a single 80 GB GPU with headroom, and about

234 GB if expanded to 16 bit. It carries the agentic work surface and ontology maintenance: the named
agents that draft, while engineers decide. It is Apache-2.0 and US origin, so the owner hosts it itself with
no vendor trigger and no per-token obligation.

The edge screening model is Granite Tiny Time Mixers (TTM r2), an IBM time-series foundation model at
about 0.003 GB in 32 bit, small enough that precision barely matters, running under ONNX Runtime on
the edge units at the logger network. It screens every reading for anomalies close to the instrument, so
only flagged or contextualized data needs explaining downstream. It is Apache-2.0 and US origin; its NPU
load on the edge core is unmeasured, so a dev-board measurement is the phase gate.

The trend baseline model is Chronos-2, an Amazon time-series model at about 0.48 GB at 32 bit, about
0.24 GB at 16 bit, running at the site tier beside the GPU node. It gives zero-shot multivariate forecasting
with covariates, taking rainfall and pond level alongside instrument readings, so the pattern agent
receives trend context without a training run, which the requirement forbids anyway. It is Apache-2.0 and
US origin.

The embedding model is Nomic Embed Text v2 MoE, 475 million parameters, about 0.95 GB at fp16 and
about 0.5 GB at 8 bit, with the Hub weights published at 32 bit so the download itself is about 1.9 GB. It
has an 8K context window and Matryoshka truncation, and its training data is published, which matters for
a surface that answers with citations over the engineer of record's reports and the inspection text nobody
used to search. It is Apache-2.0 and US origin, and all parameters stay resident because every expert
runs at inference.

8.2 The Model and Equipment Register

PA R T I I I · C H A P T E R 9

Shadow Mode Comes Before Any Draft Is Trusted

Three phases carry the work from one section bound into the ontology for two quarters,
through operation and hardening, to whole-facility scale-out, with drafts shadowed against
the owner's measures before anyone acts on them.

Chapter 8 settled the four models and the licenses that let the owner hold their weights on its own
hardware, which is the property that separates an industrial AI reference architecture for mining from
hosted analytics. This chapter carries that stack into the field in three phases, each stopped by a gate that
can end the work cheaply, with every agent draft shadowed against the owner's own measures before
anyone acts on it.

9.1 Three Phases, Fifteen Items and a Gate That Can Stop the Work

Phase One binds one section of the embankment for two quarters of record, and it carries 12 items
across five workstreams: the agents and memory, the facility ontology, the on-site platform, the phase one
gates, and the command centre. Its exit gate is that one section's records are bound into the ontology,
and its item order makes the method visible: bind one section's records, ingest logger readings with edge

validation, then ingest the surveys, inspections and plans that give those readings their context. The Run
phase carries 2 items under the on-site platform and the run, operate and harden workstreams, hardening
the running platform and then training the tailings team and handing over. Phase Two carries a single item
under the facility ontology workstream, scaling the ontology to every section, and it opens only after the
Run phase has hardened what Phase One proved. Figure 8 sets the three phases side by side with their
item counts, workstreams and gates. Each of the 16 requirements is traced to an item and to a gate, so
coverage is a matter of record rather than assertion: an item that answers no requirement is cut, and a
requirement with no item becomes an open question rather than a silent gap.

            Figure 8. The three phases and their gates, and coverage of the 16 requirements across them.

9.2 What the Rollout Measures

The owner stated four measures, and Phase One is judged against them and nothing else. Around them
the design carries gates of its own: a false trigger rate gate on the pattern drafts, an alert budget per
engineer per shift so that alarm fatigue is measured rather than argued about, a measurement of the
screener's load on the edge core taken on a development board before the edge tier is committed, and
data availability checks on the historian at the start of the phase, so that assumed history becomes known
history before any memory is built. The sector's own safety reporting shows everyday injuries falling while
preventing fatal and catastrophic events remains a persistent challenge (CIM 2026), and the annual
fatality and injury reporting across member companies is how the industry watches itself (ICMM n.d.); the
measures here therefore weigh the quality of the decision, not the volume of the data.

9.3 Failure Modes and Their Answers

Table 5 states what can fail and what the design does about each, and every row is carried into the phase
gates rather than left as a note.

  Table 5 · Failure Modes

   cooling for the GPU node                      fallback

9.4 Lessons

Bind the records before the agents run. The temptation in a facility with more readings than engineers
is to reach for the reasoning first, because the reasoning is what the owner asked to see. The design
refuses that order: the ontology workstream binds one section's objects and proves the joins on real
readings, and only then do the three drafting agents run against a model that can actually answer for
itself. Every phase gate in Figure 8 sits on that sequence.

Shadow the drafts before anyone acts on them. A pattern draft, a response draft and a reporting draft
are arguments, not actions, and the design keeps them that way until the owner's four measures say the
arguments are worth reading. The existing alarm path stays untouched beside them, so the worst case of
a noisy draft is a wasted review, never a missed trigger.

State the blind spot in every document. The failure mode that instruments did not see coming in the
sector's worst inquiries is carried as unsensed in every story, draft and submission the system produces.
A monitoring system that hides its own limits invites the reader to trust it beyond what it can see.

9.5 What Is Still Open

Four questions remain open, and settling each changes something specific. The screener's load on the
edge core is unmeasured, and settling it either confirms the edge tier as designed or moves anomaly
screening up to the site tier. The server room's power and cooling are unverified, and settling them either
places the reasoning node on site or moves it to the in-country colocation fallback, which changes the

boundary. The historian's depth and cleanliness are assumed, and settling them fixes how far back
matched past episodes can reach, which bounds what the memory can hold. The on-site compute
obligation is not yet bound to a scope item, and settling it with the owner's compliance owner locks the
boundary before design freeze, because no integration in the baseline answers it on its own.

PA R T I I I · C H A P T E R 1 0

The Intelligence Should Stay with the Facility That
Produced It

The object model, the weights, the memory of confirmed patterns and the decision record all
stay with the facility that produced them, which is what makes the sovereignty real rather
than a hosting choice.

Chapter 9 ended on the open questions the rollout must settle before design freeze. This chapter settles a
different question, the one that outlasts every phase: who owns what the work produces, and what that
ownership actually consists of.

10.1 What the Operator Holds at the End

The object model is the owner's, and it is a projection rather than a copy: the 15 objects and their typed
links describe the facility by joining the eight systems of record, and because the systems of record are
never replaced, never modified and never loaded elsewhere, the projection can be rebuilt from them at
any time and cannot be held hostage by the design that made it. The weights are the owner's in the
strongest available sense: all four models arrive under Apache-2.0, a license with no field of use trigger
and no termination on the owner's own decisions, and they run on the owner's own hardware beside its
logger network and in its site server room. There are no fine-tunes to own, because the design improves
by memory rather than by training, and that is a deliberate ownership choice: an asset that changes only
through recorded, reviewable memory cannot drift out from under the people accountable for it. The
decision record is the owner's as evidence, not just as data: every confirmed pattern, every approval by
the engineer of record and every outcome is kept and read by the next decision, which is what the
standard's accountability clauses actually demand. The sector has already seen what deficient record
keeping costs in an inquest after a mineworker's death (Nscafoundation 2020), and a record that lives in a
vendor's cloud is a record the owner holds on terms it does not set. The boundary, finally, is the owner's:
nothing crosses it, identity is served on site, and the single write path into the systems of record is a
named person approving a draft.

10.2 The Offer Behind the Design

The design maps directly onto what CodeNinja builds: Adaptive Operations carries the sensing, detection
and forecasting of physical behavior, from the piezometer and inclinometer readings through the edge
screening and the trend baselines that give the pattern agent its context; Hyper Ontology is the object
model itself, the governed 15-object projection over the systems of record that gives one embankment
section one story; Hyper Pragma is the work surface where the tailings team runs the named agents that
draft while engineers decide, on models the owner can change without losing what was built; Hyper
Engram is the kept record of confirmed patterns and outcomes that each run reads before it acts, memory
that does not update model weights; Sovereign Infrastructure is the posture the whole design stands on,
own hardware, Apache-2.0 weights and operation inside the owner's boundary; and Praxis is the platform
that produced this design, which is how every choice in it can be traced to recorded reading.

PA R T I V · C O N C L U S I O N

The Facility That Keeps Its Own Context Can Answer for
It
In one view, the design is a governed projection over eight systems of record the operation already holds:
2 adapter families carry their data into an object model of 15 objects, 6 services and 5 surfaces turn that
model into trends, drafts and read-only stories, and 4 permissively licensed models run from the logger
network to one eight-GPU node in the site server room, with three drafting agents proposing and named
engineers deciding. Nothing is trained, nothing replaces the alarm path, nothing leaves the owner's
hardware, and every confirmed pattern becomes memory the next decision reads, so the intelligence the
facility produces compounds where the accountability for it already sits, with the engineer of record, the
review board and the regulator behind the same story.

Running the same shape elsewhere takes four things rather than a particular industry: systems of record
that can be read without being replaced, a named person with the authority to confirm or reject every
interpretation, a site able to power and cool one GPU node of the 80 GB class, and model weights under
licenses that permit the owner to hold, inspect and keep them. Any operation with instruments,
inspections, plans and a regulator's correspondence can bind its own objects through the same grammar,
and the first gate, one section bound into the ontology against real readings, is cheap enough to stop the
work before it wanders.

PA R T I V · C H A P T E R 11

How Praxis Contextualized and Reasoned This Design

Every choice in this design traces to recorded reading in Praxis, from the ask and its
assigned family and industry, through the eight lenses and their cited sources, to the patterns

adopted and the equipment classes the design settles on.

Chapter 10 argued that the intelligence should stay with the facility that produced it. This chapter shows
where the design itself came from, because a reader being asked to trust the argument deserves to see
how it was reasoned. Every design in this series is produced on Praxis, CodeNinja's platform for
designing physical AI systems, and this chapter lets a reader trace any choice back to what justified it
(Figure 9). Nothing in the preceding chapters was asserted from preference: each model, each equipment
class and each phase gate lands on a recorded read.

11.1 Contextualizing the Ask

The ask was a requirement written in the owner's voice: a system design for monitoring a large tailings
storage facility classified at a high consequence level, instrumented under the global industry standard on
tailings management and under state dam safety regulation, operated by a mining company in the United
States. Praxis assigned the design to the Physical AI family and the Mining industry; the family and
industry pin was the designing engineer's own decision rather than a reasoned match, and the brief was
still read whole as reasoning input. What Praxis read was the corpus shelf of each lens, assembled
before the design was reasoned rather than from searches made to fit the conclusion.

 Figure 9. From the ask to the design: the family and industry Praxis assigned, the eight lenses and what each cited, the
                        patterns adopted and set aside, and the equipment the design lands on.

11.2 The Eight Lenses

Table 6 records what each lens could see, how many sources it cited, and what it contributed to the
design. No lens returned nothing, but two lenses worked without a shelf, and their contributions came
from the brief itself rather than from retrieved records.

11.3 Patterns Adopted and Set Aside

One pattern was adopted, system of context, as the primary, and it was pinned rather than won: the
requirement demands exactly its shape, in the owner's own words, one model of the facility as a
governed ontology, memory without training, and named agents that draft while engineers decide. The
pattern's fixed order governs the stack: systems of record below, never replaced, never modified, never
loaded; the owner-owned object model in the middle as a projection rather than a shadow copy, with
crossing mappings answering the questions no single system can; one small grammar in which nouns
become objects, facts become properties, relationships become typed links and actions change them;
and the kinetic loop closing on the model so the sense, decide, act, learn cycle makes it living rather than
static. No pattern was set aside, and that absence is itself informative: the ask matched the pattern so
exactly that no competing shape survived the first pass, which is why the design spends its rejected
alternatives on scoping decisions instead.

11.4 Where the Reasoning Lands

The reasoning lands on two equipment classes that carry the whole footprint: the 80 GB HBM GPU class,
which holds the reasoning model's weights with the headroom the memory arithmetic requires, and the
frontier model GPU footprint sizing rule for vLLM and SGLang serving, which turned the model's filed
parameters into a single eight-GPU node rather than a cluster guess. Everything else in the design, from
the telemetry adapter at the logger network to the read-only review views the review board sees, follows
from the joins the ontology must make and the boundary the owner set. The closing point is the one this
chapter exists to make: everything shown here was recorded reading, the ask, the shelf, the lenses and
their citations, and nothing in the design is inferred beyond it.

title: Industrial AI Reference Architecture for an Engine MRO Shop Floor in the United States
text:
V E R T I C A L - D R I V E N A R C H I T E C T U R E S · AV I AT I O N & A E R O S PA C E M A N U FA C T U R I N G · D E S I G N E D W I T H P R A X I S ·
NOVEMBER 2026

Industrial AI Reference Architecture for
an Engine MRO Shop Floor in the United
States
Critical Path Watch: Industrial AI in Engine Maintenance on Hardware the Shop Owns

Muhammad Umar, Cofounder, CodeNinja

For the shop general managers and operations directors accountable for engine turnaround, their planning, materials
and quality leads, and the data, integration and platform engineers who would build and run it.

Vertical-Driven Architectures is a CodeNinja series of system designs. Every design in the series is driven by a real-
world problem and scenario in a single industry, and every one is designed on Praxis, CodeNinja's platform for
designing physical AI systems. Operations are described by class, never by name.

ABSTRACT

Industrial AI in Engine Maintenance Must See the Critical
Path
An industrial AI reference architecture for an engine maintenance, repair and overhaul shop in the United
States has to answer one concrete question that industrial AI in engine maintenance, arriving as
dashboards, has not: which of the engines in work will miss its promised release date, and which part,
vendor repair or build slot is holding it. It has not been answered because the answer is split across the
maintenance and engineering system, the parts tracking system, the vendor repair order system and the
workscope contract, and those four meet only when the date is missed; shops of this class carry
hundreds of engines in work and tens of thousands of parts in flow at any time, in a year when turnaround
on narrowbody engines runs to six months or more, and the fix for a part that goes late at the same
vendor every quarter lives in a retiring planner's memory rather than in any system.

The design reads seven systems of record through one integration adapter family into a governed object
model of fifteen objects joined by typed links, runs seven services, among them a critical path agent that

drafts and a memory that improves the next plan without training, and presents four surfaces: a command
center, an approval queue, a vendor queue and a quality queue. One model carries the agentic work
surface and ontology maintenance, GLM 5.3 open weights, a frontier-class model at 753 billion
parameters, held by the shop itself under a license that permits commercial use, fine tuning and
redistribution, and served at INT4 on the shop's own hardware, one node of eight GPUs of the 80 GB
HBM class, where 376 GB of weights leave room for the key value cache and activations; there is no
edge tier and no third party model service, because the shop floor is watched through records rather than
cameras.

The paper covers the industry problem and the join failure across the shop's systems, the constraints that
shape the design, the stack from records to surfaces, the fifteen-object model, the adapter tier and event
backbone, the placement of inference on the shop's own servers, the model and its license, the two-
phase rollout with its gates and measurements, who owns what the design builds, and finally how Praxis
contextualized and reasoned the design, so that any choice in it can be traced back to the recorded
reading that justified it.

 Figure 1. Critical Path Watch on one page: the sources the operation already runs, one object model, what it computes,
                                             and the person who decides.

Contents
Each chapter is tagged for the reader it serves most directly: Executive, Team Lead, FDE, Reference.

  PA R T I · T H E P R O B L E M

  PA R T I I · T H E D E S I G N

 11      How Praxis Contextualized and Reasoned This Design                          Team Lead     FDE

         Sources                                                                     Reference

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 1

Industrial AI in Engine Maintenance Begins at the
Critical Path

Every engine in an overhaul shop has exactly one critical path, and today no system,
spreadsheet or person can see it before the promised date is missed.

The abstract put the whole industrial AI reference architecture on one page: seven systems of record, one
adapter family, an object model of fifteen objects, seven services, four surfaces and one frontier model on
the shop's own hardware. This chapter steps back to the question that design exists to answer, because

industrial AI in engine maintenance begins at the critical path of each engine, not at any model, and the
shape of the question decides everything downstream.

1.1 The Question and the Ground It Stands On

The shop needs one question answered continuously: for every engine in work, what is its critical path
today, and what will break it next? Answering it requires data no single system holds. The gate plan lives
in the maintenance and engineering system, the physical location of every serialized part in the parts
tracking and inventory system, the status of every vendor repair in the vendor repair order system, the
material orders that follow a workscope change in the material purchasing system, the findings that
trigger cascades in the inspection findings records, the outcome in the test cell data, and the promised
date and the terms that govern what the shop may decide in the workscope and contract records. The
regulatory ground is fixed alongside the data. As a repair station the shop answers to the FAA's part 145
regime, which requires maintenance records in English, retained two years from return to service and
producible to the FAA and the NTSB, with the content of each maintenance record entry fixed by 14 CFR
43.9. Because engine technical data is export-controlled, any release of it to a non-United States person
is a deemed export under the ITAR. Any system that reads these records inherits both regimes, and the
design must satisfy them rather than route around them.

1.2 The Documented Cost

The cost in practice is engines held on stands: turnaround on narrowbody engines at this point in the
demand cycle runs to six months or more, and one late vendor repair or one scarce part holds a finished
engine regardless of how much bay capacity the shop has. The supply chain that this parts flow runs
through carries documented integrity failures, which is the public record of what a shop without sight of its
own flow is exposed to. The Department of Transportation's Inspector General concluded that
enhancements were needed to the FAA's oversight of the Suspected Unapproved Parts Program (DOT
2017), and a United States District Court has sentenced a machine shop to probation and a fine for
aircraft parts fraud (DOT 2023). The FAA alerts owners, operators, air agencies and suppliers to
suspected unapproved parts reaching the fleet (FAA 2023), Europe's regulator publishes confirmed and
investigated unapproved parts cases (Europa 2018), and an industry coalition's final report recommends
controls across the supply chain, including for aircraft on ground situations (ARSA 2024). A shop that
cannot join its own parts, vendor and gate records cannot see a bad actor, a bad lot or a late vendor until
the engine is already held.

1.3 The Operation as a Scenario

The operator is an aircraft engine maintenance, repair and overhaul shop in the United States that serves
airlines and lessors, in a year when engine shop visit demand is at its peak. Shops of this class carry
hundreds of engines in work and tens of thousands of parts in flow at any time, and the design takes
those bands as its scale; anything specific to the shop is an assumption the design confirms rather than a
figure it asserts. The people in the loop are the planners who own the gate plans, the materials managers

who own orders and vendors, the inspection staff who raise findings, the engineers who disposition them,
the quality staff who keep the record honest, and the program manager who faces the airline. The
physical environments are the induction line, inspection, in-house repair, vendor repair beyond the wall,
assembly stands and test cells. The named estate is seven systems of record, all read-only to the design,
at a single site, with a rollout of two phases, each carrying a gate that can stop the work cheaply before it
spreads.

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 2

Every Shop System Sees One Slice of the Engine

The gate plan, the part's location, the late vendor repair and the promised date live in four
separate places that only meet when the engine misses its date, and the cost of that join
failure is measured in engines held on stands.

Chapter 1 stated the question and the regulatory ground it stands on. This chapter shows why nothing in
the shop can answer it today: each of the seven systems of record sees one slice of the engine, and the
slices only meet when the promised date is missed.

2.1 What Each System Sees

The maintenance and engineering system is the spine: it holds work orders, task cards, gates and the
engine's position against them, and it is where release is recorded, yet it has no idea where any serialized
part physically sits or which vendor holds it. The parts tracking and inventory system knows exactly which
part is where, in stock, in repair at a vendor, on order or installed, but it does not know the gate plan or
the date the airline was promised. The vendor repair order system knows a repair order is open, in work,
late or closed, and it knows the vendor, but it cannot see which engine's build slot that late order is
holding. The material purchasing system issues and tracks the purchase orders that follow a workscope
change, without knowing the inspection finding that triggered them. The inspection findings records hold
the finding, the engine manual reference, the inspector and the disposition, but not the cascade through
parts, vendors and build slots that the finding sets off. The test cell data holds parameters and the pass
outcome that closes an engine's story, without the parts story that explains a marginal parameter. The
workscope and contract terms hold the promised date and the terms governing what the shop may
decide, without any view of where the engine actually stands against that date. Figure 2 sets these seven
slices side by side.

    Figure 2. Seven systems, each seeing one part of the answer. The question needs all of them in one place at once.

2.2 What None of Them See Together

The critical path is a join across all seven: this engine's gate, the module on it, the serialized part in that
module, that part's repair order at a particular vendor, that vendor's on-time record and lead times, the
build slot and test cell booking waiting at the end, and the promised date judging all of it. No system holds
that join, so a planner's head holds it, and the knowledge that the same part on the same engine type
goes late at the same vendor every quarter lives in memory that retires with its holder. When a workscope
change at inspection moves a module from repair to replace, the cascade through parts, vendors and the
build slot is worked by hand over days, and the engine sits on its stand while it is worked. The cost is
measured in engines held, in six-month turnarounds on narrowbody engines, and in a planning bench
that is thinning into a market short of exactly the people who carry the join. That is the failure this design
removes: not any one system's blindness, but the absence of the place where the slices meet.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 3

Sovereignty and Export Control Shape Everything
Downstream

Open weights of United States origin on the shop's own hardware, export-controlled technical
data fenced as an ontology property, every decision left to a named person, and a first gate

that can stop the work cheaply, together fix the shape of everything the design does.

Chapter 2 showed the join failure: seven slices and no place where they meet. Four goals now fix the
shape of the fix before any component is chosen, because in this industry each goal is hard in a way that
removes whole families of architecture before the stack is even discussed.

3.1 Sovereign Operation on the Shop's Own Hardware

The first goal is the boundary the operator set in its own words: engine, airline and vendor data never
leave the shop's hardware, the models are open weights of United States origin, and no third party model
service is ever in the path. This is hard in this industry because the work surface needs a frontier model,
and a frontier model is a physical commitment: the design's model carries 753 billion parameters, which
at INT4 precision occupies 376 GB of weights, held with headroom for the key-value cache and
activations on one node of eight GPUs of the 80 GB class. A hosted service would make that someone
else's problem and the operator's exposure, so the design instead owns the arithmetic, the room, the
power and the support contracts as part of its own ground, served on site with vLLM.

3.2 Export Control Fenced in the Data Model

The second goal follows from the first and is harder than it: engine technical data is export-controlled, and
a non-United States person's access to it is a deemed export under the ITAR. A network rule alone cannot
be the fence, because the join the ontology exists to build is exactly the kind of crossing a blunt perimeter
control would break. The design therefore fences access control as a property on the objects themselves,
so the join works inside the fence and stops at it, and it carries a data classification pass before go live so
every object's exposure is known rather than assumed.

3.3 Every Decision Left to a Named Person

The third goal is that agents draft and people decide: a critical path draft, a workscope cascade, a vendor
chase or an airline notification is a draft until a named planner, materials manager or program manager
confirms it, and the confirmation is written back with an audit trail. This is hard because part 145 record
entries and dispositions require an approving person, and because the likeliest failure of an assistant is
over-trust: a planner confirming without reading. The design answers with drafts that carry their sources, a
disagreement path built before the agreement path, and agreement rates logged so the agents' own error
rate is instrumented.

3.4 A First Gate That Can Stop the Work Cheaply

The fourth goal is a stop that costs little: phase one covers one engine type and its induction line for a
quarter, and it exits only if the simulated failure of a high pressure turbine blade set is drafted the same
day against the shop's own baseline. This is hard because an engine type extension touches manuals,

vendors and test cells, so an unproved architecture spread across the estate is expensive to unwind; the
gate keeps the unwind cheap and lets the measured baselines decide whether extension happens at all.

Chapter 3 fixed the constraints and priced the scoping decisions taken under them. This chapter lays out

4.1 The Pattern and Why It Fits

The pattern is three layers in a fixed order. Below sit the systems of record, never replaced, never
modified, never loaded anywhere else; the seven systems the shop already runs hold every fact the
design reads. In the middle sits one object model, a projection over those systems rather than a copy of
them, where fifteen objects and the typed links between them form the one model of the shop the
operator asked for. Above sit seven services that draft, rank, remember and bind, and four surfaces that
put each draft in front of the named person who decides. The counts run end to end: seven sources pass
through one adapter family into fifteen objects, seven services and four surfaces, served by one open
weights model on the shop's own hardware.

The pattern fits because of what Chapter 2 showed: every system sees one slice of the engine, and the
slices meet only when the engine misses its date. A stack that joined nothing would change nothing; a
stack that joins the seven changes the question the shop can ask. Figure 3 shows the layered stack with
the count at each layer, and it marks one further decision: there is no edge tier, because the design
watches records and plans rather than the floor, and all inference runs centrally.

4.3 A Reusable Pattern

The reusable shape is the middle of the stack: systems of record left untouched below, one projection
ontology over them, drafting agents above with the decision reserved to a named person, memory that
improves the next plan without touching weights, and everything running on hardware the operator owns
inside its own boundary. A team carrying a similar brief would swap the source inventory, the object list
and the model with its GPU class, because those belong to the shop and the brief. What it should keep
unchanged is the discipline around them: every source enters through an adapter and never directly,
every join is a typed link rather than a keyword match, and the single write path back to a system of
record runs after named approval with an audit trail. Those decisions, not any particular component, are
what make the pattern sovereign and what let it survive the first workscope change at inspection.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 6

Every Source Enters Through an Adapter, Never Directly

All seven systems of record are read event by event through the integration adapter tier, with
change data capture offsets and monotonic sequence numbers ordering the stream, so the
model of the shop never goes stale and never writes back except after named approval.

Chapter 5 defined the fifteen objects and their typed links, the argument the shop has never been able to
make. This chapter describes how that argument stays current: how each of the seven systems of record
is read event by event, and what guarantees the reading carries.

6.1 Seven Sources, One Adapter Family

Every source named in the design is an operational system the shop already runs, and each enters the
same way: through the integration adapter, never directly. The maintenance and engineering system
holds work orders, task cards, gates and build slots, and it anchors the engine, module, gate, build slot
and release objects. The parts tracking and inventory system resolves serialized part instances and
material lots. The vendor repair order system holds repair orders and the vendor records behind them.
The material purchasing system issues purchase orders. The inspection findings records carry the
findings and dispositions that trigger the workscope cascade. Test cell data closes each engine's story
with parameters and pass findings. The customer workscope and contract terms hold the promised date
and the terms governing what the shop may decide, and it is read only. All seven are of operator
provenance, all are read, and none is written to by ingestion. Figure 5 sets each named system beside its
provenance class and its adapter path. Material integrity makes this tier more than plumbing: the aviation
supply chain carries a documented risk of unapproved parts, which the regulator actively works to
discover and remove (FAA n.d.), and the adapter preserves each record's certification and condition
properties so a quarantined lot can never silently become an installed part.

       Figure 5. The 7 named systems, the adapter path each one takes, and the object model they all map into.

6.2 What the Adapter Tier Guarantees

The adapter tier is one family, the integration adapter, built per system in scope work rather than bought,
and it guarantees four things. It reads event by event through change data capture and APIs rather than
batch extracts, so the ontology stays current status by status instead of nightly. It projects: each event
becomes a property change or a typed link on an existing object, so the model of the shop is a projection
over the systems of record, never a shadow copy of their tables. It preserves provenance, carrying the
source system, the record identifier and the capture position onto every object it touches, so any

statement the surfaces make can be traced to the record that produced it. And it never writes back: the
single write path into a system of record runs after a named person approves an agent draft, with an audit
trail.

6.3 The Event Backbone

Apache Kafka 4.4 carries the streams between adapters and the object model. Ordering comes from
change data capture offsets and monotonic sequence numbers per partition, which is why the design
needs no precision time protocol: a gate completion, a disposition and a repair order status change arrive
in the order the source systems committed them. Delivery is at least once, with consumers idempotent on
the capture position so a replayed event cannot double-apply a status change. Buffering absorbs a slow
consumer or a paused source, and replication inside the shop's estate means a broker loss does not lose
an event. When a link fails, adapters buffer and resynchronize from the last committed offset, and the
status-lag gauge in observability shows how far the model of the shop trails the shop itself.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 7

All Inference Runs on the Shop's Own Servers

Because the design watches records and plans rather than cameras, there is no edge tier:
every token is generated inside the shop's boundary on one node of eight 80 GB GPUs, and
nothing crosses the network boundary except what the shop's own people send.

Chapter 6 described how every one of the seven source systems enters through the integration adapter
tier as ordered, event-driven reads, so that the ontology stays current status by status. This chapter
describes where the tokens that read and reason over that ontology are generated, and why the answer
is a single tier inside the shop's own boundary.

7.1 One Tier, Because There Is Nothing to Sense at the Edge

The design watches records and plans, not cameras: the shop floor is not sensed, parts flow arrives from
the systems of record, and every fact the reasoning tier touches has already crossed the adapter tier as
structured data. Because there is no sensing, there is no edge tier, no edge orchestration of containers,
and no edge model serving; the honest architecture is one central inference tier running on the shop's
own servers, on the shop's existing network with a segregated VLAN agreed in scope work. Figure 6
shows that single tier, what runs on it, and the one thing that leaves it: what the shop's own people send.

The memory arithmetic fixes the tier's size. The work surface runs GLM 5.3 open weights, a frontier class
model with 753 billion parameters filed, at or above the 300 billion parameter threshold that defines the
frontier class. At INT4 precision each parameter occupies half a byte, so the weights alone are 376 GB.
The 1.2 planning factor reserves roughly another 75 GB for the KV cache, the memory that holds

conversation context so each new token does not force a recomputation of everything before it, and for
activations; the GPUs must therefore hold about 452 GB in total. One node of eight 80 GB GPUs offers
640 GB of high bandwidth memory, which holds the weights with 264 GB left beside them, headroom that
lets the KV cache ceiling rise with concurrent planner sessions rather than capping the number of
planners who can work at once. Serving runs on vLLM, the stack's on site language model serving
choice, with observability on Prometheus 3.13 LTS, Grafana and Loki.

        Figure 6. Where each tier runs, what runs there, and the narrow set of outputs that cross the boundary.

7.2 The Latency Budget Is Planner Paced, Not Machine Paced

Every surface in this design faces a person making a decision: the command center with engines by
promised date and risk, the approval queue for workscope cascades, the vendor queue with drafted
chases, and the quality queue for record integrity. The latency budget is therefore human paced, and the
binding constraint is not token generation but ontology freshness. A critical path draft is only as good as
the last change data capture event behind it, so the budget is spent on ingestion first: event driven reads
via APIs and CDC keep the object model current status by status, and the status lag between a system of
record and the ontology is a gauge in observability, a lesson taken from a record system that users
worked around because it could not see its own staleness. Generation that completes within a planner's
read of the draft it accompanies is inside the budget; a fast answer built on a stale part location is not,
which is why the freshness gauge outranks any serving benchmark.

7.3 The Boundary, and What Fails When It Fails

What crosses the network boundary is only what the shop's own people send: agents draft the customer
notification and the vendor chase, and the customer program manager and the materials manager send
them, because people decide. Customer, engine and vendor data never leave the shop's hardware, no
third party model service receives anything, and there is no outbound analytics zone. The link that matters

most is the update path, not the inference path: artifacts and model weights arrive through Harbor, the air
gapped registry, and if that path fails the running versions continue on pinned versions until it recovers,
since nothing in the daily loop depends on an external endpoint. If power fails, the node sits in a standard
conditioned server room and the clean shutdown practice is confirmed at design, with recovery reading
the event backbone's replicated log to resynchronize the object model. The remaining failure is human:
drafts that run on stale statuses, which the reconciliation pass and the lag gauge exist to catch.

8.1 One Open-Weight Frontier Model Carries the Work Surface

Figure 7 shows the model stack, and it is deliberately short: one model in the register, running on the
central tier, serving the agentic work surface and ontology maintenance that the command center, the
conversational interface with citations, and the drafting agents all depend on. The model is GLM 5.3 open
weights, frontier class with 753 billion parameters filed, served at INT4 on vLLM. Its role is the work
surface's: every planner works on a frontier model, on open weights only, and the design holds no closed
or hosted model anywhere in the loop.

The license, not the benchmark, is what decides whether the operator can own this. The GLM-5.3 license
is bespoke, and its terms permit commercial use, fine tuning and redistribution, which is exactly the set of
permissions a sovereign posture needs: the operator may run the weights for its own work, adapt them,
and hand copies onward inside its own estate without asking permission per use. Because the weights

are open and the terms allow holding them, the work surface survives the end of any engagement; the
sovereign exit rehearsal in phase two exists to prove that the model, the memory and the object model
leave together, which is the ownership argument in operational form. The register also records what was
weighed and set aside: gpt-oss-120b, a US-origin model on permissive, ungated terms, was proposed for
a site inference server, but its provenance was never rechecked against a returned source this session,
so it sits outside the register and the sizing for that layer remains open work rather than a settled figure;
BGE-M3, proposed for citation retrieval, was set aside for the same reason.

The retrieval the citations depend on matters beyond convenience, because the shop's records carry
safety weight: the regulator runs a standing program on suspected unapproved parts in the aviation
supply chain (FAA n.d.), and courts have sentenced parts suppliers for fraud (DOT 2023), so a draft that
cites its source records lets the quality queue check the provenance class of every material lot and

9.1 Two Phases, Two Gates and Fourteen Traced Requirements

Phase one covers one engine type and its induction line for one quarter, and it carries 14 items across six
workstreams: one model of the shop; agents that draft while planners decide; memory that improves the
next plan; the command center; rules that bind; and what runs where on the shop's own hardware. Its first
gate is the governed shop ontology build, passed on evidence rather than assertion: the joins are proved
on a week of production data before any agent runs, because an object model that cannot reconcile one
part's status across the systems of record has nothing to draft from. The phase's exit test is the fault the
shop named as the one that hurts, a simulated high pressure turbine blade set failing inspection: the
failure is injected into the phase's engine type, and the phase exits only if the drafted cascade appears
the same day against the shop's own baseline, covering the parts it moves, the repair orders it re-routes,
the purchase orders it raises and the build slot it reschedules.

Phase two carries 2 items, the engine type extension path and the sovereign exit rehearsal, and its gate
is that rehearsal: the export of the model, the memory and the object model is practiced end to end before

the shop ever needs to exercise it in earnest. Fourteen requirements govern the whole build, and each is
traced to a phase item; the trace is reviewed at each gate, and a requirement with no item behind it stops
the phase rather than surviving as intent.

             Figure 8. The two phases and their gates, and coverage of the 14 requirements across them.

9.2 What the Rollout Measures

The headline measure is engines released on the promised date, expressed in percent, with a nominal of
85 and a breach when the measured rate falls below it. That figure is the shop's own promise discipline,
not a benchmark imported from another industry, and the simulated blade failure tests the same discipline
at the cascade level, comparing the same-day draft against the baseline of how long the same cascade
took by hand. Around the headline sit the four baselines the shop keeps today, against which the agents
are measured; the agreement rate between planner and draft, logged on every confirmation; and a
status-lag gauge in observability that shows how far the object model trails the systems of record. The
memory loop records confirmed outcomes from the first day, so the measure of memory is whether the
next plan on the same engine type starts better informed than the last.

9.3 Failure Modes the Design Answers

The failure modes in Table 5 are drawn from the shop's own risk list and from precedents read in the
sector, and the supply chain context sharpens them: regulators maintain a program to discover and
remove unapproved parts (FAA n.d.), an industry coalition has published recommendations on supply
chain integrity under aircraft on ground pressure (ARSA 2024), and an oversight body has concluded that
oversight of such programs needs enhancement (DOT 2017). A shop that cannot see its critical path is
exposed to exactly the pressures those documents describe.

  Table 5 · Failure Modes

   W H AT FA I L S                        W H AT T H E D E S I G N D O E S

   Stale statuses in the systems of       A reconciliation pass on a week of production data precedes any
   record, so drafts run on bad data      agent, and a status-lag gauge in observability keeps the lag visible

   Planners confirm drafts without        Every draft carries its sources, the disagreement path is built first, and
   reading them                           agreement rates are logged

   Export-controlled technical data       US-person access control is an ontology property, with a data
   reaches a non-US person                classification pass before go-live

   A manual license forbids machine       Each manual source is license-reviewed before the retrieval index is
   reading                                built

   Planner knowledge retires before       The memory loop records confirmed outcomes from day one, and an
   memory captures it                     elicitation pass runs with retiring planners

   Draft quality on the shop's own work   Agents run beside the planners' process, measured against the four
   is unproven                            baselines, with gates that can stop extension

9.4 Lessons the Phase Structure Encodes

Shadow the drafts before anyone trusts them. The agents run beside the planners' process, never in
front of it, and every draft carries the sources it was built from; the disagreement path, the route by which
a planner rejects a draft and says why, is built before the agreement path is celebrated, because
agreement rates only mean something when disagreement is cheap.

Instrument the exception path, not the happy path. A workscope change at inspection, a crack that
moves a module from repair to replace, is where the record systems fail in practice, so the design treats
that cascade as its exit test rather than as an edge case; the lesson comes from the door plug case read
in the sector, where the exception was the path that mattered.

A record system users work around must instrument its own error rate. The military fleet logistics
lesson holds here: when planners keep private spreadsheets beside the system of record, the system's
numbers look clean while the shop runs on the shadow copy, which is why the status-lag gauge and the
reconciliation pass exist to make the gap visible.

Capture the planner's memory before it retires. The same part goes late at the same vendor every
quarter and the fix lives in one planner's head; the memory loop plus an elicitation pass with retiring
planners turns that head knowledge into records the next plan reads.

9.5 What Is Still Open and What Settling Each Would Change

Three questions remain open, and each narrows the build rather than changing its shape. The on site
inference server is sized against a model the register set aside, so its node count is open work until the
register's held model is sized; settling it fixes the hardware bill of materials and the KV cache ceiling. The

choice between the two time series stores held on the shelf for test cell data is an open decision; settling
it picks the store and its retention settings. The scale figures, hundreds of engines in work and tens of
thousands of parts in flow, come from public reporting on shops of this class, and confirming the shop's
own counts would fix object volumes and size the event backbone.

PA R T I I I · C H A P T E R 1 0

The Intelligence Should Stay with the Shop

The object model, the weights, the memory of confirmed outcomes and the decision record
belong to the shop that produced them, and the design rehearses their export before the
shop ever needs to exercise it.

Chapter 9 showed how the build earns trust in stages. This chapter settles the question those stages end
on: when the gates are passed, what the shop holds, and who can take it away.

10.1 What the Shop Owns on the Day the Gates Are Passed

The object model is the shop's from the first day of the build. It is a projection over the seven systems of
record, anchored in them object by object, never a copy that could drift into a second source of truth; the
crossing mappings, the typed links that answer questions no single system can, are the shop's working
asset, and they survive every change to the systems beneath them. The weights are the shop's under a
license that permits commercial use, fine tuning and redistribution, and the design deliberately creates no
fine-tunes to own: nothing is trained into weights, so what compounds is a memory the shop can read,
audit and export rather than a binary it cannot inspect.

The decision record is the shop's as well. Every approval carries the named person who made it and the
basis they made it on; release records carry their return to service date, approving person and retention
date as properties of the record itself; and material lots carry condition and certification with a quarantined
status, in a supply chain where regulators publish confirmed unapproved parts cases (Europa 2018) and
maintain a program to discover and remove them (FAA n.d.). The boundary is the shop's to hold: engine,
airline and vendor data never leave the shop's own hardware, no third party model service is called, and
the sovereign exit rehearsal in phase two proves the shop can walk away with all of it intact.

10.2 The Offer Behind the Design

CodeNinja builds this shape as products the shop can own outright. Decision Systems carries the
ranking, attribution and reconciliation that a named planner decides on, which is what the critical path
drafts and the workscope cascade are. Hyper Ontology holds the governed object model this design
projects over the seven systems of record. Hyper Pragma is the work surface on which the shop's own
people build and run their agents, on models the shop can change without losing what was built. Hyper

Engram is the kept record of decisions and outcomes that the next decision reads, and it never updates
model weights. Sovereign Infrastructure is the posture the whole design runs on: the shop's own
hardware, open-weight licenses and operation inside its own boundary. Praxis is the platform on which
the design was produced, and this paper is its record.

PA R T I V · C O N C L U S I O N

The Shop Should Keep the Intelligence Its Own Flow
Produced
The design is one governed model of an engine overhaul shop: seven systems of record read through
adapters and never replaced, fifteen objects whose typed links answer the questions no single system
can, agents that draft a critical path, a chase or a workscope cascade while a named planner decides,
and a memory that carries each confirmed outcome into the next plan, all of it running on one node of the
shop's own hardware under a license that lets the shop hold its weights, so the intelligence compounds
inside the operation that produced it rather than in a service it rents.

Running the same shape elsewhere takes four things the design already names: serialized part instances
as the spine of the object model, a reconciliation of live statuses proven on production data before any
agent runs, drafts that carry their sources with a disagreement path built first, and a sovereign exit
rehearsed before it is needed; any operation whose flow is dictated by parts rather than capacity, from
airframes to rotating machinery, can carry this shape by swapping its own systems of record, its own
objects and its own regulatory ground for the ones written here.

PA R T I V · C H A P T E R 11

How Praxis Contextualized and Reasoned This Design

This chapter records the ask, the family and industry assigned, and the reading behind each
choice, so that any decision in the paper can be traced back to what justified it.

Chapter 10 settled who owns what the build produces. This chapter opens the reasoning itself, so that
any choice in the paper can be traced back to the reading that justified it. Every design in this series is
produced on Praxis, and this chapter lets a reader trace any choice back to what justified it; Figure 9
shows the ask, the family and industry assigned, what it read, the eight lenses, the patterns and the
equipment the reasoning landed on.

11.1 Contextualizing the Ask

The ask arrived as a requirement written in the operator's own words: an industrial AI reference
architecture the shop owns, open weight models of United States origin on its own hardware, reading its
systems of record, with nothing about airlines' engines leaving its control or reaching a third party model
service. Praxis assigned the design to the Enterprise AI family and to Aviation and Aerospace
Manufacturing as the industry, with the country of operation, the United States, fixed by the operator's
own requirement. Praxis read the case study, tooling, hardware, rules, approach and history shelves;
every count, name and figure in this paper traces to that reading.

 Figure 9. From the ask to the design: the family and industry Praxis assigned, the eight lenses and what each cited, the
                        patterns adopted and set aside, and the equipment the design lands on.

11.2 The Eight Lenses

Table 6 states, for each lens, what it could see, how many records it cited, and what it contributed. No
lens returned nothing, but two lenses, First principles and Domain fusion, worked without a shelf: the first
from the pinned sector brief, the second by fusing the pinned pattern's capabilities to the sector.

11.3 Patterns Adopted and Set Aside

One pattern was adopted, system of context, as primary and pinned before reasoning began, because
the requirement is its exact case: one governed model of the shop over systems of record, agents that
draft while planners decide, memory without training, owned by the operator. Its four moves run through
the paper: three layers in a fixed order, with the systems of record below, never replaced, never modified,
never loaded; the ontology as a projection whose crossing mappings answer the questions no single

system can; one small grammar in which nouns become objects, facts become properties and
relationships become typed links; and a kinetic loop that closes on the model, sense, decide, act, learn,
with the return edge making the model living rather than static. No pattern was set aside. The design
stands on one pattern, which is what makes it an industrial AI reference architecture rather than a survey
of examples, because the precedents that shaped it were read as builds that happened, not as
illustrations. Two models were set aside, gpt-oss-120b and BGE-M3, in each case because the cited
source was never returned by this run's search; GLM 5.3 open weights is the register's one held model.

11.4 Where the Reasoning Lands

The equipment the reasoning lands on is two classes: the 80 GB HBM GPU class, and the Frontier Model
GPU Footprint Sizing Rule for vLLM and SGLang serving. The sizing arithmetic follows that rule: 753
billion parameters at INT4, at half a byte per parameter, are 376 GB of weights; the 1.2 planning factor for
KV cache and activations brings the requirement to 452 GB; and one node of eight 80 GB GPUs holds
640 GB, clearing it with headroom. Everything shown in this chapter was recorded reading: the ask as
written, the records read, the lenses with their citations, the precedents read as builds. Nothing is inferred
beyond the joins the paper itself states.

title: Industrial AI Reference Architecture for Fertilizer Plant Reliability in Pakistan
text:
V E R T I C A L - D R I V E N A R C H I T E C T U R E S · H E AV Y I N D U S T R Y & C O N S T R U C T I O N · D E S I G N E D W I T H P R A X I S ·
NOVEMBER 2026

Industrial AI Reference Architecture for
Fertilizer Plant Reliability in Pakistan
Cycle Watch: Sovereign AI Reference Architectures for Plant Reliability in Pakistan

Muhammad Umar, Cofounder, CodeNinja

For the complex's reliability and turnaround leads, the control, inspection and maintenance engineers in the loop, and
the platform, data and OT engineers who would build and run it.

Vertical-Driven Architectures is a CodeNinja series of system designs. Every design in the series is driven by a real-
world problem and scenario in a single industry, and every one is designed on Praxis, CodeNinja's platform for
designing physical AI systems. Operations are described by class, never by name.

ABSTRACT

An Industrial AI Reference Architecture for Plant
Reliability Begins With the Cycle Count
An industrial AI reference architecture for plant reliability exists to answer one question this operation
cannot answer today: what several gas-suspension restarts in 2026 have done to the reformer tubes, the
synthesis compressor and the seal history of a plant in Pakistan designed to run steadily between annual
turnarounds. Each stop and hot restart costs days of production and stresses equipment built for
continuous duty, and the hidden cost of every thermal cycle only surfaces at the turnaround, while the
reliability engineers rebuild each failure's history by hand across the historian, the work orders and the
inspection files, and the engineers who remember the last five restarts are retiring. The records needed to
answer the question already sit in the plant's systems of record, but they are joined after the failure rather
than read together before the next restart.

The design reads twelve source systems one-way, through four adapter families and across a hardware
data diode, into a governed object model of fourteen objects linked by typed relations; five services run
three drafting agents, for restart plans, cycle damage and turnaround scope, onto three surfaces for the
reliability team, with every draft confirmed by a named superintendent. Three models carry the reasoning:

Chronos-2 forecasts historian tags and thermal-cycle stress residuals, and BGE-M3 embeds work orders,
findings and shift log entries for cited retrieval, both on the site's air-cooled inference server, while GLM
5.3, a 753B-parameter frontier model held at FP8, runs the command center on one node of eight 141
GB-class GPUs on dedicated in-country hardware, so nothing about the plant leaves the country and
nothing ever writes to the control system.

The paper covers the industry problem and the join failure, the constraints that shape everything
downstream, the stack, the object model, ingestion through adapters, inference placement, the models
and their licenses, the rollout with its five phases, sixteen items and gates, ownership of what the design
builds, and it closes with the chapter on how Praxis contextualized and reasoned this design.

Figure 1. Cycle Watch on one page: the sources the operation already runs, one object model, what it computes, and the
                                                person who decides.

Contents
Each chapter is tagged for the reader it serves most directly: Executive, Team Lead, FDE, Reference.

       Abstract · An Industrial AI Reference Architecture for Plant Reliability Begins
                                                                                                Executive
       With the Cycle Count
