  PA R T I V · H O W I T WA S D E S I G N E D

         Conclusion · The Cycling Becomes Countable, and the Count Stays Owned          Executive

 11      How Praxis Contextualized and Reasoned This Design                             Team Lead     FDE

         Sources                                                                        Reference

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 1

Every Thermal Cycle Borrows Against the Turnaround

A plant built to run around the clock between annual turnarounds is being cycled by gas
suspensions, and no system counts what each thermal cycle is costing the reformer tubes,
the compressors and the urea reactor until the damage is uncovered too late to plan for.

The abstract set out an industrial AI reference architecture that reads the plant's own records and drafts
what named people confirm. This chapter stays on the plant floor and states the problem in the operator's
own terms before any architecture answers it: what the cycling is doing to equipment built to run steadily,
what that costs, and who is in the room when it bites.

1.1 The Question the Operation Needs Answered

An industrial AI reference architecture for plant reliability exists to answer one question, and this operation
needs it answered per asset: what has every thermal cycle since the gas suspensions began cost the
reformer tubes, the synthesis compressor and the urea reactor, and what should the next restart and the
next turnaround therefore do differently. The data that answers it is data the operation already holds: tags,
alarms and trips from the distributed control system and its historian, the equipment master and work
order history, inspection findings and corrosion readings, vibration spectra on the large compressors,
laboratory findings, the shift log narrative, turnaround scope lines and the gas restoration notices that
start each restart. The answer must also satisfy the country's own instruments: data protection, cyber
crime, factories, boilers and pressure vessels and provincial environmental acts, together with the
insurer's engineer and the plant's management of change discipline, and none of it may leave the country.

1.2 The Documented Cost of the Problem

In 2026 the plant and others of its class were stopped and restarted repeatedly by gas supply
suspensions, pipeline damage after floods and import constraints, and the country reported a fertilizer
shortfall of over two hundred thousand tonnes as a result. Each unplanned stop and hot restart costs
days of production and stresses equipment designed to run steadily for a year between annual
turnarounds, and each restart produces trips, leaks and alarms that are handled and then forgotten while
the hidden cost accrues toward the turnaround. The cost of forgetting is documented well beyond this
industry: a review of publicly available coronial inquiries into fatalities in the resources sector since the
year 2000 traces deaths to the loss of corporate memory (Ausimm n.d.), and a coronial inquiry held that
the loss of workplace knowledge that followed changes in ownership was explainable but not excusable
when it contributed to a worker's death (Ohsalert 2025). At this complex the engineers who remember the
last five restarts are retiring, which turns a documented industry hazard into this plant's own exposure.

1.3 The Operation as a Scenario

The operator is a fertilizer manufacturer in Pakistan running an ammonia and urea complex on pipeline
gas and imported regasified gas: reformers, synthesis compressors, a granulation train and a bagging
plant, working around the clock between annual turnarounds and now cycled on the order of a dozen
times a year by gas suspensions. Scale figures come from public reporting on plants of this class in the
country, and anything specific to the complex is an assumption to confirm. The people in the loop are the
shift superintendents who confirm each restart, the reliability engineers who today rebuild equipment
histories by hand, the control engineers who own the boundary, the inspectors who walk the corrosion
routes, the turnaround planners, and the senior engineers, several of them retiring, who hold the
undocumented memory of the restarts. The physical environments are the reformer top deck, the
synthesis compressor train and the bagging plant lane, the three places sensing must watch. The named
estate holds seven systems of record plus the gas supply notice, and the full design draws on twelve
sources once sensing is counted, across one site in one country.

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 2

Each System of Record Sees One Slice

The historian, the maintenance system, the inspection files, the vibration monitors, the
laboratory, the shift log and the turnaround plan each hold part of the story of one
compressor, and none of them can hold it together before the equipment fails.

Chapter 1 set out the question. This chapter explains why no system the operation already runs can
answer it.

2.1 What Each System Sees

Distributed control system and its historian the primary signal source for tags, alarms and trips, read one-
way

Maintenance management system the equipment master and work order history the agents reason over

Inspection and corrosion monitoring records inspection findings and corrosion readings anchor the cycle
damage ranking

Vibration monitoring system continuous condition on the large compressors, the precursor signal for the
seal failure mode

Laboratory system lab findings join the equipment story for product and process quality

Shift log the narrative record of every restart's trips and leaks, today rebuilt by hand

     Figure 2. Eight systems, each seeing one part of the answer. The question needs all of them in one place at once.

2.2 What None of Them See Together

Each holds one slice, and the question needs all of them in one place at once, which today is done by
hand at the cadence of whoever has the time.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 3

Sovereignty and One-Way Reads Shape Everything
Downstream

Reading only and never writing to the control system, keeping every byte inside the country,
improving the restart plan without training a model on the fly, and putting a cheap first gate in
front of the work are the four constraints that decide every layer below them.

Chapter 2 showed the join failure: seven systems and a notice, each holding one slice of the same
compressor. This chapter turns the operator's own requirements into four constraints that decide every
layer below them, and then records what the design scoped and what it chose against.

3.1 The Control System Is Read Only

The first constraint is the operator's own sentence: the architecture never writes to the control system.
This is hard in this industry because the distributed control system is the plant's safety-relevant nervous
system, and the standard integration habit is a firewalled read-only database connection, which is one-
way only as a matter of policy and policy drifts with time and staff turnover. The design therefore crosses
the OT boundary through a hardware data diode carrying a one-way file transfer, physically incapable of a
write, and any later change to the boundary passes management of change with the control engineer's
signature. The plant keeps running exactly as it does today if the read path is cut.

3.2 Nothing Leaves the Country

The second constraint keeps every byte about the plant inside Pakistan, which rules out foreign clouds
and any inference outside the boundary. It is hard because the work surface model is frontier class: 753
billion parameters at FP8 precision mean roughly 756 GB of weights that must be held on the operator's
own new dedicated in-country hardware, and the country's export control position means a license
determination under the ECCN 3A090 and 4A090 categories, which turn on total processing performance
rather than memory, precedes any GPU class being quoted. This is where an industrial AI reference
architecture earns the word sovereign: the weights, the records and the decision all stay with the
operation that produced them, with an approved in-country data center held as the fallback placement.

3.3 Improvement Runs Through Memory, Not Weights

The third constraint is the requirement's own phrasing: the next restart plan must be better without
training a model on the fly. This is hard because the obvious way to make an agent better at restarts is to
fine tune it on restart histories, which the requirement rules out. The design instead keeps a memory of
confirmed restart causes and accepted inspections that every run reads before it acts, so improvement
compounds through what people have confirmed rather than through weight updates, and the weights the
operator holds remain the ones it can account for.

3.4 A Cheap First Gate Stands in Front of the Work

The fourth constraint puts a stoppable gate before the expensive commitments. Phase one covers only
the ammonia front end and the synthesis compressor train for one quarter, including at least one restart,
and it is gated on the operator's four baselines. If the baselines are not met, the work stops before the
ontology of the whole estate, the extension to urea and utilities and any further hardware are committed,
which is where learning the design is wrong still costs little.

3.5 Scoping Decisions

The scoping decisions trade reach for control, and Table 1 records each one with what it buys and what it
costs.

Each rejected alternative was rejected for a stated reason, and Table 2 records them, ending with what

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 4

One Stack Runs From Diode to Command Center

Systems of record sit below a hardware data diode, one governed object model holds the
plant's story in the middle, and drafting agents, services and the reliability team's surfaces
run above it, all on the operator's own hardware.

Chapter 3 settled the constraints that shape everything downstream: nothing about the plant leaves the
country, the control system is never written to, the plant's story must outlast the engineers who hold it in
memory, and the first gate must be cheap to stop. This chapter sets the stack that meets them, from the
diode at the bottom to the command center at the top.

4.1 Three Layers, One Boundary

The architecture is a three-layer pattern. Below sit the systems of record in the OT zone: the distributed
control system and its historian, the maintenance management system, the inspection and corrosion
records, the vibration monitoring system, the laboratory system, the shift log, the turnaround planning
system and the gas supply notice. In the middle sits one governed object model that turns those records
into a single story of equipment under cycling stress. Above it run the applications and agents: three
drafting agents for restart, cycle damage and turnaround scope, five services and the reliability team's
three surfaces. The layers are separated by hardware, not by policy: lidi over a hardware data diode
carries the read out of the OT zone, and nothing above the diode has a path back in. The pattern fits
because the problem is a join failure rather than a sensing failure, and because it keeps every tier on the
operator's own hardware in Pakistan, which is the shape every sovereign industrial AI reference
architecture shares. Figure 3 shows the layered stack with its counts: twelve sources, four adapter
families, fourteen objects, three models, five services and three surfaces, with the frontier tier on one in-
country node.

4.3 A Reusable Pattern

The shape a team can carry away is this: read the systems of record through a physically one-way
crossing into a governed object model anchored on one equipment master, let agents draft against that
model, put a named person between every draft and every action, and let memory rather than fine tuning
carry what each cycle teaches. A team carrying a similar brief swaps the object set, here fourteen objects
for a cycled ammonia-urea complex, the source list and the agent set, here restart, cycle damage and
turnaround. What they keep is the diode, the single equipment master, the confirmation loop and shadow
mode before any draft is trusted, because those four are what make the pattern safe to point at a running
plant.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 5

Fourteen Objects Turn Cycling Into One Argument

Equipment, tags, trips, restarts, thermal cycles, work orders, findings, readings and plans link
into one typed graph, so the question the turnaround asks can be answered by query instead
of by the archaeology reliability engineers perform by hand today.

Chapter 4 put one governed object model at the middle of the stack and made it the one place the plant's
story is joined. This chapter opens that model: fourteen objects, the typed links between them, the human
loop wrapped around them and the posture they are hosted under.

5.1 Every Object and Its Links

Fourteen objects hold the story. On the asset side sit Process Unit and Equipment; on the measure side,
Historian Tag, Corrosion Reading and Vibration Reading; on the event side, Trip, Restart and Thermal
Cycle; on the record side, Work Order, Inspection Finding, Lab Result and Turnaround Task; on the
document side, Shift Log Entry and Restart Plan. Each is anchored in a system of record: Equipment in
the maintenance management system, Historian Tag and Trip in the distributed control system and its
historian, Restart in the shift log, Inspection Finding and Corrosion Reading in the inspection and
corrosion records, and the rest accordingly. The links are typed and directional: a Trip belongs to a
Restart and is cited by a Restart Plan; a Thermal Cycle, a Work Order, an Inspection Finding and a

Turnaround Task each point at the Equipment they concern; a Shift Log Entry references the Restart it
narrates and the Restart Plan it supports. Figure 4 draws all fourteen objects and their links, with
Equipment as the focal object. What the links buy is traversal: a query can ask for every trip on the
synthesis compressor across this year's restarts, each with the shift log entry that narrates it, the work
orders that followed and the vibration readings either side, and get one answer, where a document store
holds all those records but cannot join them. That join failure is why reliability engineers rebuild equipment
histories by hand today, and its cost is documented well beyond this plant: reviews of coronial inquiries
into resources-sector fatalities trace deaths to the loss of corporate memory (Ausimm n.d.), a coroner has
called the loss of workplace information after ownership changes explainable but not excusable (Ohsalert
2025), and a labor union has had to mine its own old newsletters to recover its record of past accidents
(OR 2021). Cycling a plant a dozen times a year makes that loss more likely, not less. Table 8, printed by
the platform, sets out each object, the system of record it is anchored in and its typed links.

5.2 The Human Loop and the Hosting Posture

The human loop lives in the status vocabularies. A Restart moves from Drafted to Confirmed by
superintendent to In progress to Stable; an Inspection Finding moves from Open to Accepted to Closed or
Brought forward; a Restart Plan moves from Drafted to Confirmed to Superseded, never silently
overwritten. Every status change carries a named person and a timestamp, so the graph records who
confirmed what, and an agent's output remains a draft until someone with authority says otherwise. The
hosting posture follows the constraints. The model runs on the operator's own hardware in Pakistan,
identity is held on site by Keycloak, external links are blocked except the controlled export path through
which report packs for the insurer's engineer leave after a disclosure review, and the single write path into
the object model is the adapter tier below and the confirmation loop above. Nothing writes back through
the diode, and nothing about the plant leaves the country.

Every Source Enters Through an Adapter, Never Directly

Twelve named sources cross the boundary through four adapter families, each carrying its
provenance class, so the plant's systems of record are read one-way and the ontology

Chapter 5 defined the fourteen objects the model holds and the confirmation loop that guards them. This
chapter describes how data reaches those objects: every source crosses the boundary through an
adapter, and nothing crosses back.

6.1 Twelve Sources and Their Provenance

Twelve sources feed the model, and each arrives with its provenance class stamped on every record.
Eight are systems of record named by the operator, all read-only: the distributed control system and its
historian, the maintenance management system, the inspection and corrosion monitoring records, the
vibration monitoring system on the large compressors, the laboratory system, the shift log, the turnaround
planning system and the gas supply notice whose arrival triggers the restart agent. The design adds the
rest as sensing feeds: the fixed camera lanes at the reformer top deck, the synthesis compressor train
and the bagging plant lane, and the citation check that runs on conversational answers before they are
shown. Each source is assigned to one of four adapter families, integration, telemetry, ops systems and
ERP, chosen by the shape of the interface rather than by the vendor, and Figure 5 maps every source to
its family, its provenance class and its path across the boundary. The shift log deserves its own note,
because it is the narrative record of every restart's trips and leaks and today it is written but rarely
retrieved: an inquest into a site death heard that none of the contractor's employees had read the safety
manual for the machine that killed him (Constructionnews 2009), the familiar pattern of records held but
never joined, which is exactly what the digitized shift log and its links exist to end.

6.2 What the Adapter Tier Guarantees

The adapter tier guarantees five things. First, one-way flow: the crossing is lidi over a hardware data
diode, which is physically one-way where a firewalled read-only connection is only policy one-way, and
any later change to the boundary passes management of change with the control engineer's signature.
Second, provenance: every record carries the source system it came from and its class, so a trip from the
historian and a trip recalled in a shift log entry are distinguishable forever. Third, binding in place:
adapters translate each source into the object model's vocabulary, so the systems of record are never
replaced and never moved. Fourth, no bulk migration: the build reads live feeds and the agreed opening
balances only, leaving historic cleansing out of scope. Fifth, store and forward: when the far side of the
diode is unavailable the near side buffers, and the plant's systems never wait on the model.

6.3 The Event Backbone

Apache Kafka 4.3.x with KRaft is the backbone the adapters publish onto. Ordering is per partition key,
the tag id, the work order number or the restart identifier, so a trip never arrives in its partition before the
restart it belongs to. Delivery is at least once with idempotent writes keyed by source timestamp and
source identifier, so a replay after a store and forward drain deduplicates instead of double-counting a
trip. Buffering sits on the OT side of the diode, where store and forward rides out link loss without
touching the control system. Replication stays in country on the operator's own hardware, consistent with
the nothing-leaves rule. Time is held by the OCP Time Card grandmaster under linuxptp with a chrony
NTP fallback, so the historian, vibration and shift log records join on a common clock, and Prometheus,
Grafana and Loki watch delivery lag so a stalled feed is seen before the next shift's refresh is short.

Forecasting Belongs on Site and Reasoning in Country

Chronos-2 forecasting and BGE-M3 retrieval run beside the historian on the site server, GLM
5.3 drafts and answers on the dedicated in-country node, and only confirmed objects,
residuals and drafts cross between the tiers, with defined behavior when the link, the power
or the update path fails.

Chapter 6 described how every source enters through one of four adapter families and lands on the event
backbone, with nothing written back to a system of record. This chapter decides where the three models
run, and the decision follows two forces: the home of the data each model reads, and the patience of the
person waiting on its output.

7.1 Two Places to Run, and the Arithmetic That Fixes One of Them

The design runs inference in two places. A site server, air-cooled and inside the plant boundary, holds
Chronos-2, BGE-M3 and the vision models, with ONNX Runtime serving the edge duties; phase one runs
vision on this server rather than on camera-group edge units. A dedicated in-country node holds GLM 5.3,
served with vLLM. Forecasting belongs beside the historian because it reads the tag stream continuously
and writes residuals no one watches in real time; retrieval belongs on site because the work orders,
inspection findings and shift log entries it embeds are already there; vision watches the reformer top deck,
the synthesis compressor train and the bagging plant lane for steam plume, flange leak, operator,
maintenance scaffold and fire or smoke. Figure 6 sets the two tiers side by side with what crosses
between them.

The frontier node is fixed by arithmetic rather than preference. GLM 5.3 carries 753 billion parameters,
and at FP8, one byte per parameter, its weights are 753 GB; a node of eight GPUs of the 141 GB class
holds 1,128 GB, leaving 375 GB beside the weights, of which the 1.2 planning factor reserves about 151
GB for KV cache and activations. At BF16 the same weights would be roughly 1.5 TB and would not fit
the node. The site models are hardly a question: Chronos-2 is about 0.48 GB at 32 bit as published and
about 0.24 GB at 16 bit, and BGE-M3 is about 2.27 GB at float32 and about 1.1 GB at the FP16 the
design runs, so both sit beside the vision models with room to spare. The retrieval tier exists because the
records it makes findable are the ones that leave with retiring engineers, and reviews of coronial inquiries
tie fatalities in the resources sector to exactly that loss of corporate memory (Ausimm n.d.).

7.2 The Latency Budget

The budget is set by who waits, and only one model has a person in front of it. Chronos-2 runs on
cadence against the tag stream, so its budget is the freshness of the residuals the cycle damage agent
ranks against, not a human attention span. BGE-M3 answers inside a conversation: the query is
embedded, the matching records return, and only then does the answer begin, with a citation check on
conversational answers keeping it honest. GLM 5.3 carries the one real deadline, because a gas
restoration notice starts a clock that ends when the plant is stable; a restart draft must reach the
superintendent's surface before the walkthrough, and it never blocks one, since drafts run in shadow
beside the standing procedure the plant executes either way. An inquest into a fatal machine accident
heard that none of the employees had read the machine's safety manual (Constructionnews 2009), which
is the case for keeping the written procedure warm and the superintendent's confirmation real rather than
ceremonial. The slowest cadence is the shift by shift ontology refresh, which no one waits on at all.

7.3 What Crosses, and What Happens When Something Fails

Only three kinds of thing cross between the tiers: confirmed objects, residuals and drafts. Telemetry
crosses the OT boundary once, through a hardware data diode carrying the lidi file service, and never
crosses back; the diode is physically one-way where a firewall would be policy one-way, and any change
to the boundary passes management of change with the control engineer's signature. Report packs for
the insurer's engineer are generated inside the boundary, checked against a disclosure checklist and
released only through the controlled export path.

Each failure has a defined behavior. If the link between the tiers drops, the backbone's store and forward
buffers the confirmed objects while the site tier keeps forecasting and retrieving, the command center
degrades to its last complete model state, and the standing written procedure stays warm; the plant runs

as it does today. If power takes the site server, the historian's own record remains the authority and the
site tier resynchronizes from the backbone on return. If the update path stalls, the running versions
continue: artifacts arrive through the air-gapped Harbor registry on the controlled import path, and the
registry's versions are the rollback, so a stalled update is an inconvenience rather than an outage.

8.1 The Command Center Model

Figure 7 shows the model stack: one frontier model on the in-country node, two small models on the site
server, and the licenses beneath all three. GLM 5.3 is the command center model, the one the operator's
own requirement names. Its filed count is 753 billion parameters, frontier class at or above the 300 billion
threshold, published at about 756 GB of weights at FP8 and roughly 1.5 TB at BF16; the design runs it at
FP8 on one node of the 141 GB class, as Chapter 7 sized. Its role is the agentic work surface: the restart,
cycle damage and turnaround drafting agents and the conversational interface that answers with
citations. Its license is the GLM-5.3 bespoke license, whose terms allow commercial use, fine tuning and
redistribution, and whose MaaS trigger does not bind an operator using the model internally. It was

chosen because it is the one model in the register whose filed parameter count is frontier class, and
because the requirement asks for a command center whose agent drafts and cited answers run on a
single model the operator holds.

8.2 The Site Models and Why Holding the Weights Matters

Chronos-2 forecasts. It is about 0.48 GB at 32 bit as published and about 0.24 GB at 16 bit, it performs
zero-shot multivariate forecasting with covariates, and it runs on the site server against the historian tag
mirror, where thresholded residuals give the cycle damage agent its cycling-stress signal. Its Apache-2.0
terms place no condition on internal use, and the plan fine tunes nothing, which fits the rule that
improvement never runs through weights. BGE-M3 retrieves. It is about 2.27 GB at float32, about 1.1 GB
at the FP16 the design runs and about 0.6 GB at 8 bit, and it produces dense, sparse and multi-vector
retrieval from one pass, which keeps tag numbers and error codes findable across the free-text records
engineers rebuild by hand today; its MIT terms sit at the permissive end of the register.

The licenses matter beyond permission, because they are the reason the intelligence can stay. A coronial
inquiry linked a worker's death to the loss of workplace information that followed changes in ownership
and management, and called that loss explainable but not excusable (Ohsalert 2025); at another
operation a labor union had to mine its own old newsletters to recover records of past accidents (OR
2021). An operator whose restart memory lives in file paths and retiring engineers stands in that position,
and an operator whose memory lives in weights and records held on its own ground does not.

9.2 What the Rollout Measures

The rollout measures against the operator's own four baselines, taken before the agents draft anything. It
measures tag delivery from the historian read path against the threshold the pilot gate pattern sets, and it
measures agreement between the shadowed restart drafts and the standing written procedure, since
agreement is what moves a draft from shadow toward confirmation. It also measures the restart object's

own recorded properties: gas restoration time, stable production time, suspension duration, trips count
and leaks observed, which together say whether a restart went better than the last one. The cycle
damage ranking is measured against the inspection findings it points to, because a ranking that survives
the next inspection is a ranking worth trusting.

9.4 Lessons

Shadow the drafts before anyone trusts them. The standing written procedure remains the sole restart
authority until agreement is measured, because a procedure nobody reads is no protection at all; an
inquest into a worker's death heard that none of the contractor's employees had read the safety manual
for the machine that killed him (Constructionnews 2009). Shadow mode keeps the draft beside the
procedure the crew actually uses, and the superintendent confirms every step of it.

Make the license determination a gate, not a procurement step. Export controls turn on total
processing performance rather than memory, so the determination precedes any card quoted; if it blocks
the class the frontier node was sized on, the fallback route is already held and the rest of the design is
unchanged.

Elicit the retiring memory before the ranking depends on it. The engineers who remember the last
restarts are leaving, and the cost of that kind of loss is documented: coronial review of fatalities in the
resources sector traces them to corporate memory loss (Ausimm n.d.), a coroner called the loss of
workplace information after management change explainable but not excusable (Ohsalert 2025), and one
workforce had to mine its own old newsletters to recover records of past accidents (OR 2021). The
elicitation is an item with a gate, not a courtesy.

9.5 What Is Still Open

Four questions stay open, and each one changes something concrete when settled. The export license
determination for the GPU classes decides whether the frontier model runs on the operator's own node or
the fallback in-country route, which moves the work surface but not the agents. The application of the
operator's own cited legal instruments is routed to counsel, and settling it fixes what the disclosure
checklist for report packs must satisfy. The agreed opening balances of historic records decide how far
back the cycle damage ranking can reach, since the build reads live feeds and those balances only.
Whether continuous sensing is added on the critical tier decides the sensing plan's shape, because
condition collection is route based as the requirement describes it everywhere else.

PA R T I I I · C H A P T E R 1 0

The Intelligence Stays with the Plant That Produced It

The object model, the weights and their memory, the decision record and the boundary all
belong to the operator, so the intelligence compounds inside the organization whose cycled
equipment produced it rather than leaking out through a vendor, a cloud or a report pack.

Chapter 9 left four questions open, each of which moves a mechanism rather than the design's shape.
This chapter states who owns what the rollout builds, because a system that reads a cycled plant's own
records and improves its own restart plans is only worth building if the intelligence it accumulates stays
where the cycling happened.

10.1 What the Operator Owns

The operator owns the object model. Its fourteen objects are anchored in systems of record the operator
already holds: the equipment master in the maintenance management system, the tags and trips in the
distributed control system and its historian, the findings in the inspection and corrosion records. The

ontology is a governed projection of those records, so it is an asset of the plant it describes, and every
typed link in it was built for this operation's questions. The operator owns the weights. GLM 5.3 runs
under a license that permits commercial use, fine tuning and redistribution, and it runs on the operator's
own hardware inside the country; Chronos-2 carries the Apache-2.0 license and BGE-M3 the MIT license,
so every model in the register can be held, audited and re-served by the operator without a vendor's
permission. No fine tune is in scope, and any the operator later makes under these licenses is the
operator's. The operator owns the decision record: every confirmed restart plan, every accepted
inspection, every ranking a named superintendent acted on, held as a memory the next run reads before
it acts and one that never updates model weights. And the operator owns the boundary: the hardware
diode, the zones and conduits architecture and the controlled export path, with any change to them
passing management of change under the control engineer's signature.

10.2 The Offer Behind the Design

CodeNinja built this design on Praxis, and its parts map onto what CodeNinja offers where the design
contains the matching element. Adaptive Operations covers the sensing, detection and forecasting of
physical behavior: the historian tag mirror, the compressor vibration monitoring, the route-based corrosion
readings, the fixed cameras on the reformer top deck and the bagging plant lane, and the Chronos-2
residuals that turn thermal cycles into a stress signal. Decision Systems covers the rankings and drafts a
named person decides: the cycling stress ranking, the restart drafts the superintendent confirms step by
step, and the turnaround scope additions the planner accepts or rejects. Hyper Ontology is the object
model itself, the governed model of the cycled plant. Hyper Pragma is the work surface on which the
reliability team builds and runs its own agents against that model. Sovereign Infrastructure is the posture
the whole design rests on: the operator's own hardware, open-weight licenses and in-country operation
with nothing about the plant leaving the country. Praxis is the platform that produced the design, and the
design stands with industrial AI reference architectures that keep the intelligence, the weights and the
record of every decision inside the organization whose equipment produced them.

PA R T I V · C O N C L U S I O N

The Cycling Becomes Countable, and the Count Stays
Owned
In one view, the design is a one-way read of a cycled plant's own records into fourteen governed objects,
three drafting agents whose drafts are confirmed by named people, and a command center running on a
frontier model the operator holds on its own hardware in Pakistan; the diode makes the read physically
one-way, the ontology makes the cycling countable before the turnaround, and the memory loops make
the next restart plan better without touching a single weight.

Running the same shape elsewhere takes a plant whose systems of record are worth reading, a
boundary someone is accountable for defending, an export-control determination made before any GPU

class is quoted, and a named person willing to confirm each draft before it is trusted; the objects and the
agents change with the plant, but the diode, the governed model and the shadow gate travel unchanged.

PA R T I V · C H A P T E R 11

How Praxis Contextualized and Reasoned This Design

Every choice in this paper traces back to recorded reading on Praxis, and this chapter shows
the ask as it arrived, the eight lenses and what each contributed, the patterns adopted and
set aside, and the equipment classes the reasoning landed on.

Chapter 10 closed the argument on ownership, and everything it claimed about what the operator holds
traces back to recorded reading. Every design in this series is produced on Praxis, and this chapter lets a
reader trace any choice in the paper back to what justified it, from the ask as it arrived to the equipment
classes the reasoning landed on (Figure 9).

11.1 Contextualizing the Ask

The ask arrived as a requirement written in the operator's voice: an industrial AI reference architecture for
fertilizer plant reliability in Pakistan, for a fertilizer manufacturer running an ammonia and urea complex on
pipeline gas and imported regasified gas, cycled repeatedly by gas supply suspensions and restarted
from a procedure written for a plant that was not cycled. Praxis assigned it to the heavy industry and
construction family and to that industry's reliability problem. What Praxis read was recorded per lens: the
case study, tooling and recency, hardware and equipment, rules and regulations, approach and history
shelves, with every cited record read whole.

 Figure 9. From the ask to the design: the family and industry Praxis assigned, the eight lenses and what each cited, the
                        patterns adopted and set aside, and the equipment the design lands on.

11.2 The Eight Lenses

Table 6 states what each lens could see, how many records it cited, and what it contributed to the design.
Two lenses returned nothing this run and are shown as gaps rather than papered over, because a gap
that is named is a question the operator can put to counsel or to a later run.

11.3 Patterns Adopted and Set Aside

Three patterns were adopted. The hardware data diode with one-way file transfer was adopted instead of
a firewalled read-only database connection into the OT zone, because the ask says the architecture never
writes to the control system and a diode is physically one-way where a firewall is only policy one-way. A
memory loop of confirmed restart causes and accepted inspections was adopted instead of fine tuning
the frontier model on restart histories, because the ask requires the next restart plan to improve without
training a model on the fly. The shared-objects pattern was adopted for the compressor's history, so one
story joins tags, work orders, vibration and inspections across the links. Three duties were set aside with

reasons: object tracking and trajectory forecasting, because the cameras watch fixed process equipment
rather than moving objects; labelling and retraining, because nothing is trained or distilled into weights
and improvement runs through memory; and people and vehicle positioning, because the design senses
process and condition data, not people.

11.4 Where the Reasoning Lands

The reasoning lands on named equipment classes rather than named products where the choice belongs
to the operator's estate: the 141 GB HBM GPU class, one node of eight GPUs holding the FP8 weights
with the KV cache ceiling beside them; the hardware data diode carrying the one-way file service across
the OT boundary; the GNSS time card grandmaster with holdover oscillator for time synchronisation; and
the rated edge compute class, specified for the plant environment if a camera-group edge unit is ever
needed, with phase one running vision on the site server instead. Every figure in this chapter, from the
shelf reads to the node sizing, was recorded reading on Praxis, and nothing in it is inferred.

title: Physical AI System Design for a Mobile Robot Fulfilment Centre in Saudi Arabia
text:
V E R T I C A L - D R I V E N A R C H I T E C T U R E S · WA R E H O U S I N G & I N T R A L O G I S T I C S · D E S I G N E D W I T H P R A X I S ·
NOVEMBER 2026

Physical AI System Design for a Mobile
Robot Fulfilment Centre in Saudi Arabia
Robot Field Watch: Physical AI for Warehouse Robot Safety at Every Gate, Pick Front and
Charging Bay. A sovereign physical AI system that detects people inside the robot field, fallen
totes and blocked lanes on the cameras a robotic fulfilment center in Saudi Arabia already
runs, and drafts the zone slowdowns, clearance tasks and handovers that supervisors
approve.

Muhammad Umar, Cofounder, CodeNinja

For fulfilment center operations directors, shift supervisors and safety leads, and the platform, data and vision
engineers who would build and run it.

Vertical-Driven Architectures is a CodeNinja series of system designs. Every design in the series is driven by a real-
world problem and scenario in a single industry, and every one is designed on Praxis, CodeNinja's platform for
designing physical AI systems. Operations are described by class, never by name.

ABSTRACT

A Near Miss Should Surface in Seconds, Not in Days
A physical AI system design for a warehousing and intralogistics operator in Saudi Arabia that runs a
robotic e-commerce fulfilment center of roughly 400,000 square feet with more than 250 autonomous
mobile robots and needs one question answered continuously: who and what is inside the robot field right
now, and what is that doing to throughput and safety. The operator's own framing of the ask is physical AI
for warehouse robot safety, and today that question cannot be answered because the answer is scattered
across six systems of record that were never built to join: the robot fleet orchestration system holds stall
codes but not causes, the warehouse management system holds waves but not field state, and the
incident and near miss log records people entering the field days after the event, if at all. Throughput
drops are seen an hour later in orders per hour rather than in the field where they start, and supervisors
rebuild every incident by scrubbing camera recordings by hand.

The design joins those six sources, the warehouse management system, the robot fleet orchestration
system, the warehouse control system, the labour management system, the incident and near miss log
and the building's camera recorders, through one adapter family of read-only integration adapters into a
governed object model of fifteen objects, served by ten services and six surfaces, with five models: RF-
DETR small detectors run on the edge units of the CodeNinja on device AI stack, industrial SoCs
watching the existing cameras, Grounding DINO and BGE-M3 run on the site servers beside the ontology,
motion-only trackers run at the edge, and GLM 5.3 is self hosted in the site data room on one node of
eight 141 GB-class GPUs that holds its 753 billion FP8 parameters with KV cache headroom. Every
frame, detection, weight and memory record stays inside the building, and named incursion, stall and shift
agents draft zone slowdowns, clearance tasks and handovers that supervisors and the fleet controller
approve and execute manually.

The paper covers the problem and the join failure, the constraints and the stack, the object model,
ingestion, inference placement, and the models with their licenses, then the rollout in three phases from
one zone for one quarter to the whole field and the next site, ownership of what the system produces, and
finally how Praxis contextualized and reasoned the design, so that every choice can be traced to what
justified it.

  Figure 1. Robot Field Watch on one page: the sources the operation already runs, one object model, what it computes,
                                             and the person who decides.

Contents

Each chapter is tagged for the reader it serves most directly: Executive, Team Lead, FDE, Reference.

  PA R T I · T H E P R O B L E M

         Autonomous

 11      How Praxis Contextualized and Reasoned This Design                        Team Lead     FDE

         Sources                                                                   Reference

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 1

Physical AI for Warehouse Robot Safety Starts in the
Field

The operator's safety and throughput losses both begin inside the robot field, but every
system that could see them records only a slice, and always too late.

The abstract promised a physical AI system design that opens the robot field to the people who run it, and
this chapter states the problem that design must solve. Physical AI for warehouse robot safety is the
operator's own requirement, in the operator's own words, and it exists because the place where people
and robots share a building is exactly the place the operation cannot see. The losses, human and
financial, both start there.

1.1 The Question and the Regimes It Must Satisfy

The operation needs two questions answered at the moment they arise, not an hour or a week later: who
is inside the robot field right now, where, how often and why; and why has throughput dropped, in the field
where it starts rather than in the orders per hour figure that surfaces an hour later. Answering them
requires data the operator already holds but never joins: per-robot state, position, battery and fault codes
from the fleet system; order and wave progress from the warehouse management system; role and shift
context from the labour system; camera coverage of the field gates, pick station fronts, charging bays and
dock crossings; and the incident record against which any live detection must be reconciled. Three
regimes frame the work. The kingdom's Personal Data Protection Law makes an impact assessment
mandatory for constant monitoring and dataset linking, which rules out identifying individuals and pushes
the design toward anonymous presence with role context. Civil Defense licensing governs the building
and anything added near the field. The ISO 3691-4 standard for automated industrial trucks defines the
zone classes the robot field is divided into, and national cybersecurity and communications controls
govern what may be connected and how.

1.2 The Documented Cost of Learning Late

The cost of this blindness is documented in the industry's own enforcement record. A United Kingdom
manufacturer was fined £500,000 after a worker was killed when the forklift truck he was driving
overturned, a case in which the underlying machinery risk was ordinary and the failure was in its
management (HSE 2023). Warehouse fatalities from struck-by events remain a recurring pattern in
federal investigations, including a worker killed by material falling from a pallet (DOI 2022) and an
operator crushed by a shifting load (CDC 2020). The safety profession's own guidance treats
investigation as a structured discipline that must be performed deliberately after an incident (HSE n.d.),
with root cause analysis for logistics incidents set out as a formal method (CEFIC 2015); an operation that
learns of near misses days late, if at all, cannot run that discipline on time, and its supervisors rebuild
each incident by scrubbing recordings by hand.

1.3 The Operation as a Scenario

The operator is a warehousing and intralogistics operator in Saudi Arabia, running a robotic fulfilment
center opened in 2026. The building covers roughly 400,000 square feet and runs more than 250
autonomous mobile robots for goods to person picking and order sorting, with robot shuttles feeding the
pick stations; sites of this class are designed to process over three million orders a month at peak, and
peak season doubles the fleet's workload. People and robots share the building: pickers at the stations,

replenishment teams in the robot field during maintenance windows, technicians at the charging bays,
dock crews where inbound pallets meet the sortation output, and shift supervisors above all of them, the
newest of whom have never run a peak. The physical environments are the robot field with its lanes, the
pick station fronts, the charging bays where fire load concentrates, and the dock crossings. The operation
holds six named systems of record: the warehouse management system, the robot fleet orchestration
system supplied with the robots, the warehouse control system for conveyors and sorters, the labour
management system, the incident and near miss log, and the building's camera recorders. One site, one
robot field and one data room define the places; the roles in the loop are the pickers, replenishment
teams, technicians, dock crews and supervisors named above.

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 2

Every System Sees One Slice of the Floor

Six systems of record each hold a true but partial picture of the same building, and the
question that matters lives only in their join.

Chapter 1 set out the question. This chapter explains why no system the operation already runs can
answer it.

2.1 What Each System Sees

Warehouse management system owns orders, waves, totes and locations; the ontology's order wave to
stall story is impossible without it, and entity resolution starts from its identifiers.

Robot fleet orchestration system the black box the operator wants opened: robot state, stall and fault
codes and charging queues all live here, and no command path is ever opened into it.

Warehouse control system conveyor and sorter jams and faults are half of the blockage picture between
the robot field and the dock.

Labour management system supplies the role and shift context that turns an anonymous presence into 'a
replenishment team member outside a maintenance window' without identifying the individual.

Incident and near miss log the record the operator learns from days late today; reconciling it against live
detections measures the reporting gap and seeds the memory with confirmed causes.

The building's camera recorders the existing estate carries every detection point; reuse is the design, and
only detections and evidence frames are kept from it.

      Figure 2. Six systems, each seeing one part of the answer. The question needs all of them in one place at once.

2.2 What None of Them See Together

Each holds one slice, and the question needs all of them in one place at once, which today is done by
hand at the cadence of whoever has the time.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 3

Sovereignty and Privacy Shape Every Downstream
Choice

Four constraints, national data protection law, nothing leaving the building, no write path into
the fleet, and every decision owned by a named person, decide the stack before any
component is chosen.

Chapter 2 showed that the answer lives in the join of six systems, not in any one of them. Before any
component is chosen, four constraints decide what that join may look like: national data protection law,
nothing leaving the building, no write path into the fleet, and every decision owned by a named person.
They shape every downstream choice in this design.

3.1 Privacy Is Settled by Law Before It Is Settled by Design

The kingdom's Personal Data Protection Law makes an impact assessment mandatory for exactly what
this system does: dataset linking, constant monitoring, new technology and automated processing
together trigger Article 25, and its absence blocks go live. The design therefore detects anonymous
presence and infers role from pseudonymised badge and shift data, never identity; there is no face
recognition and no person re-identification across cameras, the tracking runs motion-only with the re-
identification branch switched off, and frames, detections and the incident memory stay on site. This is
hard in intralogistics because the temptation runs the other way: identifying the individual would make
enforcement easier, and wearable or tag-based positioning of people would add personal data the
minimization case does not need.

3.2 Nothing Leaves the Building

Frames, detections, weights and the memory the system accumulates all stay inside one perimeter, on
the operator's own hardware in the site data room. The one boundary crossing is the read-only conduit
from the fleet and control systems through a firewalled DMZ, which is a firewall, not a one-way diode. This
is hard because the reasoning tier wants frontier-class compute: the self-hosted model runs on one node
of the 141 GB HBM class in the data room, and export controls on that accelerator class may require a
license before order, with an in-country sovereign data center as the fallback placement rather than a
cloud endpoint outside the operator's control.

3.3 No Write Path Is Ever Opened Into the Fleet

The fleet's own sensors stop robots when they detect a person, and its safety case depends on that. This
design never drives a robot, never issues a motion command, and treats its camera analytics as an
operational feedback loop, never a safety-rated stop; integration with all six systems of record is read-
only. This is hard because the visible value of a write path is real: a slowdown applied automatically would
recover throughput faster than one a supervisor must approve by hand. The design declines it, because a
system that could move robots would have to be certified as a safety function, and nothing in this design
is.

3.4 Every Decision Is Owned by a Named Person

Agents draft; supervisors and the fleet controller approve and execute manually. Each draft carries its
own evidence and citations, each approval is logged with reasoning, and known-answer probes on the
review queue measure whether approvers are rubber-stamping, because an approval that always
confirms the model is not a decision. This is hard on a warehouse floor at peak, when the review queue is
longest and the newest supervisors have never run one.

3.5 Scoping Decisions

Three scoping decisions carry most of the shape: reusing the existing camera estate, proving the system
on one zone for a quarter before earning the field, and self-hosting the reasoning tier on site. Table 1

states what each buys and what it costs.

3.6 What the Design Chose Against

Each rejected alternative below was rejected for a reason the constraints state, not for convenience. The

                   labels

                   identification branch switched off    anonymous-presence posture rules out

                   executed manually by named            would cross into the fleet's safety case
                   supervisors

    WHERE                W H AT WA S P I C K E D    I N S T E A D O F, A N D W H Y

    Scope                Operational feedback and   Robot motion control and safety functions, order release and
    boundary             decision support only      wave orchestration, and individual identification, all out of
                                                    scope because the fleet's safety case and the PDPL posture
                                                    depend on their exclusion

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 4

One Stack Runs From the Cameras to the Command
Center

A layered architecture of sources, adapters, one object model, services and surfaces fits this
site because it opens the fleet black box without opening a command path into it.

Chapter 3 fixed the constraints that shape everything downstream: intelligence stays inside the building,
people on the floor stay anonymous, the existing camera estate is reused, and no command path is ever
opened into the fleet. This chapter sets out the architecture that satisfies all four at once, by separating
what the design reads from what it can ever touch.

4.1 The Pattern and Why It Fits

The architecture is three tiers with one spine. Below sit the systems of record, all six of them: the
warehouse management system, the robot fleet orchestration system, the warehouse control system, the
labour management system, the incident and near miss log and the building's camera recorders. In the
middle sits one governed object model, fifteen objects joined by typed links that carry the site's own
vocabulary, such as the link from a robot to the tote it carries. Above sit ten services, six surfaces, and the
three named agents, for incursions, stalls and shift handovers, that draft actions for a supervisor to
approve.

The pattern fits this site because it opens the fleet black box without opening a command path into it. The
robot fleet orchestration system is a source at the bottom of the stack, never a destination; the design
reads robot state, stall codes and charging queues, and nothing above the adapter tier holds credentials
to write to it. The same separation delivers sovereignty, because every rung runs on site, from the NPUs
of the edge units reading the reused cameras to the single 141 GB-class node in the site data room
serving the reasoning model, so no frame, detection, weight or memory record crosses the building's
boundary. Figure 3 shows the layered stack with the count at each layer, and every arrow points upward:
sources feed adapters, adapters feed the object model, and only the services and surfaces above it
compose the argument.

              Figure 3. The layered stack: 6 sources, 1 adapter family, 15 objects, 10 services and 6 surfaces.

4.2 The Stack Stage by Stage

Table 3 walks the stack stage by stage, naming what each stage is responsible for and the components
that carry it. Two stages deserve comment. The sensing stage is the one stage that touches the physical

4.3 A Reusable Pattern

The reusable shape of this physical AI system design is this: read-only adapters carry an operation's
systems of record onto a replicated event backbone; one governed object model joins them; agents draft,
named people approve, and execution stays manual; and every tier of inference runs inside the operator's
perimeter. A team carrying a similar brief into a port terminal, a mine or a baggage hall would swap the
source list, the fifteen objects and the detection classes for their own, and resize the models to their
sensors, but should keep four things unchanged: the read-only direction, the single object model that
every service reads, the evidence frame attached to every detection, and the approval loop with logged
reasoning. The single-zone phase one gate belongs to the pattern too, because it is what lets an operator
stop cheaply if the sensing does not hold up on its own cameras.

Fifteen Objects Turn the Field Into One Argument

The object model gives every detection, robot, wave and shift a typed place in one governed
graph, so a query can walk from a person at a gate to the orders their presence delayed.

Chapter 4 placed one object model at the center of the stack and made it the one thing the services
above read. This chapter opens that model: what its fifteen objects are, how they are linked, and why the

links rather than the objects carry the argument.

5.1 The Fifteen Objects and Their Links

The fifteen objects fall into seven kinds. Of these, the zone is the one site object, anchored in the fleet
map with its boundary, its ISO 3691-4 zone class and its maintenance window schedule. Four assets
follow: the robot and the charging bay, both anchored in the fleet orchestration system; the pick station,
anchored in the warehouse management system; and the camera view, anchored in the building's
camera recorders. The tote is the one material object, anchored in the warehouse management system.
Four events carry the operational story: the order wave, anchored in the warehouse management system;
the shift, anchored in the labour management system; and the incursion and the stall, which are the
design's own, anchored in its detections. The person role, anchored in the labour management system,
holds a pseudonymised badge reference with authorized zones. Three records close the loop: the near
miss and the corrective action, anchored in the incident and near miss log, and the agent draft, the
design's own. The edge unit, the fifteenth object, is the system that watches the cameras.

The typed links are what a query walks. An incursion is evidenced by a camera view and sits inside a
zone; the robots in that zone suffer stalls; a stalled robot carries a tote that fulfils an order wave with a
carrier cutoff; the shift names the supervisor on duty and the person role whose badge explains the
presence; a near miss references the stall and triggers a corrective action with an owner and a
verification. A document store holding the same content returns documents that mention the gate; it
cannot walk that chain in typed hops, it cannot enforce that every delayed wave carries a stall with an
approved reroute, and it cannot answer which orders the person at a gate delayed without a join rebuilt by
hand each time. Figure 4 shows every object and its typed links, with the incursion as the focal object.

5.2 The Human Loop and the Hosting Posture

The human loop lives in one object: the agent draft, with its drafting agent, its approver role, its approval
state and its citations. The incursion, stall and shift agents draft zone slowdowns, clearance tasks and
handovers; a supervisor approves or rejects with logged reasoning, and execution is manual, by the fleet
controller or the floor team. The single write path into the object model runs through the adapter tier and
the approvals service, so no detection, no draft and no approval can enter any other way. The hosting
posture follows the same closed loop: the graph store and the reasoning node run in the site data room,
identity is served by the on-site Keycloak, and there are no external links, the sole boundary crossing
being the read-only conduit from the fleet and control zone through a firewalled DMZ. Person data stays a
pseudonymised badge reference with role and shift context, never a face, under the national personal
data protection law and its mandatory impact assessment. The near miss and corrective action objects
carry structured investigation and root cause discipline into a live record rather than a workbook exercise,
which is exactly the discipline the investigation literature prescribes (HSE n.d.; CEFIC 2015).

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 6

Every Source Enters Through an Adapter, Never Directly

One adapter family of read-only integration adapters carries all six sources onto a replicated
event backbone, guaranteeing that the design can read the operation but never write to it.

Chapter 5 described what the object model holds. This chapter describes how data gets into it, through
one adapter family onto one event backbone, with the guarantee the whole design stands on: the system
can read the operation but never write to it.

6.1 Six Sources, One Provenance Class

All six named sources carry the same provenance class, operator-held, and the same direction, read. The
warehouse management system owns orders, waves, totes and locations, and entity resolution starts
from its identifiers, so the order wave to stall story is impossible without it. The robot fleet orchestration
system is the black box the operator wants opened: robot state, stall and fault codes and charging
queues all live there, and no command path is ever opened into it. The warehouse control system
supplies the conveyor and sorter jams and faults that are half the blockage picture between the robot field
and the dock. The labour management system supplies the role and shift context that turns an
anonymous presence into a replenishment team member outside a maintenance window, without
identifying the individual. The incident and near miss log is the record the operator learns from days late;
reconciling it against live detections measures the reporting gap, and investigation guidance treats that
lag as evidence lost (HSE n.d.). The building's camera recorders carry every detection point, reuse is the
design, and only detections and evidence frames are kept from them. Figure 5 maps each named
system, its provenance class and its adapter path.

       Figure 5. The 6 named systems, the adapter path each one takes, and the object model they all map into.

6.2 What the Adapter Tier Guarantees

The read-only direction is guaranteed structurally rather than by policy: the adapters hold credentials for
read endpoints only, so no service above them can reach a write path even by mistake. One adapter
family means all six integrations share one behavior, one failure mode and one upgrade path, instead of
six bespoke connectors. Change data capture through Debezium reads the transactional systems'
change logs rather than polling them, which adds no query load to a system running a peak, and stream
ingest through MediaMTX and Frigate takes the camera substreams where they already exist. Every
message is stamped with its source, its timestamp and its adapter version, so provenance is a queryable
property of every object rather than a claim. Because the backbone retains messages, the object model

can be rebuilt from the log, and schema contracts are versioned so that an upgrade to a source system
degrades coverage rather than breaking the join.

6.3 The Event Backbone

The backbone is Apache Kafka 4.3.x in KRaft mode, running on the site servers. Ordering is per partition,
keyed by robot, zone and wave, so the sequence for each entity holds even when global order does not,
which is what lets a stall's start and clear times be trusted. Delivery is at least once, and the writes into
the object model are idempotent, keyed by message offset, so a replayed message cannot double-count
an incursion. The retained log is the buffer: when peak season doubles the fleet's workload and the
detection rate with it, consumers fall behind and catch up rather than drop, and the correlated worst hour
is what the segment was sized against. Replication runs inside the data room with no off-site mirror, since
nothing leaves the building. Time synchronisation through linuxptp and chrony, disciplined by a GNSS
PTP grandmaster, puts evidence frames, robot positions and badge extracts on one clock, which is what
makes the reporting-lag property of the near miss object measurable at all. Telemetry lands in InfluxDB 3
Core, model versions live in the on-site registry, and the observability stack watches the whole path.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 7

Edge Units Detect and the Data Room Reasons

Per-frame detection runs on NPU edge units beside the cameras, open-vocabulary
classification and embedding run on the site servers, and the frontier model runs on one self
hosted node, with a latency budget that keeps each tier inside its job.

Chapter 6 described how six source systems enter through one adapter family and land on the event
backbone. This chapter places the computing that consumes them, sizes each tier from the weights up,
states the latency budget that keeps every tier inside its job, and says what happens when the link, the
power or the update path fails.

7.1 Three Tiers, Each with Its Own Job

The edge tier is a camera-group unit built on an industrial-grade octa-core SoC with a 6 TOPS NPU rated
for -40 to 85 C, mounted beside the cameras it serves. It decodes the RTSP substreams of the reused
estate and runs RF-DETR (small) per frame for person detection, with the Roboflow trackers holding
identities across frames; the Apache-licensed checkpoints run about 61 to 68 MB at 16 bit, so the binding
constraint is NPU load rather than weight storage. The shelf's published load figures cover forklift
dashcam workloads on MIPI cameras rather than substream decode from an existing estate, so the
design settles its own load with a dev-board measurement on the real substreams at the analyzed frame
rate, and that measurement is the phase one gate before any unit is ordered at fleet scale.

The site tier runs on the site servers in the data room, on CPU: ingest, the backbone, the ontology, the
BGE-M3 embedder and Grounding DINO on selected evidence frames only, never per frame. Grounding
DINO's Swin-T checkpoint is about 345 MB at 16 bit, Swin-B about 467 MB and BGE-M3 about 1.1 GB at
FP16, all comfortable in server memory; the constraint here is CPU latency on the evidence path, which is
why the open-vocabulary classifier sees only frames the edge tier has already flagged, and no third
accelerated tier is bought.

The central tier is one self hosted node in the site data room holding GLM 5.3, and the arithmetic fixes its
size: 753 billion parameters at FP8, one byte per parameter, is 753 GB of weights; a factor of 1.2 for KV
cache and activations gives 904 GB the accelerators must hold; one node of eight accelerators at 141 GB
each provides 1,128 GB, which leaves roughly 280 GB of KV cache ceiling. Figure 6 shows the three
tiers, what runs on each, and what crosses between them.

         Figure 6. Where each tier runs, what runs there, and the narrow set of outputs that cross the boundary.

7.2 The Latency Budget

The budget is an ordering of loops rather than one number, because nothing in this design closes a
control loop: the fleet's own sensors stop robots when they detect a person, and these analytics are an
operational feedback loop, never a safety-rated stop. The shortest loop is awareness, so detection runs
per frame on the edge unit at the analyzed frame rate; a person inside the robot field must surface while it
still matters, and a round trip to the data room would make the answer stale on arrival. The middle loop is
confirmation: the evidence frame, the open-vocabulary classification and the ontology join may take the
time a supervisor needs to read a draft, since a named person decides. The longest loop is conversation,
bounded by a shift team's questions rather than any actuation deadline, and that ordering is what lets the
frontier tier be sized for reasoning quality instead of control latency.

7.3 The Boundary and the Failures

Only one thing crosses a network boundary: the read-only conduit from the fleet and control zone through
a firewalled DMZ, which is a firewall, not a diode, and if a future phase ever exports analytics off site a
one-way transfer layer is added then. Frames, detections, weights and memory never leave the building.

Each failure path has a named answer. When a recorder link fails, the edge unit moves from Healthy to
Degraded in its status vocabulary, Kafka buffers what the backbone misses, and the command center
shows the gap rather than a silent absence. When power fails, Network UPS Tools watches the units and
the servers, and each edge unit's evidence buffer rides the interruption it was sized for. When the update
path is in question, the air-gapped MLflow registry on site holds every model version, K3s orchestrates
the containers, and each edge unit records the models loaded and their versions, so an update is a
versioned change with a rollback rather than a reflash. Time is the silent dependency: linuxptp and
chrony, fed by a GNSS PTP grandmaster of the OCP Time Card class, hold camera frames, fleet
telemetry and control fault codes to one clock, because the join between an incursion and a stall is only
as good as its timestamps. The one placement risk is regulatory: the 141 GB-class accelerator falls inside
export controls for the operator's country position, so license determination is a phase one procurement
gate, with an in-country sovereign data center as the fallback placement for the reasoning tier.

8.1 Five Models and the Terms That Bind Them

Figure 7 sets the model stack out from the edge checkpoints to the frontier node: two Apache-2.0 vision
models and an Apache-2.0 tracker across the edge and site tiers, an MIT-licensed embedder beside the
ontology, and one frontier-class model under a bespoke license in the data room. Every term in the stack
permits the operator to keep the weights.

GLM 5.3 is a 753 billion total parameter mixture of experts model published at FP8: about 756 GB of
weights as published, roughly 1.5 TB at BF16, so it needs the eight-accelerator 141 GB-class node before
any KV cache. It runs in the site data room on the operator's own hardware, and the operator named it. It
carries the agentic work surface, ontology maintenance and the cited conversational command center,
and it is the one model in the register whose filed parameter count is frontier class. Its bespoke license
permits commercial use, fine tuning and redistribution with an attribution notice, and its MaaS trigger does
not reach a third-party logistics operation, so the operator can hold the weights it reasons on.

RF-DETR (small) is a pretrained COCO detector under Apache-2.0 across the small sizes, with
checkpoints of about 61 to 68 MB at 16 bit for the Nano through Large sizes and about 254 MB for 2XL. It
runs per frame on the edge units' NPUs for person detection, and it was chosen because a pretrained
detector needs no training for this operator, per Zone 1 of system of context; the dev-board measurement
on the real substreams gates phase one before any fleet-scale order.

Grounding DINO supplies open-vocabulary classification of fallen totes, replenishment cages and blocked
lanes on evidence frames, on the site servers. Its zero-shot, text-conditioned boxes find site objects from

a text prompt with no training and no site labels, which is the same Zone 1 constraint. Only the Apache-
2.0 Swin-T and Swin-B checkpoints are used, never the commercial API versions; Swin-T is about 345
MB at 16 bit and Swin-B about 467 MB.

BGE-M3 embeds the cited retrieval over the ontology, incident history and handovers, on CPU beside the
ontology. It is multilingual across Arabic and English, produces dense and sparse retrieval in one pass so
robot IDs and fault codes survive the embedding, carries an 8,192 token window, and is MIT licensed; at
about 2.27 GB at float32, about 1.1 GB at FP16 and about 0.6 GB at 8 bit, it is small enough that no third
inference tier is bought. The Roboflow trackers carry object tracking and trajectory forecasting at the edge
under Apache-2.0: motion-only tracking with the re-identification branch switched off keeps the incursion
record anonymous under the personal data protection posture, and the trackers eval command chooses
the association on the site's own labelled clip.

Three phases carry the work from read-only feeds and camera reuse gates through one zone

9.1 Phases, Workstreams and Gates

Three phases carry the sixteen items, and each phase ends at a gate that can stop the work cheaply.
Phase 0 carries four items across four workstreams, Floor sensing, Phase one evidence, Privacy and
safety approvals, and Read-only integration: the read-only feeds from the warehouse management
system, the robot fleet orchestration system and the warehouse control system; camera reuse verification
with its six gates per view, covering access, density and angle, time behavior, condition, worst-hour
environment and headroom; and the privacy and safety approval pack. Its exit gate is camera reuse
verification and detection gates passed with recorded evidence at the worst hour, and until it passes
nothing is ordered at fleet scale.

Phase 1 carries eleven items across six workstreams, Floor sensing, Building ontology, Agents and
approvals, Memory, Command center, and Peak readiness. Its items include robot field incursion
detection on the existing cameras, fallen tote and blocked lane detection, and stall signatures drawn from
fleet telemetry, and its exit gate is incursion detection proven live on one zone against the operator's own
baselines. Phase 2 carries a single item, the whole field and next site rollout, and it is earned by that
evidence rather than scheduled on a calendar. Requirement coverage closes at one requirement
covered, none partial and none open. Figure 8 sets the three phases, their item counts, their workstreams
and their gates side by side.

9.2 What the Rollout Measures

The rollout measures two families of numbers, one about detection and one about the floor. On detection,
it measures precision and recall of incursion, fallen tote and blocked lane detections on the live zone, and
it measures the reporting gap: how many detections have no matching entry in the incident and near miss
log, and how much time passes between a detection and its report. Reconciling detections against that
log both quantifies the gap and seeds the memory with confirmed causes, which is the same root cause
discipline the investigation workbooks and logistics incident guidelines teach (HSE n.d.; CEFIC 2015). On
the floor, it measures orders per hour on waves delayed by stalls, stall clear times, charging queue

lengths and the uphold rate on the review queue, the last measured with known-answer probes planted
among the drafts supervisors see. System health is watched throughout: NPU load, evidence buffer fill
and stream health per camera view.
