8.1 Three Open-Weight Models, Each Held Under Terms That Permit Ownership

Figure 7 shows the model stack: one frontier model, one site-tier model and one embedding model, all
open weights, all served inside the facility. The frontier model is GLM 5.3, a 753 billion parameter model
whose published footprint is about 756 GB of weights at FP8 and roughly 1.5 TB at BF16. Its role is the
agentic work surface and ontology maintenance: the command center's conversational interface with

citations, the triage and recovery drafting, and the governed model of the freight network. It runs on the
frontier node described in Chapter 7, and it was chosen because its bespoke license permits commercial
use, fine tuning and redistribution, which means the operator holds its own copy outright, on hardware it
owns, with no per-token obligation to anyone outside the estate.

The site-tier model is Qwen3.8 27B, dense, served at FP8 on the 48 GB PCIe card class. Its role is high-
volume thread and note parsing, the layer that turns years of emails and chat threads into structured
resolutions without spending frontier capacity on it. Its footprint runs about 56 GB at 16 bit, about 28 GB
at 8 bit and about 14 GB at 4 bit, weights only and excluding KV cache, and at FP8 the about 31 GB of
weights leave about 13 GB of KV ceiling on one card. It carries the Apache-2.0 license, whose terms let
the operator copy, serve and modify the weights commercially.

The embedding model is Qwen3-Embedding 0.6B, also Apache-2.0, whose role is embeddings over
threads, notes and resolutions so that retrieval can find the past exception that matches this week's. Its
weights occupy about 1.2 GB at BF16 and about 0.6 GB at 8 bit, with activation memory that grows with
the 32K window; it shares the site-tier server.

8.2 Improvement Runs on Memory, Not on the Weights

The requirement asks for a system that gets better every week from what coordinators confirm, without
training a model on the fly, and the license terms are what make that promise durable. Recursive self-
improvement is already an active priority at frontier AI companies and is spreading into the wider
corporate ecosystem (Stanford 2026), and its security implications are an open question in the literature
(Cloudsecurityalliance 2026). This design's answer is structural rather than probabilistic: no model's
weights are trained, fine tuned or distilled in either zone, and improvement runs on memory loops over
confirmed outcomes, each confirmation recorded against a named coordinator. The decision record the
next run reads is therefore auditable in a way silent weight drift never is, and because every license
named above permits the operator to hold, serve and keep its copies, the improving asset stays inside
the estate boundary. That is the property the whole design defends, and the property that a self-improving
AI system built this way exists to guarantee: the intelligence compounds where the data lives, under
governance the operator can inspect.

9.1 Phases, Workstreams and Gates

The rollout carries 18 items across 2 phases, and every phase ends at a gate rather than at a date.

9.2 What the Rollout Measures

The measures exist to make the gate honest. Time to resolve is measured from the moment an exception
is raised to the moment a coordinator confirms its resolution, and it is the figure shippers already hold the

desk to. Repeat exceptions per lane, carrier and consignee measure whether last week's fix is at hand
this week, which is the specific failure the operator named. Claims per thousand shipments, fed from the
claims system, track which unmanaged exceptions become money. Missed appointment windows and
declined change requests catch the case where an approved change is not consumed by the scheduling
tool and the delay simply relocates to the dock. The confirmation rate, read with known-answer probes
injected into the queue and a weekly sample of unflagged exceptions, tests whether coordinator
confirmations are genuine decisions or reflexes. Every measure is read against the recorded baseline,
because self-improvement that no one can audit is exactly the systemic risk the security literature warns
of (Cloudsecurityalliance 2026), and the practice is already spreading through the corporate ecosystem
ahead of the governance to check it (Stanford 2026).

9.4 Lessons

Shadow the drafts before anyone trusts them. The desk improves only if confirmations are decisions,
and the evidence on algorithmic management in logistics is that automation pressed onto workers without
a genuine decision left to them is associated with psychological distress and worse outcomes (Springer
2025). The probes, the preliminary framing and the weekly sample exist to keep the coordinator the
decision-maker in fact and not only in the process diagram.

Keep the manual way warm. The worst hour for the node to fail is the hour the desk needs it most, so
the thread, phone and note path is rehearsed rather than merely documented, and the rollback from
pinned on-site images has been exercised once under observation so that restart is a procedure and not
a hope.

Reconcile the entities before the network scales. A governed vocabulary built on one lane group,
where the entity count is small enough to check by hand, is cheaper than repairing wrong matches after
every lane group has inherited them.

9.5 What Is Still Open

Three questions remain open. The network scale figures come from public reporting on providers of this
class and must be confirmed against the operator's own shipment and carrier counts; settling them fixes
the node's concurrency headroom and the size of the pilot's baseline sample. The scheduling tool's
request surface must be verified to consume the approved change requests the write path sends; settling
it confirms whether the missed-window and declined-request alarms are a backstop or a primary control.
The scope of driver data use, already narrowed with counsel to the hours of service rules that bind
recovery options, awaits final confirmation; settling it fixes whether driver objects carry contact routes in
the pilot or only in the governed vocabulary. None of these questions blocks the phase 1 gate, and each
is priced into an item rather than left to the extension.

its product choices and its not-needed verdicts; the model register with footprints and licenses; the phase
and workstream plan of 18 items across two phases; and the register of six failure modes with their
mitigations.

11.2 The Eight Lenses

Each lens read the room from its own side, and Table 6 records what each could see, what it cited and

11.3 Patterns Adopted and Set Aside

Four patterns were adopted. Every source enters through the adapter tier, one integration adapter family
carrying change capture from the systems of record, so no system is read directly and none is modified.
The baseline comes before the flag: the pilot lane group's exception measures are recorded before any
coordinator sees a draft, so improvement is measured against evidence rather than impression.
Improvement runs on memory, not weights: every confirmed outcome compounds into the record the next
decision reads, which is the requirement's own phrasing honored exactly. The write path is single and
gated: the appointment change request is the one operational write, and it moves only on a named
coordinator's approval.

Four were set aside, each with its reason. Fine tuning and on the fly training were set aside because the
requirement rules them out and memory carries the improvement instead. Automated load re-tendering
was set aside because the systems-first constraint routes every carrier swap through a person, and any
later automation would be its own gated scope. The edge and video layers were set aside because the
trucks are seen through the tracking feeds the operator already owns and the exception desk is

knowledge work. Two-node serving on the 80 GB class was set aside because the arithmetic favors one
141 GB class node at FP8 over joined nodes carrying BF16 weights.

11.4 Where the Reasoning Lands

The reasoning lands on equipment classes, which is where a design of this shape becomes buildable.
The frontier inference cluster class, GPU nodes for 300B to 1T parameter open weight models, carries
the frontier work surface, one node of eight GPUs holding the FP8 weights with room for concurrent
coordinator sessions. The site inference server class carries the site tier, where the dense Qwen model
parses threads and notes under an air-cooled server the facility room already takes. The GLM 5.3 node
count by GPU class and the frontier model GPU footprint sizing rule turn any future model change into
arithmetic rather than a re-design. Every figure in this chapter, as in the paper, was recorded reading on
Praxis: the lenses, the citations, the patterns and the equipment classes were recorded as read and are
available on request, and nothing here is inferred beyond what the record holds.

title: A Self-Improving AI System for Canal Irrigation Water Allocation in Pakistan
text:
V E R T I C A L - D R I V E N A R C H I T E C T U R E S · A G R I C U LT U R E & E A R T H O B S E R VAT I O N · D E S I G N E D W I T H P R A X I S ·
NOVEMBER 2026

A Self-Improving AI System for Canal
Irrigation Water Allocation in Pakistan
Canal Share Ledger: Ontologies for Canal Water Allocation Across the Rotation

Muhammad Umar, Cofounder, CodeNinja

For the officer accountable for canal water allocation, the divisional and subdivisional engineers who set indents and
gates, and the data, ontology and platform engineers who would build and run it.

Vertical-Driven Architectures is a CodeNinja series of system designs. Every design in the series is driven by a real-
world problem and scenario in a single industry, and every one is designed on Praxis, CodeNinja's platform for
designing physical AI systems. Operations are described by class, never by name.

ABSTRACT

A Shortfall Should Surface Within the Rotation, Not After
the Complaint
A provincial irrigation department in Pakistan needs one question answered continuously, and the self-
improving AI system it asked for exists to answer it: did every distributary on the main canal receive its
entitlement share this rotation, and if not, where, why and what should be done about it. It cannot answer
the question today because the answer lives in pieces no system joins: telemetry measures what arrived
at the main heads within minutes, the indent and release ledgers state what was asked for and released,
the gauge reader diaries record what the field saw, and the complaint register is the first signal that a tail
has gone short, usually after the crop is lost. This is the problem ontologies for canal water allocation exist
to solve, and in the Indus basin it is politically sensitive, because inter provincial water is contested and
the same shortfalls recur every season at the same tails.

The design is a sovereign, self-improving allocation system for one main canal in its first season: eight
source systems, two adapter families, a governed ontology of sixteen objects with typed links, six
services, three surfaces and three drafting agents for shortfall, indent and dispute, each confirmed by a
named engineer. Telemetry enters through a historian read and every paper source through an OCR

pipeline with a human verification stage; together they feed one object model that is a projection over the
systems of record, never a replacement of them. Improvement runs through memory rather than training:
confirmed causes and accepted adjustments compound season over season, so the tails get their share
more often without any model being trained on the fly. Everything runs on the operator's own hardware
inside Pakistan, in the circle server room, with frontier-class open weights self-hosted for sovereignty; the
model register stands open, with no weights committed until a model is verified live, and nothing about
the canals leaves the country.

The paper covers the industry problem and the join failure across the existing systems, the constraints
and scoping decisions, the stack, the object model, ingestion, inference placement, the open model
register, the rollout in two phases carrying seventeen items with their gates and measurements, and
ownership of what the system builds. It closes with the chapter that shows how Praxis, the platform the
design was produced on, contextualized and reasoned it.

Figure 1. Canal Share Ledger on one page: the sources the operation already runs, one object model, what it computes,
                                            and the person who decides.

Contents

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 1

Ontologies for Canal Water Allocation Begin at the Tail

A distributary at the tail loses its share for weeks before any complaint arrives, because no
system joins what was indented, what was released and what the gauge reader wrote.

The abstract put the whole design on one page: a sovereign, self-improving AI system for water allocation
on one main canal in its first season. This chapter starts where the operator feels the problem, at the tail
of a distributary, and works back to the question no ledger can answer alone.

1.1 The Question, the Data and the Rules It Must Satisfy

The operation needs one question answered every rotation, for every distributary on the main: did it
receive its entitlement share, and if it did not, since when, and why. Answering it requires data that today
lives in seven separate places: telemetry readings of flow depth and velocity at the main heads, the
indent submitted ten days ahead, the release recorded against that indent, the rotation schedule that fixes
each outlet's share, the gauge reader's diary entry from the field, the complaint if one was ever filed, and
the revenue department's crop and area record that explains what the water was for. Four regimes govern
the answer. The interprovincial accord sets each province's share of river water, and the national authority
administers it. Canal and drainage law, with the department's own gate operating procedures, governs
how water may be moved and who may move it. National cybersecurity and data placement controls
decide where records may be held and who may read anything that touches a named farmer, which
constrains the system before a single pipeline is drawn.

1.2 What the Shortfall Costs

The cost is stated plainly in the operator's own words: a distributary at the tail receives less than its share
for weeks before a complaint arrives, and by then the crop is lost. Around that core loss sit three more.
When the national authority or a farmers' body disputes a figure, the answer is assembled from paper
ledgers by hand. The same shortfalls recur every season at the same tails, because no confirmed cause
survives from one season to the next. And the experience that sets gates lives with a few divisional
engineers who move posts every few years, so the department's judgment walks out of the building on a
transfer order. The pattern has a documented analogue in the earth observation literature: a peer
reviewed study of coordinated planning for heterogeneous observation resources found that satellites,
airships and unmanned aerial vehicles are usually managed by different operators, which complicates
any coordinated plan across them (DOI 2015). The operator's canals are the same failure one level down,
with ledgers, diaries and telemetry in place of aircraft.

1.3 The Operation as a Scenario

The operator is a provincial irrigation department in Pakistan, running a canal network that serves millions
of farmers. It takes its share of river water at barrages and head regulators and moves it through the
main, branches, distributaries and minors to outlets that farmers share by rotation. Telemetry was
installed on the mains after a national research program handed it over, and it now sends flow depth and
velocity readings every few minutes from the main heads and some interprovincial points. Seven named
systems of record hold the operation's memory: the telemetry system, the barrage and head regulator
gauge records, the indent and release ledgers, the rotation schedules per distributary, the gauge reader
diaries, the complaint register and the revenue crop records. Four roles sit in the loop: the divisional
engineers who set gates by hand on telephone instructions and move posts every few years, the gauge
readers who walk fixed routes with paper diaries, the national authority that sets the provincial share, and
the farmers' bodies that dispute figures when a season goes wrong. The physical environments run from
barrage decks and head regulators to canal banks, field routes and one circle server room where the
department's compute already sits. The regulatory ground is the interprovincial accord, canal and

drainage law, the department's gate procedures, and the national controls on data and cybersecurity, all
of which the design must satisfy rather than route around.

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 2

Every System Sees One Slice of the Canal

Telemetry, ledgers, diaries, complaints and crop records each hold one slice of the network,
and none of them alone can say whether a distributary received its entitlement.

Chapter 1 set out the question. This chapter explains why no system the operation already runs can
answer it.

2.1 What Each System Sees

Telemetry system flow depth and velocity readings at the main heads are the live sensing the shortfall
agent triggers on.

Barrage and head regulator gauge records paper gauge records beside telemetry form the baseline
comparison and the dispute account.

Indent and release ledgers the indent is the entitlement baseline every delivery is judged against.

Rotation schedules per distributary the rotation schedule defines each outlet's entitlement share.

Gauge reader diaries field gauge readings are the tail delivery evidence between telemetry points.

Complaint register complaints trigger the dispute agent and are a season success measure.

    Figure 2. Seven systems, each seeing one part of the answer. The question needs all of them in one place at once.

2.2 What None of Them See Together

Each holds one slice, and the question needs all of them in one place at once, which today is done by
hand at the cadence of whoever has the time.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 3

Sovereignty and Memory Shape Every Choice
Downstream

Open weights on the operator's own hardware in Pakistan, no gate actuation, no training on
the fly and no replacement of systems of record together fix the shape of everything the
design builds.

Chapter 2 showed that each system sees one slice and none can join them. This chapter states the goals
that fix the shape of everything the design builds, and the decisions and rejections those goals force.

3.1 Nothing About the Canals Leaves the Country

The operator requires open weight models on its own hardware in Pakistan, no third party model service,
and telemetry and ledger data that never leave its network. This is hard in this industry for three reasons.
Shortfall and dispute figures are politically sensitive in the Indus basin, where interprovincial water is
contested, so any egress path is a governance risk, not merely a technical one. National cybersecurity
and data placement controls constrain where farmer-linked records may sit and who may read them. And
the GPU class the frontier tier needs sits above the US advanced computing export threshold for
Pakistan, so an export license determination must precede any quotation of a GPU class, with an in-
country procurement route or colocation named as the fallback before any order is placed.

3.2 A Named Engineer Keeps the Hand on the Gate

No agent operates a gate. Agents draft gate settings and shortfall corrections, a named engineer confirms
or rejects them, and the gate itself remains a hand operation on telephone instructions under the
department's own procedures. This is hard because canal and drainage law and the department's
operating culture place accountability with a person at the structure, and because a wrongly drafted
setting that is acted on without confirmation would put the automation, not the engineer, in the
accountability chain. The design keeps actuation out of scope so that every physical action keeps its
existing owner.

3.3 Improvement Without Training on the Fly

The operator requires a system that gets better every rotation without a model being trained on the fly. All
improvement therefore runs through memory: confirmed causes and accepted adjustments accumulate
as reason-coded records that the next decision reads, and nothing updates weights. This is hard because
shortfall causes are contested and politically loaded, so only what a named engineer confirms at the
decision may compound, and confirmations must be captured then rather than reconstructed afterwards,
since the engineers move posts every few years and their unrecorded judgment leaves with them.

3.4 The Systems of Record Stay Untouched

The telemetry system and the paper ledgers remain the systems of record, and the ontology is a
projection over them, never a migration. This is hard because the paper ledgers are the legal record, so
the digitisation pipeline that reads them must carry a human verification stage on every batch with a 2
percent failure gate before any entry reaches the ontology, and because a wrong entitlement baseline in
the projection would corrupt every downstream comparison while the paper original stays silent about it.

3.5 Scoping Decisions

The goals above force scoping decisions, and each buys something at a cost. Table 1 records the three
that shape the build most: the single main for the first season, the sovereign hardware posture, and
memory in place of training.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 4

One Stack Runs From Paper Ledgers to Draft Settings

Systems of record stay untouched below, one governed object model joins them in the
middle, and drafting agents with human confirmation run above, all inside the operator's
boundary.

Chapter 3 fixed the constraints that shape everything downstream: telemetry and ledger data stay inside
the operator's network, the systems of record are never touched, no model trains on the fly, and a named
engineer confirms every draft. This chapter lays out the single stack that satisfies all four at once.

4.1 The Pattern and Why It Fits

Ontologies for canal water allocation carry weight because the argument they must hold already has a
physical shape: water moves from a barrage through a main canal to distributaries and outlets, while
entitlement is fixed by accords, indents and rotation schedules before anything is measured. The pattern
is three layers in a fixed order. Below sit the systems of record, eight sources from the telemetry system
to the revenue crop records, read in place, never replaced, never modified, never loaded. In the middle
sits one governed object model, a projection over those sources rather than a copy of them, holding
sixteen objects joined by typed links. Above run the applications and agents that draft gate settings,
indents and dispute accounts, and the three surfaces where engineers confirm or reject each draft. Figure
3 shows the layered stack with its counts: eight sources, two adapter families, sixteen objects, six
services, three surfaces.

The fit with this industry is a matter of fragmentation. Where different Earth observation resources are
managed by different operators, coordination is documented to suffer (DOI 2015), and an irrigation
department shows the same fragmentation in paper: gauge diaries, ledgers, registers and crop records sit
with different offices that never join them. Readers who have met a self-improving AI system built on this
pattern elsewhere will recognize the three-layer shape; what differs here is that the physical world is
modeled first, so a telemetry reading becomes a measured property of a head regulator rather than a
stream analyzed on its own. The middle layer is the load-bearing one: every question the operator cannot
answer today is a join failure, and the join happens there or nowhere.

              Figure 3. The layered stack: 8 sources, 2 adapter families, 16 objects, 6 services and 3 surfaces.

4.2 The Stack Stage by Stage

Table 3 walks the stack from source to surface, naming the component that carries each responsibility.
Two stages deserve comment. The inference stage runs embedding, OCR and forecasting models on a
48 GB PCIe class site server, while the frontier open-weight tier that will serve the work surface is open
work, sized when a verified model stands in the register, so no GPU count is stated for it. The services
stage carries the six services the operator runs, and the surfaces stage is where every draft stops for a

4.3 A Reusable Pattern

The reusable shape is the three-layer projection, and a team carrying a similar brief can keep it whole.
Keep the fixed order: systems of record below, untouched; one governed object model in the middle,
stated as a projection and never a migration; drafting agents and confirmation surfaces above. Keep the
single write path, by which only a named person's confirmation changes the model, and keep
improvement in memory rather than in weights, so nothing trains on the fly. Swap the vocabulary: canal
objects such as Barrage, Reach and Outlet become substations, wellheads or road links, whatever the
domain holds; swap the sources and the two adapter families to match them; swap the verification gate
and the forecast horizon to match the paper the domain runs on. What must not be swapped is the order
of the layers, because every other order ends in a copy of the record systems that drifts from them.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 5

Sixteen Objects Turn Canal Records Into One Argument

Sixteen objects and their typed links turn eight record systems into one entitlement versus
delivery argument that a query can walk from barrage to outlet.

Chapter 4 left the object model as the load-bearing middle layer of the stack. This chapter opens that
layer: sixteen objects, their typed links, the human loop that writes to them, and the posture that hosts
them.

5.1 Every Object and Its Typed Links

The model holds sixteen objects in five kinds. Five assets carry the hydraulic structure: Barrage, Head
Regulator, Reach, Gate and Outlet. Two sites locate the network: the main canal and its Distributaries.

Three events unfold in time: Rotation, Shortfall and Season. Four records are the paper trail: Indent,
Release, Complaint and Crop Area. Two measures are readings: Telemetry Reading and Gauge Reading.
Figure 4 draws every object and its typed links, with the Shortfall object in navy as the pivot of the
argument, and Table 8, printed by the platform, sets out each object with the source it is anchored in and
its typed links.

The links are typed, and that is the whole difference from a document store. A Barrage commands Head
Regulators; a Head Regulator reports Telemetry Readings and sets Gates; a Rotation entitles Outlets; a
Release instructs a Gate and is measured at a Head Regulator; a Shortfall is judged against an Indent; a
Complaint names a Distributary; Crop Area grounds an Indent's demand basis and belongs to a Season.
The reach of one query shows what this buys. Asked which outlets were short of share for two
consecutive rotations while the main's head met its indent, the model walks Complaint to Distributary to
Rotation to Outlet, then Shortfall to Indent and Release to Telemetry Reading, in one traversal with every
step carrying its provenance. A document store can hold the same fields, but it cannot walk the edges: it
would need one join per source, and it would still lack the typed relation that says this shortfall is judged
against that indent.

            Figure 4. The sixteen objects of the model and the typed links that let a query reach across them.

  Table 8 · The Object Model

5.2 The Human Loop and the Hosting Posture

The human loop lives at the three surfaces, and nowhere else. The shortfall surface puts a drafted cause
and correction in front of the controlling engineer, who confirms or rejects it before any gate instruction is
drafted. The indent surface carries the approval that must precede submission to the national authority.
The dispute surface shows an account drafted from cited records. Agents draft, people commit, and a
confirmation at a surface is the single write path into the object model.

The hosting posture follows the boundary the operator set. Everything runs on the operator's own
hardware inside Pakistan, identity is issued by Keycloak 26 on site, there are no external links and no
third-party model service, and telemetry and ledger data never leave the network. Improvement
compounds in memory, which holds confirmed causes and accepted adjustments that each run reads
before it acts; it never updates model weights, which is how the design improves every rotation without
training anything on the fly.

5.3 One Object in Its Recorded Form

The Barrage record below shows the identifier, label, kind, properties, status vocabulary and links the
platform prints for every object. The Shortfall object, where telemetry, ledgers and engineer judgment
meet, is recorded the same way: its properties run from measured versus indent to confirmed by, its
status vocabulary runs Open, Cause drafted, Cause confirmed, Corrected, and its links tie it to the Indent
it is judged against.

  "head-regulator", "label": "commands" } ] }

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 6

Every Source Enters Through an Adapter, Never Directly

Telemetry enters through a direct historian read and every paper source through an OCR
pipeline with human verification gates, so no system of record ever touches the object model
directly.

Chapter 5 described what the object model holds. This chapter describes how data reaches it: every
source enters through one of two adapter families, and no system of record ever touches the model
directly.

6.1 Every Named Source and Its Provenance

Eight sources feed the design, all operator held and all read-only, and they split cleanly into two paths.
The live path is the telemetry system, which measures flow depth and velocity at the main heads and
some inter provincial points and sends readings every few minutes. The paper path holds everything else:
the barrage and head regulator gauge records that baseline the telemetry, the indent and release ledgers
that fix entitlement, the rotation schedules per distributary that define each outlet's share, the gauge
reader diaries that carry the field evidence between telemetry points, the complaint register that triggers
the dispute agent, and the crop and area records from the revenue department that give indents their
demand basis. Figure 5 maps every named system, its provenance class and its adapter path. The
fragmentation is the ordinary condition of infrastructure records: where different operators manage
different observation resources, coordination is documented to suffer (DOI 2015), and the adapter tier
exists so the operator never has to coordinate by hand.

       Figure 5. The 8 named systems, the adapter path each one takes, and the object model they all map into.

6.2 What the Adapter Tier Guarantees

Two adapter families carry the load, and the guarantees are the same for both. The telemetry adapter
performs a direct historian read, polling the telemetry system's store without ever writing to it. The
integration adapter runs the OCR pipeline over the paper sources, and every batch passes a human
verification stage with a 2 percent failure gate before anything enters the object model, because a wrong
entitlement baseline would corrupt every downstream comparison. Handwritten Urdu and English entries
on the department's own forms make that gate non-negotiable.

Every item enters stamped with its provenance: source system, adapter, timestamp and verification state.
Reads are idempotent, so a replayed batch cannot double-count a reading or a ledger entry. One clock
disciplines the whole tier: telemetry timestamps, diary dates and ledger entries are reconciled to a single
time base before any entitlement versus delivery join is attempted, because a join across unsynchronized
clocks will not survive a dispute.

6.3 The Event Backbone

Apache Kafka 4.3.x, in KRaft mode with no separate coordination cluster, is the backbone. Ordering is
per partition keyed on station identity, so readings from one telemetry station arrive in order even when
stations interleave. Delivery is at least once with idempotent keys, which trades occasional duplicates,
removed by the keys, against any loss. Buffering is broker retention, so a slow consumer or a dropped
link holds readings rather than dropping them. Replication across brokers means one broker failing does
not stop the flow. TimescaleDB holds the telemetry as time series beside the backbone, Harbor holds the
artifacts and images the services run from, Keycloak 26 issues identity, and Prometheus 3.13 LTS with

Grafana 13.3 and Loki observes the whole tier, so a stalled adapter is seen on a dashboard before it is
felt at a distributary.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 7

All Inference Stays Inside the Circle Server Room

Every model the design will run, from OCR to the frontier work surface, runs on the operator's
own hardware inside Pakistan, and nothing about the canals crosses the network boundary.

Chapter 6 followed every source through the adapter tier and the event backbone into the object model.
This chapter follows the data the rest of the way: where the models that read it run, how fast they must
answer, and what the boundary around them does when the link, the power or the update path fails.

7.1 Two Servers in One Room

All inference in this design happens in one physical place, the circle server room, on hardware the
operator owns inside Pakistan. There is no edge tier: nothing is served at a canal head in phase one, and
the telemetry that reaches the department network is read centrally rather than reasoned on locally. The
room holds two machine classes. The first is a 48 GB PCIe class site server that carries the small model
tier: the embedding models that project ledger text and telemetry annotations into the retrieval space the
agents search, the OCR models that read the handwritten Urdu and English paper ledgers, and the
forecasting models that carry shortfall detection. The second is the frontier class node the work surface
runs on, one node of eight GPUs in the 141 GB HBM class.

The frontier footprint is unsized on this plan, because no model stands in the register, and Chapter 8
explains why. What the plan does hold is the arithmetic for the candidate the operator names, GLM 5.3 at
FP8: published FP8 weights of about 756 GB, which fit one 141 GB class node of eight GPUs, about
1,128 GB of aggregate memory, with about 280 GB left as the KV cache ceiling, the working memory that
grows with the length of the context the model reads. That arithmetic is a conditional shape, not a filed
footprint; it becomes one only when a verified model stands in the register, and until then no GPU count is
derived from it. The small model tier is sized the other way: it is chosen by class, a 48 GB PCIe server
beside the frontier node, because embedding, OCR and forecasting work is modest, continuous and must
survive independently of whatever the frontier layer becomes. Figure 6 shows both tiers, what runs on
each, and the boundary around them.

        Figure 6. Where each tier runs, what runs there, and the narrow set of outputs that cross the boundary.

7.2 The Latency Budget

The cadences this system serves are human, and the budget follows them. Telemetry arrives every few
minutes; indents are set ten days ahead; gates are adjusted by hand on telephone instructions; the failure
the design exists to catch is a three day head shortfall; and the season measure is whether about 85
percent of the tail outlets receive their rotation share. Each of those numbers sets a deadline no model
needs machine speed to meet.

Shortfall detection must land inside one telemetry cadence, so a developing head shortfall is visible on
the first of the three days it takes to breach. Indent drafts must be ready for approval ahead of the ten day
submission window, which means the crop stage basis from the revenue records and the current shortfall
picture must be joined with days to spare. OCR batches must clear their human verification stage, with its
2 percent failure gate, before the rotation they record closes, so that the entitlement versus delivery
comparison for that rotation rests on verified figures. Dispute accounts assemble from records already
inside the object model, so their budget is a working day of assembly and citation. Nothing in this design
asks a model to answer in milliseconds, and nothing would improve if it did.

7.3 The Boundary and Its Failures

The boundary is stated in one line: telemetry and ledger data never leave the network, the models are
open weights on hardware the operator owns, and no third party model service is called. There is no
egress to protect with a one way transfer, because there is no egress.

When the link fails and a telemetry feed drops, the system marks the gap and holds the last good state
for that reach rather than extrapolating through it. The gauge reader diaries stand as the delivery
evidence between telemetry points, exactly as they do today, and the coverage gap is stated plainly: only

the main heads and some inter provincial points are instrumented, so tail delivery is measured per
rotation through field readings, not continuously. When power fails in the server room, the live loop
pauses and canal operation continues as it does now, by hand under the department's own procedures,
because the ledgers remain the systems of record and the ontology is only a projection over them; on
return, the event backbone's buffering and replication resynchronize the stream. The gates are never
automated in any of these states, and that is a deliberate constraint rather than a limitation: a
documented failure path in physical systems is a mode change between manual and automated control
(CHIRP 2024), so actuation stays with people and the system only drafts.

When the update path is the failure, the air-gapped artifact registry is the control. Model and container
updates enter as staged, versioned artifacts in Harbor, are verified before promotion, and nothing reaches
the running system directly from outside the network. A failed or suspect update leaves the previous
version serving, which is the correct outcome for a system whose first duty is to keep the entitlement
versus delivery record defensible.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 8

No Weights Are Committed Until the Register Verifies

No open weight model was verified live for this run, so the frontier layer is named as a class
and sized only when a verified model stands in the register.

Chapter 7 placed every tier of inference in the circle server room and left the frontier footprint unsized.
This chapter explains why it was left that way: the register, and the discipline that no weights are
committed until it verifies them.

  Figure 7. The model stack holds no verified model yet: classes and roles stand where the names will go, with the work
                                                    each one does.

8.1 The Register Holds Classes, Not Weights

Figure 7 shows the model stack, and its frontier layer is drawn as a class rather than a named model,
because that is honestly what the plan holds. No open weight model was verified live on this run. The
register carries catalog entries instead: each entry was verified by a person on the date it carries, and
none was rechecked live for this build, so rechecking them is outstanding work before any weights are

committed. Writing a name into the frontier row before that work is done would be the one dishonest
move available here, and the design declines it.

The work surface is committed by class: frontier class open weights, self hosted for sovereignty, in the
Kimi class, running on the operator's own hardware in Pakistan. The operator names GLM 5.3, and the
plan holds that model's arithmetic: published FP8 weights of about 756 GB, fitting one node of eight
GPUs in the 141 GB HBM class with about 280 GB of KV cache headroom, chosen against GLM 5.3 at
BF16 on two nodes or a mid-size model. But that row does not stand on this run's shelf, so no parameter
count is filed under the work surface and no GPU count is derived from it. The arithmetic is the shape the
frontier tier will take when the register verifies a model; it is not a purchase order.

The small model tier is committed the same way, by role rather than name: embedding models for
retrieval, OCR models for the handwritten Urdu and English ledgers, and forecasting models for shortfall
detection, all on the 48 GB PCIe class site server. Every license question follows the same rule the
requirement sets: open weight terms that let the operator hold the weights, run them without a third party
service, and keep nothing about the canals outside the country. The exact terms attach to the register row
when it stands, because license terms belong to a named model at a named version, not to a class.

8.2 The Ground and the Sensing

The ground the models run on is the operator's own hardware in the circle server room, inside Pakistan,
against weighed alternatives of an in-country sovereign data center or colocation and a dedicated data
center. The sensing the models read is already in the field: flow depth and velocity telemetry at the main
heads, telemetry at some inter provincial points, route-based gauge reader readings, complaint register
entries, and the digitisation verification checks that gate OCR output into the ontology. Crop areas come
from the revenue department's records rather than imagery, which keeps the demand basis inside the
operator's own systems of record and avoids a coordination problem the literature documents:
heterogeneous Earth observation resources are usually managed by different operators, which
complicates coordinated use (DOI 2015).

One rule of the ground is external and must be stated: the 141 GB class GPU node sits above the US
advanced computing export threshold for Pakistan, so no GPU class may be quoted before a license
determination, and the plan runs that checkpoint first in phase one with an in-country procurement route
or colocation fallback named before any order.

8.3 The Model and Equipment Register

Table 4 gathers the choices this chapter has argued: each model class, the hardware classes and sizing
rules, the sensing, the pattern the design stands on, and the ground it runs on. Every row is a class or a
rule rather than a committed weight, which is the honest state of the plan, and each becomes a named
commitment only through the register's verification.

PA R T I I I · C H A P T E R 9

One Season on One Main Before Any Extension

Phase one proves the ontology, the digitisation and the three agents on one main canal for
one cropping season, and only its gate opens the extension to the other canals.

Chapter 8 closed the model register with its live checks still open and the export license question still
standing, and those two gaps shape everything in this chapter: the case for ontologies for canal water
allocation is not argued from the stack, it is proven on one main canal for one cropping season, and only
the gate at the end of that season opens the rest of the network. Figure 8 sets the two phases, their item
counts and their gates side by side.

9.1 Phases, Item Counts and Exit Gates

Phase one, the main canal prototype, carries 16 items across six workstreams: network ontology, ledger
digitisation, agents and memory, command center, season pilot and the sovereign infrastructure
workstream that stands up the in-country hardware. Its items include the governed canal network
ontology, the telemetry historian ingestion pipeline and the paper ledger OCR digitisation with its human
verification stage. The exit gate is the ontology itself: the model of barrage, main, distributary, reach, gate,
outlet, rotation, indent, release and shortfall must reconcile one real week of telemetry against the ledgers
before any agent is allowed to draft, so the ontology is proven on one main canal before any extension.
Phase two, network extension, carries a single item, the extension of the gates to the other canals, and it
opens only through that gate. The requirement register holds twenty requirements, each traced to an item
and a workstream, and Figure 8 shows that coverage against the phases. Extending to several canals
running together is an operations problem in its own right, and other regulated domains have reached for
explicit guidance before multiple simultaneous operations are run as one (Jarus-rpas 2023).

             Figure 8. The two phases and their gates, and coverage of the 20 requirements across them.

9.2 What the Rollout Measures

One measure governs the season: the percent of tail outlets receiving their rotation share, with a nominal
of 85 percent, breached when the figure falls below it and the fault defined as a three day head shortfall.
The tail outlets are the ones the rotation schedules entitle, the share is judged against the entitlement the
schedule states, and the head shortfall is measured at the main head telemetry against the indent for the
period. The complaint register is read as a second, season-level measure rather than a live signal,
because complaints arrive after the crop is lost.

9.3 Failure Modes

Table 5 states what fails and what the design does about it. One failure deserves prose: gate instructions
travel by telephone and are executed by hand, and investigations in other safety-critical work trace losses
to communication paths long before they trace them to decisions (BBC 2013), which is why every drafted
adjustment carries its controlling engineer by name.

  Table 5 · Failure Modes

   Pakistan                                        before any order

                                                   claimed

9.4 Lessons

Reconcile the baseline before claiming any improvement. A comparable irrigation automation
program found its computed efficiency fell once continuous measurement exposed manual under-
measurement, so the first month of phase one takes the manual and telemetry baselines together and
reconciles them in the open before the season measure means anything.

Capture the confirmation at the decision, not afterwards. The experience that sets gates belongs to a
few divisional engineers who move posts every few years, so every confirmed cause and accepted
adjustment is recorded at the moment the engineer decides, and the memory becomes the department's
rather than the individual's.

Keep every automated draft under a named human. No agent operates a gate, and the discipline is
wider than water: an unmanned aircraft that changed into an automated flight mode and had to be
wrestled back to manual is the pattern to avoid (CHIRP 2024), so drafts propose and named engineers
dispose, every time.

9.5 What Is Still Open

Four questions stay open past this design. First, no open weight model survived this run's live checks, so
the work surface weights and the GPU sizing that follows from them stand only when a verified model row
stands in the register. Second, the export license determination for the 141 GB class node must precede
any quotation, and settling it chooses between in-country procurement and colocation. Third, OCR
accuracy on the department's own handwritten forms is unmeasured, and settling it fixes the verification
effort per batch. Fourth, the water accord, the canal and drainage law and the gate procedures are named
by the operator but not held in the corpus, so they route to counsel; the crop records arrive from another
authority entirely, and coordination across separately managed resources is a documented complication
in Earth observation (DOI 2015).

PA R T I I I · C H A P T E R 1 0

The Intelligence Stays with the Canal Operator

The object model, the memory of confirmed causes and accepted adjustments, and the
hardware all belong to the operator, so the intelligence compounds inside the department
that produced it.

Chapter 9 left the season pilot holding the proof and four questions open. This chapter settles the quieter
question underneath all of them: when the season closes, who holds what the build produced.

10.1 What the Operator Holds

The operator holds the object model outright: sixteen objects and their typed links, built as a projection
over the telemetry system and the paper ledgers, never a migration and never a shadow copy, so the
systems of record stay untouched and the ontology stays the department's own. The operator holds the
weights: they are open weights running on hardware the department owns inside Pakistan, and because
the requirement fixes improvement without training a model on the fly, no fine-tune ever accrues, the
weights stay exactly as acquired and the license terms they carry permit the operator to hold them in
country. The operator holds the decision record: every confirmation, reason code and accepted
adjustment is a kept entry that the next decision reads, which is what makes the memory the retention
mechanism when engineers move posts. The operator holds the boundary: telemetry and ledger data
never leave the department's network, no third party model service is called, and nothing about the canals
crosses the country's edge.

10.2 The Offer Behind the Design

CodeNinja builds this shape, and the design maps directly onto its offer: Adaptive Operations covers the
telemetry reading and the forecasting and shortfall detection of physical behavior on the canal network;
Decision Systems covers the indent, shortfall and dispute drafts that a named engineer confirms or
rejects; Hyper Ontology is the governed object model that joins entitlement to delivery; Hyper Pragma is
the command center where the department's own people run the three drafting agents; Hyper Engram is
the kept record of decisions and outcomes that each later decision reads, and it does not update model
weights; Sovereign Infrastructure covers the own hardware, the open-weight licenses and the in-country
operation the boundary requires; and Praxis is the platform on which the whole design was produced.

PA R T I V · C O N C L U S I O N

Fair on Paper Becomes Measured in the Field
The design is one governed argument: eight systems of record that never touch each other are projected
into sixteen linked objects, so that an indent, a release, a telemetry reading, a gauge reader's line and a
complaint about the same distributary become one entitlement versus delivery story a query can walk end
to end. Around that model stand three drafting agents that propose, named engineers who confirm, and a
memory that keeps every confirmed cause and accepted adjustment, so the experience of divisional
engineers who move posts every few years stays with the canal rather than leaving with them. The first
season on one main canal is the proof, and its gate, the governed canal network ontology reconciled
against one real week of telemetry and ledgers, is cheap to stop at.

Running the same shape elsewhere takes the same four things it took here: systems of record that stay in
place below, an object model owned outright in the middle, a human confirmation loop that makes every
draft a decision by a named person, and a boundary that keeps the data and the weights inside the
operation. The objects change with the network, the agents change with the decisions, and the memory
changes with every season, but the shape holds wherever allocation is fair on paper and uneven in the
field.

PA R T I V · C H A P T E R 11

How Praxis Contextualized and Reasoned This Design

Every choice in this design traces to recorded reading, and this chapter shows the ask, the
records read, the eight lenses and the patterns that produced it.

Chapter 10 closed the argument with ownership. This chapter opens the record behind it: every design in
the series is produced on Praxis, and this chapter lets a reader trace any choice in the preceding pages
back to what justified it, shown in Figure 9.

11.1 Contextualizing the Ask

The ask arrived in the operator's own words: a self-improving AI system for canal irrigation water
allocation, owned by the operator, reading telemetry and ledgers, open weights on its own hardware in
the country, getting better at drafting gate settings and spotting shortfalls every rotation from what its
engineers confirm, without training a model on the fly and with nothing about its canals leaving the
country. Praxis assigned the design to the Physical AI family and the Agriculture and Earth Observation
industry, an assignment made by the engineer who led the project rather than a reasoned match, though
the brief was still read as reasoning input. What Praxis read: the case study, tooling and recency,
hardware and equipment, rules and regulations, approach and history shelves, and every record cited in
the lenses below was read end to end.

 Figure 9. From the ask to the design: the family and industry Praxis assigned, the eight lenses and what each cited, the
                        patterns adopted and set aside, and the equipment the design lands on.

11.2 The Eight Lenses

Table 6 states what each lens could see, how many records it cited and what it contributed to the design.
One lens returned nothing, and it is shown as a gap rather than papered over.

   fusion                                      sector's physical world first rule: the ontology carries the canal

11.3 Patterns Adopted and Set Aside

One pattern was adopted, system of context, and it was pinned as primary because the requirement
crosses silos no single system reconciles and the operator wants a governed ontology it owns outright.

The pattern fixes three layers in order, systems of record below that are never replaced or modified, the
operator-owned ontology above them as a projection whose crossing mappings answer the questions no
single silo can, and applications and agents on top; it carries one small grammar, nouns become objects,
facts become properties, relationships become typed links and actions change them; and it closes a
kinetic loop on the model, sense, decide, act, learn, with the return edge keeping the model living. No
pattern was set aside on this run.

11.4 Where the Reasoning Lands

The reasoning lands on three equipment classes: the 141 GB HBM GPU class, the frontier model GPU
footprint sizing rule under vLLM and SGLang serving, and the node count rule by GPU class that together
size the work surface once a model row stands. Everything shown in this chapter was recorded reading,
and nothing is inferred.

title: Physical AI System Design for Weld and Assembly Quality in a Vehicle Plant in Pakistan

V E R T I C A L - D R I V E N A R C H I T E C T U R E S · D I S C R E T E M A N U FA C T U R I N G & A U TO M O T I V E · D E S I G N E D W I T H P R A X I S
· NOVEMBER 2026

Physical AI System Design for Weld and
Assembly Quality in a Vehicle Plant in
Pakistan
Discrete Manufacturing & Automotive Watch: One Living Picture of the Operation

Muhammad Umar, Cofounder, CodeNinja

For the leaders accountable for discrete manufacturing & automotive operations, their supervisors, and the data and
platform engineers who would build and run it.

Vertical-Driven Architectures is a CodeNinja series of system designs. Every design in the series is driven by a real-
world problem and scenario in a single industry, and every one is designed on Praxis, CodeNinja's platform for
designing physical AI systems. Operations are described by class, never by name.

ABSTRACT

The Answer Already Exists in the Systems the Operation
Runs
A physical AI system design for weld and assembly quality in a vehicle plant in Pakistan starts from the
auditor's question: when the parent's auditors ask why a body shop defect rate rose on a given day, the
plant rebuilds the answer by hand across the robot logs, the torque records and the inspection sheets.

The design reads 6 source systems through 1 adapter family into one object model of 16 objects, runs 6
services over it and opens 5 surfaces to the people who decide, with 4 models placed where the data is.
This design puts triggered cameras and edge units on the CodeNinja on device AI stack at the body shop,
trim and underbody station exits, checks every body against the weld point list and the sealer bead with
Apache-2.0 detectors the operator owns, and lands every result in a governed plant ontology built from
the MES, controller logs, torque tools, end of line rigs, QMS and receiving records. Agents draft, people
decide, memory improves the next check without training, and the whole thing, including GLM 5.3 on one
141 GB-class node in the plant's own server room, stays inside the plant network in Pakistan.

The paper covers the operation and the problem its systems cannot answer, the constraints, the stack,
the object model, ingestion, inference placement, the models and their licenses, the rollout and its proof,
ownership, and finally how Praxis contextualized and reasoned the design.

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 1

A Daily Question Goes Unanswered in the Systems That
Hold the Data

The operation holds every fact the question needs and no system answers it.

The abstract promised a physical AI system design that checks every body as it passes the station exits
and keeps every byte of the reasoning inside the plant. This chapter starts where the operator's
requirement starts, with physical AI at the station named as the ask: the question the plant needs
answered every day, the data that question requires, the regimes that govern it, and the operation as it
actually runs.

1.1 The Question and the Data It Requires

The question is stated in the operator's own framing: why did the body shop defect rate rise on a given
day, and which supplier lot sits behind a defect pattern, answered while the shift is still running rather than
weeks later in warranty. Answering it needs six kinds of fact at once: the weld point list and weld currents
from the robot and weld controllers, the sealer bead outcome, the per-fastener torque readings, the
presence of clips, connectors and fasteners on the trim line, the genealogy that ties a body number to a
vehicle and a kit lot, and the lot identity that ties a defect cluster to a supplier. The answer must satisfy
three regimes together: the parent company's global quality standards, which the plant passes through
equipment validation, production trials and quality audits before commercial production; national data
protection rules that govern cameras in a workplace; and a localisation policy that obliges the plant to

track each part's localisation status and local value addition, the end to end supplier traceability the
International Automotive Federation frames as a requirement for its members' supply bases (IAF n.d.).

1.2 Defects Found Late Cost More Than Defects Caught at the Station

When a defect escapes the station, the cost jumps from a repair bay to a campaign. A US regulator's
recall chronology for incomplete software remedies shows a concern group reconstructing an event
history months after vehicles left the plant, the same hand-assembly of evidence across records that this
plant performs by hand today whenever auditors ask a question (NHTSA 2024). Supplier-side blindness
compounds the escape: a nonprofit study reports that many supplier factories of automobile brands
misrepresent facts about work accidents, calling it a lost opportunity for improvement, and a plant that
cannot trace a defect cluster to a lot cannot correct what it cannot see (Safeinindia 2024). The join itself is
becoming a regulatory subject, because meeting the first Digital Product Passport deadlines depends not
only on connecting data across systems but on proving how products were actually made (Qualitymag
2026).

1.3 The Operation as a Scenario

The operator is a vehicle assembly company in Pakistan starting production of new energy vehicles at a
new plant, sized for about 25,000 vehicles a year on one shift, assembling kits shipped from the parent
company with a rising share of locally made parts. Bodies pass through a body shop with robot and
manual spot welding and sealer application, then paint, then a trim and final line where harnesses,
interiors, battery packs and underbody parts are fitted and torqued, then end of line test and a final
inspection booth: four physical zones in all, of which the body shop, with weld fume, spatter and summer
heat, is the hardest environment for electronics. Six named systems of record hold the facts: the
manufacturing execution system, the robot and weld controller logs, the torque tool controllers, the end of
line test rigs, the quality management system and the supplier parts receiving records. Two named
decision roles sit in the loop, the body shop quality inspector who confirms or dismisses flags at the
station terminal and the quality manager who approves corrective actions, alongside plant engineers, the
parent's auditors and a supplier base whose parts arrive through receiving records. The team is new to
the parent's standards, and the experienced engineers who set up the line leave at handover, so the
system must carry their knowledge rather than depend on their presence.

PA R T I · C H A P T E R 2

Every System Sees One Slice of the Operation

Each system of record sees its own part of the answer and none sees the whole.

Chapter 1 stated the question, the regimes and the operation. This chapter shows why none of the six
systems of record can answer that question alone, by walking through what each one sees.

2.1 Each System Sees One Slice

The manufacturing execution system owns orders, body numbers, genealogy and routing, so it knows
which body is where and which vehicle it becomes, but it records nothing about the metal: no weld
condition, no bead, no torque. The robot and weld controller logs own the weld point truth, the nominal
positions and the weld currents, yet a controller reports what it commanded, not what the body shows,
and nothing downstream of the body shop. The torque tool controllers own per-fastener torque readings
with tool identity on the trim and final line, but not whether the clip or connector around that fastener is
seated. The end of line test rigs own the verdict each vehicle leaves with, but not which station caused a
failure. The quality management system owns defect records, repair tickets, corrective actions and audit
findings, but they are written by hand, without evidence frames and without joins to lots. The supplier
parts receiving records own lot identity, supplier and delivery date, but nothing about what happened to
each lot inside the build. Figure 2 sets the six systems side by side, each with its sees and its misses,
converging on the question none of them can answer alone.

    Figure 2. Six systems, each seeing one part of the answer. The question needs all of them in one place at once.

2.2 What None of Them See Together

The auditor's question, why the body shop defect rate rose on a given day, requires joining weld point
flags to body numbers to operations to supplier lots to confirmed defects in one argument, and today that
argument is rebuilt by hand across the robot logs, the torque records and the inspection sheets. The
same join failure delays the supplier trace: a defect pattern that points at one local lot surfaces weeks

later in warranty, because no system holds the path from a missing clip back to a delivery date. The US
national standards body's recommendations on manufacturing data note that trustworthiness depends on
traceable provenance across the data lifecycle, which is exactly the property that hand-built joins lack,
since each rebuild depends on whoever happens to be on shift (NIST n.d.). The cost in practice is paid
three times over: in repair bay minutes for defects found at end of line, in warranty exposure for defects
found by the vehicle's owner, and in engineering hours spent reconstructing answers the data already
holds.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 3

Four Constraints Shape Everything Downstream

The goals, the scoping decisions and the exclusions were fixed before any component was
chosen.

Chapter 2 showed the join failure that no single system of record can repair. This chapter fixes the four
goals that shape every component choice downstream, then the scoping decisions the design bought and
the alternatives it set aside.

3.1 Every Body Is Checked, Not Sampled

The first goal replaces sample inspection with a check on every body, triggered once at each station exit,
so a missing weld or an unseated clip is caught at the station rather than at end of line or in the field. It is
hard in this industry because the body shop is hostile to electronics: weld fume, spatter and summer heat
exceed the ambient ratings of the packaged smart camera class, and nuisance signatures such as dust,
oil and lighting change produce false flags that make inspectors switch a system off. The design answers
by hardening industrial-grade fanless edge units against the environment and by collecting and labelling
nuisance images before any threshold is set, holding false flags under 10 per inspector per shift.

3.2 Nothing Leaves the Plant Network

The second goal keeps every frame, every model and every inference inside the plant network in
Pakistan, on the operator's own hardware, with no third-party model service in the path. It is hard because
the conversational work surface the requirement names runs on a frontier class model of 753 billion
parameters at FP8 precision, where one byte per parameter means 753 GB of weights; the 1.2 planning
factor for KV cache and activations raises what the GPUs must hold to about 904 GB, which one node of
eight GPUs of the 141 GB class, 1,128 GB in total, carries in the plant's own server room. The same
constraint forces an export license determination for the accelerator class before it is quoted.

3.3 A Named Person Decides

The third goal holds every decision with a named person: agents draft defect records, repair tickets and
corrective actions, and only approved records are written to the quality management system, while no
agent ever stops a line or rejects a supplier lot. It is hard because the value of the system is drafting
speed, and the parent's audits demand named accountability at the same point, so the approval queue
and the confirmation surface at the station terminal must be fast enough that approval is cheaper than
working around it.

3.4 Improvement Never Touches the Weights

The fourth goal improves the next check through memory over confirmed outcomes, with no on the fly
training or fine tuning anywhere in the design. It is hard because defects are rare and varied, so the
temptation is always to retrain, yet changing weights under audit would invalidate the validation evidence
the parent's standards rest on; confirmed and dismissed flags become the record each later check reads.

3.5 Scoping Decisions and Their Costs

The scoping decisions in Table 1 were fixed before any component was chosen, and each buys
something at a stated cost. The object model is grown from the plant's own six systems of record rather
than adapted from published industrial ontology examples, because the join keys are the plant's own
body numbers and lot ids, and a borrowed model would have to be re-proven against them anyway.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 4

One Stack Runs From the Systems of Record to the
Surfaces

Systems of record below, one object model in the middle, services and surfaces above.

Chapter 3 fixed the constraints that shape everything downstream: data stays inside the plant network in
Pakistan, the systems of record remain authoritative and unreplaced, no agent stops a line or blocks a
supplier lot without a named approval, and improvement happens through memory over confirmed
outcomes rather than changes to weights. This chapter turns those constraints into a stack, the layered
shape a physical AI system design takes when checks must run at station speed and the argument must
assemble itself across six systems of record.

4.1 Three Tiers and One Join

The stack has three tiers. Below sit the six systems of record: the manufacturing execution system, the
robot and weld controller logs, the torque tool controllers, the end of line test rigs, the quality management
system and the supplier parts receiving records, each owning its domain and keeping it. In the middle sits
one object model, sixteen objects with typed links, that projects those records into a single argument a

person can query. Above it run six services and five surfaces, where agents draft findings and named
people confirm, approve and decide. Figure 3 shows the layered stack with the count at each layer.

The pattern fits because the plant's failure is a join failure, not a sensing failure. A camera at a trim station
can see a missing clip, but the question the quality manager actually asks crosses every system of record
at once: which supplier lot, which body numbers, which weld points, which corrective action. The design
therefore puts the join in one place, the object model, and refuses to let any application build its own
private copy. The ontology is a projection over the manufacturing execution system, never a replacement
for it, which is what keeps the parent's audits answerable from the records of record.

4.3 A Reusable Pattern

The reusable shape is this: triggered one capture per body checks at station exits, identity from the body
number rather than tracking, an adapter-only ingestion tier, one object model that holds the join, agents
that draft and named people who decide, and memory that improves the next check without touching
weights. A team carrying a similar brief would swap the detections for their own domain, weld spot and
sealer bead becoming whatever their stations must verify, swap the six sources for their own systems of
record, and re-size the three inference tiers for their own evidence volumes. What they should keep is the
invariant set: no source is read directly, no agent holds stop or rejection authority, and every improvement
lands as a recorded, citable decision rather than a silent change to a model.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 5

Sixteen Objects Turn Operational Data Into One
Argument

The object model is the join the systems never made.

Chapter 4 described the stack that runs from the systems of record to the surfaces. This chapter
describes what the middle layer holds: sixteen objects and the typed links between them, the join the
plant's systems never made.

5.1 Sixteen Objects and Their Links

Sixteen objects carry the whole argument. Vehicle, Body, Station and Operation come from the
manufacturing execution system, which owns orders, body numbers, genealogy and routing. Weld point
and Sealer bead come from the robot and weld controller logs; Torque result from the torque tool
controllers; Part and Supplier lot from the supplier parts receiving records; and Defect, Defect class,
Repair ticket, Audit finding and Corrective action from the quality management system. Two objects are
people: the body shop quality inspector, who confirms or dismisses what the cameras flag, and the quality
manager, who approves repairs and corrective actions. Figure 4 shows every object and its typed links,
with the defect object in focus.

The links are typed, which is what separates this governed plant model from the industrial ontology
examples a search usually returns: every object here is anchored in a named system of record and every
link is a stated relationship, not a co-occurrence. A defect links to the body it was found on; the body links
to its weld points and sealer beads; a part links to the supplier lot it arrived in; the supplier lot links to the
defects counted against it and onward to the corrective action opened on it. One query can walk from a
flagged weld point to the body, the operation, the shift's inspector, the lots fitted that day and the open
corrective actions, in a single traversal with lineage at every hop, where a document store would force a
manual rebuild across exports. That manual rebuild is what the plant does today when the parent's
auditors ask why a body shop defect rate rose on a given day. The platform prints Table 8 with this
chapter, listing each object, the system it is anchored in and its typed links; the recorded form of one
object follows in 5.3.

5.2 The Human Loop and the Hosting Posture

Every judgment in the model has a named owner. A flagged weld point or a missing clip is a Defect in the
state Flagged until the body shop quality inspector moves it to Confirmed or Dismissed at the station
terminal; a repair ticket exists in Draft until the quality manager approves it; a corrective action opens only
under the quality manager's authority. The single write path back into a system of record is the approved
record: agents draft into the ontology, and confirmed findings flow to the quality management system
through the adapter, never around it.

The hosting posture follows the boundary constraint. The ontology and its memory run on the operator's
own hardware in the plant server room in Pakistan, and nothing leaves the plant network. Identity is
Keycloak, on site. There are no external links in the running system: model artifacts arrive through the air-
gapped Harbor registry, and any transfer out of a network zone passes a one-way data diode. Data
residency, personal-data tagging and a recorded lawful basis per data class follow the draft national data
protection rules, which are a planning signal rather than settled law.

5.3 One Object in Its Recorded Form

The vehicle record below shows the shape of all sixteen: an identifier, a label, a kind, the system it is
anchored in, its properties and its status vocabulary. The defect is recorded the same way, with the body
number, the evidence frame, the person who confirmed it and a three state vocabulary (Flagged,
Confirmed, Dismissed) that keeps a machine flag and a human confirmed defect distinct.
