PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 6

Every Source Enters Through an Adapter, Never Directly

Nothing reaches the object model except through an adapter that owns its contract.

Chapter 5 described the sixteen objects the middle layer holds. This chapter describes how data reaches
them: every source enters through an adapter that owns its contract, and nothing reaches the object
model directly.

6.1 Six Sources, One Adapter Family

Six named source systems feed the model, and all six are the operator's own systems of record, read-
only, classed as operator provenance. The manufacturing execution system owns orders, body numbers,
genealogy and routing. The robot and weld controller logs own the weld point truth the weld check agent's
flags are checked against. The torque tool controllers own per-fastener torque readings on the trim and
final line. The end of line test rigs own the outcome the phase-one baseline is measured on. The quality
management system owns defect records, repair tickets and corrective actions. The supplier parts
receiving records own lot identity, supplier and delivery date, which is what turns a defect cluster into a
supplier lot trace, the end to end chain that supplier quality frameworks in the sector treat as the baseline
obligation (IAF n.d.). Figure 5 sets out the integration map: each named system, its provenance class and
its adapter path into the model.

       Figure 5. The 6 named systems, the adapter path each one takes, and the object model they all map into.

6.2 What the Adapter Tier Guarantees

One adapter family serves all six sources: the integration adapter. It guarantees a contract per source, so
a schema change upstream surfaces as a broken contract rather than silent bad data. It guarantees
identity resolution: controller, MES, QMS and receiving records are joined once, with lineage, inside the
ontology rather than separately in each application, and the reconciliation is proved against yesterday's
actual production before any agent runs on it. It guarantees read direction everywhere except the single
approved write path to the quality management system. And it guarantees time discipline, with every
event stamped from the PTP grandmaster so a camera frame, a torque reading and a weld log can be
placed on one timeline. Change data capture through Debezium reads the MES and QMS databases
without touching their transaction paths, and anything crossing a network zone passes the one-way
transfer, so the boundary between office and plant networks stays one-directional. Lineage at every hop is
also what national standards guidance asks of manufacturing data used for decisions: provenance,
timestamping and a record of what was joined (NIST n.d.).

6.3 The Event Backbone

Apache Kafka 4.4 carries events between the adapters, the ontology and the services. Ordering is keyed
by body number, so every record for one body arrives in sequence regardless of how the partitions are
laid out. Delivery is at least once with idempotent writes in the ontology, which tolerates a replayed event
without double-counting a defect. Buffering is on disk at the edge: if the link from a station unit to the
backbone drops, capture continues locally and resynchronizes when the link returns, so a network blip
never becomes a missed body. Replication runs inside the plant's Kafka cluster, so the loss of a broker
does not lose an event. Telemetry and time series land in TimescaleDB, and Prometheus, Grafana and
Loki watch the backbone itself, so capture completeness is an alert the command center sees rather than
a gap the quality manager discovers at audit time.

PA R T I I · C H A P T E R 7

Inference Belongs Where the Data Is

Each tier runs what its data and its link can carry.

Physical AI at the station only pays for itself when the model runs where the body is, at the pace the line
already keeps. Chapter 6 described how all six source systems enter through the integration adapter and
land in the plant ontology. This chapter fixes where each of the four models executes, which is a
performance decision, a data-residency decision and an export-control decision at once.

7.1 Three Tiers and the Memory Arithmetic

The design runs three inference tiers, and Figure 6 sets them side by side with what crosses between
them. The edge tier sits at the body shop, trim and underbody station exits: 5 MP global shutter GigE
Vision cameras with strobed lighting capture each body once, on a body-present trigger from the station
PLC, and a fanless industrial edge unit on an octa-core 6 TOPS NPU SoC rated -40 to 85 C runs the
check on the device. The D-FINE detectors run there at INT8, where the N variant is about 8 MB at 16 bit
and the X variant about 124 MB. The Anomalib models that watch sealer beads are model dependent,
typically tens to hundreds of MB at 32 bit, and PatchCore memory banks grow with the number of
reference images, so each station sizes its model on its own variant and its own reference set.

One air-cooled 48 GB PCIe inference-class server in the plant server room is the site tier. It serves BGE-
M3 at FP16, about 1.1 GB, and re-scores the borderline detections the edge tier flags, so a station-level
doubt becomes a full-precision second opinion without any frame leaving the plant. A US ECCN 3A090
license determination for Pakistan is required before this class is quoted, which is why the class carries its
own checkpoint in the rollout.

The central tier is GLM 5.3 on one node of eight 141 GB HBM GPUs, and the memory arithmetic decides
it. 753B parameters at FP8 is 1 byte per parameter, so 753 GB of weights, and the 1.2 planning factor for
KV cache and activations raises the requirement to 904 GB; one node of 8 x 141 GB holds 1,128 GB,
leaving 375 GB beside the weights against the 151 GB the factor reserves. At the roughly 756 GB the
published weights occupy, the KV cache ceiling is about 280 GB, which bounds concurrent sessions on
the conversational surface rather than forcing a second node. The printed architecture table (Layer,
Component, Choice, Why) carries the full stack card, and these three tiers are its inference rows.

7.2 A Latency Budget Set by Takt

The budget is set by takt time, the property the ontology carries on every station object. Each presence
check must finish inside the station's takt, so no body waits on a model and no inspector waits on a
queue. The edge tier meets this by construction, because the detector runs on the unit beside the camera
with no network round trip, and the published 2.12 to 12.89 ms single-image latency on a T4 leaves wide
margin at station pace. A seconds-scale budget governs the site tier, for re-scoring and for embedding
records into the retrieval index. The central tier works on a human-scale budget: conversational answers
with citations are read and judged by named people, so the cost of a longer answer is attention, not
throughput. Recall chronologies show how late a defect pattern is usually caught when the check is not at
the station (NHTSA 2024); that delay is what this budget exists to remove.

7.3 What Crosses the Boundary, and What Fails

Nothing leaves the plant network in Pakistan. Detections, evidence frames and ontology writes move from
the edge units across the plant backbone; model and container updates enter through the on-site Harbor
registry fed by a one-way Lidi transfer; no third-party model service is ever called. Every record carries
provenance back to its source system, the practice recommended for trustworthy manufacturing data
(NIST n.d.). When the link fails, the edge units keep capturing and checking against the last loaded
model, buffer locally, and resynchronize once the backbone returns. When power fails, the sealed fanless
units ride the wide-input 24 V buck from the plant supply, and the specified universal-input supplies restart
clean on the country's 230 V 50 Hz mains. When the update path fails, the one-way gate means an
interrupted update leaves the running detector in place while the registry holds the last complete artifact.
The number that decides whether any of this is trusted is the false-flag gate, held under 10 per inspector
per shift.

8.1 Four Models and Their Terms

GLM 5.3 is the agentic work surface and the ontology's maintainer: it drafts weld checks, traces supplier
lots and answers questions conversationally with citations. It is frontier class, 753B parameters as filed, at
or above the 300B threshold that defines the class, with about 756 GB of weights at FP8 as published
and roughly 1.5 TB at BF16, which means eight or more data center GPUs of the 140 GB class before
any KV cache. Its bespoke license permits commercial use, fine-tuning and redistribution, and that is
what lets the operator run it on its own node in its own server room; the operator names the model itself
and fixes it to its own hardware.

D-FINE is the station detector for weld spots, parts, clips, connectors and fasteners, on the unconditional
Apache-2.0 terms that cover code and weights alike. The N variant is about 8 MB at 16 bit and the X
variant about 124 MB, with 42.8 to 55.8 COCO AP at 2.12 to 12.89 ms on a single T4 at batch size 1, and
it runs INT8 on the edge NPU. The COCO checkpoints are chosen because they avoid the Objects365

terms that ship with other checkpoints, and site nuisance images are collected and labelled before any
threshold is set.

Anomalib, version 2.7.0, is the sealer bead watcher on the same Apache-2.0 terms with edge export.
Sealer gaps are rare and varied, so an unsupervised model fitted on the plant's own good beads beats
any defect catalog; its footprint is model dependent, typically tens to hundreds of MB at 32 bit, and
PatchCore memory banks grow with the reference set. The plant's own images replace the non
commercial benchmark data the library ships with, which is the license's practical edge.

BGE-M3 is the retrieval model, MIT licensed, served at FP16 on the 48 GB site server: about 2.27 GB at
FP32, about 1.1 GB at FP16 and about 0.6 GB at 8 bit, with an 8,192 token window and dense, sparse
and multi-vector retrieval in one pass, so part numbers and error codes stay retrievable and every
conversational answer can cite the record behind it.

Shadow Mode Comes Before Any Flag Is Trusted

The rollout earns each phase at a gate the operator can read.

Chapter 8 closed the model register with licenses that let the operator hold every weight it runs. This
chapter sets out how the build earns its place on the line: one gated phase, measured against the plant's
own production, with no flag trusted until it has run in shadow beside the people who would act on it.

9.1 One Phase, Fifteen Items, Six Workstreams

The rollout is a single phase, Phase One, carrying 15 items across six workstreams: edge inspection,
plant ontology, agents and approvals, command center, compliance and validation, and plant
infrastructure. The items run from the station camera and edge unit layout, through the weld and sealer
check pipeline, to trim and underbody presence checking, and the phase's exit gate carries that last item's
name: presence checking at the trim and underbody stations must run on every body and vehicle that
passes before the phase closes. The phase covers the operator's 18 requirements, and coverage against

each requirement is read at the gate, so a requirement that is only partly met holds the phase open.
Figure 8 shows the phase, its item count, its workstreams and its gate on one page.

Shadow mode governs the whole phase. Every check runs alongside the manual inspection it supports,
flags are drafted for a named inspector to confirm or dismiss, and no agent stops a line or rejects a
supplier lot, because that authority was scoped out in Chapter 3 and stays out.

                     Figure 8. The one phase and its gate, and coverage of the 18 requirements across it.

9.2 What the Rollout Measures

The phase measures itself on the plant's own numbers, not on laboratory ones. The end of line test rigs
give the baseline: the defect classes the phase must catch earlier, counted per body before any camera is
switched on. Against that baseline the phase tracks the false-flag count per inspector per shift, held under
10, because a budget above that is where inspectors stop trusting flags and switch the system off. It
tracks capture completeness, meaning every body that passes a station has a frame, a verdict and a
body number joined to its genealogy. It tracks the confirmation rate of flagged defects, the number of
defect clusters that resolve to a supplier lot, and the time it takes to answer the parent's auditors when
they ask why a body shop rate rose on a given day. Measurement data carries lineage and provenance
so it can be defended under audit, following the recommendations on traceability and trustworthiness of
manufacturing data published by the US national standards body (NIST n.d.).

9.4 Lessons

Shadow the flags before anyone trusts them. A flag that arrives unproven is a complaint, and
inspectors treat it as one. Running every check in shadow, with confirmation and dismissal recorded per
flag, turns the same hardware into evidence: the inspector who confirms ten flags and dismisses one has
taught the system what this plant's bodies look like, and the record of those decisions is what the next
check reads.

Collect the nuisance images before the thresholds are set. The case-study record is unambiguous on
this: false alarms from ordinary plant grime are what switch inspection systems off, and thresholds tuned
on clean images are tuned on a plant that does not exist. The nuisance set is a phase item with its own
gate, not a tuning chore left to the end.

Resolve the body number once, in the ontology. Every join in this design rides on the body number
and the MES genealogy, so a wrong resolution poisons weld truth, torque truth and defect records at
once. Proving the reconciliation against yesterday's actual production, before any agent reads it, is
cheaper than finding a wrong join inside an audit answer.

9.5 What Is Still Open

Four questions remain open, and settling each changes something specific. The US export license
determination for the frontier node and every accelerator class is the first: settling it fixes the server room

hardware as designed, or forces the fallback path to be chosen openly rather than by shrinking the model
in place. The plant network design is still being finalised, and settling it fixes where the IEC 62443 zone
boundaries and PTP-capable switch hops sit relative to the station exits. The scale figures behind the
layout come from public reporting on plants of this class in the country and are assumptions to confirm, so
settling them fixes the camera count and the per-station capture budget against the real takt. The parent's
validation calendar is the last: settling it fixes when auditors may rely on the station checks, and therefore
when the phase's evidence pack stops being preparation and becomes the answer.

The Intelligence Should Stay with the Operation That
Produced It

What the design builds belongs to the operator.

Chapter 9 showed the phase earning trust at a gate the operator can read. This chapter settles who holds
what the work produces once the gate is passed: the model of the plant, the weights, the record of
decisions, and the boundary they run inside.

10.1 What the Operator Owns

The object model is the operator's. Its 16 objects are anchored in the operator's own systems of record,
with the manufacturing execution system holding body numbers, genealogy and routing, and the ontology
standing as a projection over it rather than a replacement. Published industrial ontology examples seldom
anchor every object in a live system of record; this one does, and because the anchors are the operator's
systems, the operator can extend the model as new parts are localised without asking anyone's
permission. End to end traceability of this kind is what the International Automotive Federation's supplier
requirements frame expects members to align against (IAF n.d.).

The weights are the operator's. The detectors carry Apache-2.0 terms and the embedding model an MIT
license, both of which permit commercial use and modification outright, and the work surface model's
bespoke license permits commercial use, fine tuning and redistribution. Every fine-tune, and every model
hardened on the plant's own nuisance images, belongs to the operator and stays inside its boundary.

The decision record is the operator's. Every flag, confirmation, dismissal, approval and corrective action
carries a named person, and that record is what the next check reads before it acts: memory improves
the checks without any weight being trained, which was a scoping decision in Chapter 3 and holds here
as ownership. Nothing about the operator's quality judgement lives anywhere it cannot be exported,
audited or carried forward.

The boundary is the operator's. Everything runs inside the plant network in Pakistan, on hardware the
operator owns, with no third-party model service in the path and evidence frames retained under the
stated limits. Where the plant's data goes, and who may move it, is a decision the operator holds.

10.2 The Offer Behind the Design

CodeNinja built this design on Praxis, its platform for designing physical AI systems, and the design maps
directly onto what CodeNinja offers: Adaptive Operations is the sensing, detection and forecasting of
physical behavior at the station exits; Decision Systems is the ranking, attribution and recommendation a
named person decides on, from weld flags to supplier lot traces; Hyper Ontology is the governed object
model the whole argument runs through; Hyper Pragma is the work surface where the operator's own
people build and run their agents; and Sovereign Infrastructure is the shape of the whole thing, own
hardware, open-weight licenses and in-country operation, with the frontier node in the plant's own server
room.

11.3 Patterns Adopted and Set Aside

Three patterns were adopted. Triggered one capture per body at each station exit, with identity from the
body number and MES genealogy, was adopted over multi-object tracking because each body is captured

once and identity is already owned by a system of record. Nuisance-image collection before threshold
setting was adopted from the case-study record as a gate, not a chore. Memory over confirmed outcomes
was adopted over any form of on the fly training, which the requirement rules out and the architecture
makes unnecessary.

Two were set aside. Packaged smart cameras were set aside for the Apache-2.0 detectors on the
operator's own edge units, because the packaged class is rated for ambient temperatures below a body
shop summer in this climate and its weights would not belong to the operator. Personnel and vehicle
positioning was set aside because cameras watch bodies and vehicles, and worker location sensing
would collide with the national data protection rules for cameras on workers.

11.4 Where the Reasoning Lands

The reasoning lands on equipment classes rather than named products where the plant environment
decides: the node count by GPU class that sizes the work surface model's node; the frontier inference
cluster class (GPU nodes for 300B to 1T parameter open weight models) itself; the plant server room
GPU node ASHRAE class; the industrial fanless edge unit on an octa-core 6 TOPS NPU SoC rated for
minus 40 to 85 degrees Celsius in a sealed aluminium enclosure; the 5 MP global shutter GigE Vision
cameras with strobed lighting that freeze a moving body without rolling-shutter skew; and the export-
control determination that turns on total processing performance rather than memory, which is why the
license checkpoint sits at phase-one start. Everything shown in this chapter was recorded reading, and
nothing is inferred: where the plan holds an assumption to confirm, it is carried as one.
